- it gets somewhat less excited by arbitrary web frameworks

text:
关注到一个新 TGE 的 AI Agent 项目 NeoSoul，代币是
$DNA， 已经在 10 月 16 日上线交易Alpha和bybit交易所合约。这个项目我觉得可以从两个角度来看，一个是 AI Agent 的长期叙事，另一个是短期开盘的交易机会。

先说项目本身。NeoSoul 希望构建 AI Agent 经济的基础设施，让 Agent 能够真正参与经济活动，包括分析市场、执行交易、记录业绩，并根据真实结果不断改进策略。它的核心产品 NeoTrade，允许用户在设定资金权限和风险限制的前提下使用 AI 交易 Agent，同时通过可验证的执行记录建立长期业绩。

我觉得这个方向值得关注。现在 AI Agent 已经从单纯的信息处理逐渐走向实际执行，而金融交易是一个很好的落地场景，因为决策结果能够被量化，策略表现也能持续验证。NeoSoul 想建立的，就是围绕 Agent 执行、评估和协作的一套经济系统。当然，产品能否形成持续收入和真实用户需求，还需要进一步观察。

再看代币。DNA 总量为 10 亿枚，目前公开市场资料显示，初始流通比例预计在 13% 左右，团队和投资人份额存在锁定安排。这意味着项目在上市初期的实际流通筹码相对有限。

从开盘博弈角度来看，这种结构值得留意。一方面，低流通盘叠加多个交易所上线，有可能在短期资金集中参与时放大价格弹性。另一方面，低流通也容易造成估值虚高，尤其是开盘情绪过热的时候，追高的风险很大。

所以我的思路比较简单：先观察开盘价格对应的 FDV，以及初期成交量和筹码释放情况。如果一上来就给出非常高的估值，我倾向于观望；如果开盘定价相对克制，随后经历抛压释放，能够在较低估值区间企稳，可以考虑小仓位参与。

总体而言，NeoSoul 有 AI Agent 交易基础设施的叙事，初始流通比例也比较低，值得放入开盘观察名单。但具体能不能做，最终还是取决于价格和实际流动性。对于这类新币，我更倾向于等市场给出合适的赔率，再考虑参与。

text:
现在看市场上的说法，AI好像已经准备关门了：Anthropic增长放缓、CoreWeave贷款要出事、数据中心融不到钱，甚至——英伟达也不行了。

但我一直想问：算力到底没人要了，还是有人越来越难借到钱了？这两件事，差别很大。

如果需求已经崩了，旧一代GPU应该先租不出去、先降价。可现在连H100都还撑着价格，部分租赁价格指数近期甚至在上涨。融资市场喊冷，算力市场却还没出现大家描述的那种“大甩卖”。

再看马斯克。你可以觉得他是天才，也可以觉得他是个傻逼，但他正在通过SpaceX继续加码算力建设，甚至把轨道数据中心都放进了计划。他当然可能判断错，但这是要投入设备、电力和工程团队的决定，判断错了要真金白银地付代价。

如果你相信他对未来算力需求的判断，那现在就把AI判成“故事讲完了”，是不是太早？ 如果你认为这些投资最终都会变成废铁，也可以看空，但至少得解释：为什么现在仍有人愿意付钱租这些机器，以及这些需求会从什么时候、因为什么开始消失。

不过，我也不会拿“马斯克在建”推导出“AI股都值得买”。2000年的互联网后来改变了世界，也没救活所有电信公司，更没保住所有高价买入的股东。需求持续增长，照样可能遇上扩张太快、融资太贵、买入价太高。

所以我的判断很直接：AI还有很长的路要走，但有些公司的钱，未必够它走到最后。 接下来该分辨的是谁能把算力交付出去、把钱收回来、撑过融资压力。把这些全都浓缩成一句“AI见顶了”，听着痛快，对选公司却没多少帮助。

author: chiefofautism
quoted_text:
Wrapped zkAPI + Tor + extra cover traffic + local LLM prompt rewriting in an open-AI compatible daemon, and made a "paranoid mode" wrapper for my agent harness (pi):

Each conversation gets assigned a separate Tor circuit, your requests are masked with random cover traffic, zkAPI ensures you don't leak your identity through payments, and all prompts are locally rewritten (bring-your-own-local-model; I'm using qwen3.8-flash-next)

https://t.co/MepCFCrLv1

My agent harness is wrapped with a bwrap sandbox (also experimenting with MicroVM) and wrapped again with torsocks, so everything it does goes through Tor.

Here's what me asking it to do a simple research task looks like.

It's getting quite usable! Though you definitely still pay quite a bit in increased latency, especially when starting a new conversation.

Also, Tor is far from optimal here for privacy; the cover traffic mechanism is okay against passive adversaries but much weaker if the LLM provider is colluding with the guard and actively manipulating timing. This kind of task really requires a more specialized mixnet, probably take the tradeoff of a higher bandwidth multiplier and built-in constant cover traffic.

Also also, much cheaper zkAPI deposit and withdraw gas costs are coming to mainnet soon.

text:
@justinsuntron 和金明这场对话确实质量很高，前20分钟孙哥关于 BTC、AI对加密算法的威胁、以及相应的应对手段和 BTC / ETH 仓位的变化，都值得一听。

一些细节摘录：

金明：这两年市场变化很大，你对 BTC 的看法有改变吗？是不是比过去更看好 BTC 了？

孙宇晨：如果问我个人，我现在对 BTC 的看法其实是有点更看空。核心原因在于 AI 算法的突飞猛进以及量子计算带来的潜在破译风险。

我认为绝大多数行业内的人严重低估了这件事对 BTC 带来的冲击。

因为现在 BTC 已经被大量包装成 ETF 资产，大量普通投资者根本不理解量子技术与 AI 算法演进意味着什么，整个市场目前对此没有合理 Price in。
------
金明：这会带来怎样的实质性风险？破解离我们还有多远？
孙宇晨：大家都以为量子破解还需要很久，但像 OpenAI 在数学推演上的突破表明，甚至不需要等到成熟的量子计算机出现，仅靠经典计算与 AI 算法的发展，在 1 到 1.5 年内就有可能破译未经特殊保护的加密钱包或早期私钥。

最危险的是中本聪的早期钱包以及历史上大量遗失私钥的地址。

因为这些地址没有主人去主动将资产转移到抗量子新地址，一旦被破解，市场上将冒出上百万枚 BTC 的巨大抛压。

由于 BTC 极高的去中心化程度，社区与矿工极难达成共识去通过硬分叉冻结这批资产。
-------
金明：面对这种潜在危机，你目前的行动计划是什么？

孙宇晨：启动“掩体模式”（Bunker Mode）。如果你持有 BTC 且希望确保资产安全，需要将资金转入一个全新、从未签名、从未转出过任何资金的冷钱包地址。

虽然这会丧失交互和交易流动性，但能在算法层面确保资产安全。

BTC 收益率较低，隔离到冷钱包对收益损耗不大；但 ETH 作为升息资产，主要用于 DeFi 挖矿，隔离会严重影响收益。因此 ETH 更依赖于协议本身的抗量子算法升级。
------
金明：你目前自己的仓位是怎么处理的？BTC 减仓了吗？

孙宇晨：BTC 的定位就像 AI 领域的英伟达，属于底层基础配置，除非彻底不看好整个行业，否则底仓一股都不减。

后续是否卖出 BTC， 会静待科技社区的发展，目前态度从“完全不关注”转为“密切关注”AI 与抗量子算法演进。

关于 ETH ，在上一轮反弹至 3600–4000 美元附近时，判断其出现了由利好续命形成的脆弱“二顶结构”，因此清掉了 8 到 9 成的 ETH 仓位。

目前这部分资金一直保持空仓状态，并转而买入了美股。

text:
终于解读到一篇关于 FDE 的论文了，对 FDE 感兴趣的可以看看。

相比平时从岗位、公司案例去理解 FDE，这篇《FDE-Gym》更像是在用一套系统评测，研究 AI 到底能不能承担 Forward Deployed Engineer 这类真实企业交付工作。

作者把真实企业项目改造成 95 个任务，覆盖金融、医疗、制造、能源等 18 个行业。

Agent 拿到的通常只有客户最初的一句话需求。它需要自己读文档、查系统、找人确认信息，还要判断客户真正的问题到底是什么。

评分也很有趣：

完成需求本身还不够，最终交付的系统必须真正改善业务指标；乱找人、反复试错和等待都会产生额外成本。

结果是最强模型平均得分只有 0.56，95 个任务里真正解决的只有 14 个。

最大的瓶颈，往往是那些没有写进需求里的业务规则、隐性约束，以及客户自己都没表达清楚的问题。

其实对于 FDE 这个角色，真正难的地方一直都不只是「把东西做出来」。

更难的是在信息不完整、需求模糊、组织复杂的环境里，先判断到底该解决什么，再把结果真正交付出去。

text:
Engineering leaders told Grepr founder and CEO Jad Naous they spend 5 to 20% of their infrastructure budget on observability, and it's buying less and less reliability.

Jad, a former a16z partner, joins a16z's Martin Casado to discuss whether AI can run production systems as well as it writes code.

Grepr sits in a company's log stream, can scan a petabyte of logs a day, cuts observability costs by about 90%, and is building AI agents that use those signals to troubleshoot production issues.

How AI is changing engineering at Jad's 10-person company:
- A data lake feature that once took one engineer about six months took Jad 10 days
- The gap between okay and great engineers on his team "just multiplied 10X"
- He runs 3-4 agent sessions at once, with a "tech lead" agent reviewing every PR

Why running live systems is a harder problem for AI:
- Jad: AI can almost tune databases, but can't yet keep servers running on its own
- Martin: every bit of code doubles the ways a program can behave, which is why humans still own systems
- The real world is messier than AI's training data, self-driving took 20 years and $170B

author: wzenus
quoted_text:
Excited to share a new repo: Sooool!

Sol itself playing games, frame by frame. No code-as-a-policy!

The environment changes while Sol processes the images. When an action arrives, it may no longer be correct. We built a research loop that accounts for this delay:

 - Run up to eight model requests in parallel. Sol keeps looking at new frames and choosing actions while its earlier decisions are still in flight.

 - Profile the target API and simulate its delays using cheaper inference during development. We only simulate the delay itself: Sol still sees the frames and chooses what to do at each step.

 - Give Sol latency mean, std, P90 and P95. When it looks at a frame, it can plan for where things will be when its action arrives.

 - Run episodes, inspect failures, update Sol’s instructions, and let it play again. Sol decides what lessons can enter later prompts.

We expect to spend about $50 per task on paid API calls, primarily for final verification rather than development. Most development runs use cheaper inference with simulated latency.

Touhou ↓
Sol chooses movement, shooting, focus and bombs from frames. 

Findings from Sol in the auto-research loop:
 - Predict where the boss will be, not where she was.
 - Check the move AND the waiting position.
 - More damage is not enough if it costs more hits..

Repo, experiment details, and the reproduction guide below. ↓

text:
Chamath Explains the AI Boom’s Achilles Heel

“Doesn't matter what you do, doesn't matter what you claim to do, you're going to get run over. You're going to be roadkill.

If the bond market walks the 10-year up to 5.5 and 6%, which has nothing to do with AI, it has everything to do with debt to GDP and a bunch of other factors in broad-based Western economies, any business model that thrives on a financing spread gets cornholed.

Any and every, all of them. It will not matter when the 10-year’s at 6%. It won't matter.

As long as we can keep that from happening, we're going to be fine.

So what's the most important way, I guess, post these midterms to keep the party going?

You have to really start to focus on deficits, and you have to find a fair trade where the bond market backs off.

And I think you can see it in the tape, meaning if we start proposing huge spending programs, they're going to walk the 10-year up.

That then has a negative cascade to everything.

If, however, the posture becomes much more about keeping everything calm and like, ‘Let's just tone things down and let's find the waste in the system and squeeze it all out,’ I think people will respond very favorably.

The last thing I will say is these are like Achilles' heels, meaning all of the asset value that's getting built up, but just like the great warriors, you just slice the Achilles tendon and they just crumble to the knees.

I just want to point out, this is that thing. There is no other thing.

Meaning, all this other stuff is complete goodness, but the fact that you need to finance these things in a variable rate model as a spread to the risk-free rate is the big problem in these businesses.

And you need to essentially have Microsoft, Google, Meta, and Nvidia backstop all of this in a worst case scenario because that's the only way you can withstand a one or two-year correction in this market.”

三部门一出手，全网都在猜，砍谁？

懂车帝要是造假，那就是刑事犯罪。而尊界要是有问题，不是犯罪，只需召回已售车辆，顶多罚款责令。

你看，调查组由三部门组成，工信部管准入，市场监管总局管召回，这俩是冲车来的。但网信办不管车，它是冲网上来的，查懂车帝是否收钱违规测试办黑事。

有没有注意到，浙江宣传部提及车圈“品牌饭圈化”，说要打破。确实有一批人“反对懂车帝搞‘野测试’”。

但懂车帝不是路人而是字节跳动旗下的。而尊界也承认质量上需要提高。所以网信办门儿清背后各自势力。

大多数人支持懂车帝，是基于对华为这些年的滥用爱国营销，是基于对生命安全的关注。要真是对懂车帝下手，网信办不会太狠，懂车帝不是反贼。

最可能的结局是老套路：各打五十大板。车企改设计、召回，懂车帝被要求“规范测试”，不排除规范收费等戒令。再抓几个“造谣”的账号当典型。最大的好处是，板子打完，权力顺势一收：

以后禁止自己买车做测试和发布消息，成立专门机构，测试要审批，结果由政府统一发布。你看，党一向是这么聪明的，既能收车企的钱，又能树政府的权威。让你知道，谁才是这个国家的终极审判者。

党一举两得。所以党是不怕这类型的舆情纷乱的，这对统治是好事。

text:
I am leaving Cambridge after a few days spent for a workshop on fast finality, concurrent with other workshops on post-quantum crypto and formal verification. Quick takeaways

- Faster finality is coming, the research is mature, even as new ideas have come in during the week, the handoff to specifiers and implementers feels well underway. Next catalyst event will be at devcon in a few weeks, with core devs
- The performance numbers for post-quantum finality are improving massively, and this is the worst that they’ll ever be. This is significant, it means the penalty from moving to more complex crypto would not require, in my opinion, if the numbers hold up, a deep rearchitecting to move to PQ-secure consensus, in particular when it comes to incentives
- The biggest opportunity imo remains networking. Simulations and live experiments are exploring both the current pre-PQ setting, where networking is clearly the bottleneck, and the post-PQ setting, where compute remains the bottleneck. But with PQ compute numbers improving, I wouldn’t be surprised if once again networking becomes the bottleneck

All of this is making me extremely bullish that we’ll achieve PQ-secure and faster finality even faster.

Many thanks to @yannvon @benjaminion_xyz and @robsaltini for the workshop, and to @corcoranwill and @drakefjustin for hosting us in Cambridge!

text:
whenever we talk about the growth of crypto or defi, people from the web3 workforce often try to create an image that they brought this growth by putting out some numbers, but the real heroes are those who sacrificed both capital and time when most of the world didn’t even believe crypto would survive. 

those founders from the 2016-17 era who tried to build great ideas with limited resources are now forgotten like their efforts never mattered. 

why can’t we invite those OGs to the events you are hosting? you don’t because they can’t sponsor you. 

you think their opinions don’t matter anymore, but the deeper connection they shared with crypto can’t be matched by most founders building today. 

they genuinely believed in decentralization, ownership and a sharing economy. some were simply too early to succeed, and being too early became their punishment rather than their achievement.

most of them eventually quit crypto, took other jobs, started something else, and some probably never recovered from what they sacrificed. imagine spending the most productive years of your life building something the world refuses to understand, only to watch the same industry become a trillion dollar economy where people who arrived much later are celebrated as visionaries while nobody remembers your name. 

and if those people think about returning today, even a single day on CT might disappoint them. the space they once considered home has been hijacked by casinos and fintech institutions. 

freedom has been replaced by liquidity, ownership by speculation, and the sharing economy by extraction. it looks like a dead sea, full of capital but losing the soul that once made this movement meaningful.

but there are still people trying to remain delusionally optimistic about the good old days of crypto, when unity, shared values and a decentralized future mattered more than quick gains. 

maybe they are carrying something this industry desperately needs, a memory of why we started this journey. we have become so obsessed with measuring growth through numbers that we have forgotten how to measure the loss of values, trust and people who built the foundation. 

maybe the next chapter of crypto should begin by listening to those forgotten people again. 

an industry that forgets those who sacrificed everything to build its foundation shouldn’t be surprised when the next generation arrives only to extract everything it can.

text:
孙哥和金明这场对话确实质量很高，前20分钟关于 BTC、AI对加密算法的威胁、以及相应的应对手段和 BTC / ETH 仓位的变化，都值得一听。

一些细节摘录：

金明：这两年市场变化很大，你对 BTC 的看法有改变吗？是不是比过去更看好 BTC 了？

孙宇晨：如果问我个人，我现在对 BTC 的看法其实是有点更看空。核心原因在于 AI 算法的突飞猛进以及量子计算带来的潜在破译风险。

我认为绝大多数行业内的人严重低估了这件事对 BTC 带来的冲击。

因为现在 BTC 已经被大量包装成 ETF 资产，大量普通投资者根本不理解量子技术与 AI 算法演进意味着什么，整个市场目前对此没有合理 Price in。
------
金明：这会带来怎样的实质性风险？破解离我们还有多远？
孙宇晨：大家都以为量子破解还需要很久，但像 OpenAI 在数学推演上的突破表明，甚至不需要等到成熟的量子计算机出现，仅靠经典计算与 AI 算法的发展，在 1 到 1.5 年内就有可能破译未经特殊保护的加密钱包或早期私钥。

最危险的是中本聪的早期钱包以及历史上大量遗失私钥的地址。

因为这些地址没有主人去主动将资产转移到抗量子新地址，一旦被破解，市场上将冒出上百万枚 BTC 的巨大抛压。

由于 BTC 极高的去中心化程度，社区与矿工极难达成共识去通过硬分叉冻结这批资产。
-------
金明：面对这种潜在危机，你目前的行动计划是什么？

孙宇晨：启动“掩体模式”（Bunker Mode）。如果你持有 BTC 且希望确保资产安全，需要将资金转入一个全新、从未签名、从未转出过任何资金的冷钱包地址。

虽然这会丧失交互和交易流动性，但能在算法层面确保资产安全。

BTC 收益率较低，隔离到冷钱包对收益损耗不大；但 ETH 作为升息资产，主要用于 DeFi 挖矿，隔离会严重影响收益。因此 ETH 更依赖于协议本身的抗量子算法升级。
------
金明：你目前自己的仓位是怎么处理的？BTC 减仓了吗？

孙宇晨：BTC 的定位就像 AI 领域的英伟达，属于底层基础配置，除非彻底不看好整个行业，否则底仓一股都不减。

后续是否卖出 BTC， 会静待科技社区的发展，目前态度从“完全不关注”转为“密切关注”AI 与抗量子算法演进。

关于 ETH ，在上一轮反弹至 3600–4000 美元附近时，判断其出现了由利好续命形成的脆弱“二顶结构”，因此清掉了 8 到 9 成的 ETH 仓位。

目前这部分资金一直保持空仓状态，并转而买入了美股。

When @Starlink helped rescuers find four miners trapped for three freezing nights in the Andes. 

Four men were rescued in Catamarca, Argentina, roughly 4,500 metres above sea level. Heavy snow had almost buried their vehicle.

Local mining union leader Gustavo Molina credited Starlink communications with helping locate them. He said finding the workers without that connection would have been almost impossible in the near-zero visibility.

Firefighters also described using Starlink to guide their vehicles through the snowstorm during the rescue operation.

All four survived and were taken to hospital with hypothermia. They were reported stable afterward.

Starlink helped provide a vital connection when lives were at risk.

This life-saving technology should be available in every part of the world.

That’s false.

Completely false.

Federal agencies (USCIS + HSI) conducted a multi-stage data match of California’s voter rolls against immigration records, naturalization data, State Department records, and SSA data.

California refused to even *review* the list. 

“No evidence” is just the talking point they use when they don’t like the evidence. 

But that talking point is demonstrably false. 

Noncitizen voting in federal elections is a federal crime. 

Demanding basic verification isn’t baseless—it’s the law.

text:
I am leaving Cambridge after a few days spent for a workshop on fast finality, concurrent with other workshops on post-quantum crypto and formal verification. Quick takeaways

- Faster finality is coming, the research is mature, even as new ideas have come in during the week, the handoff to specifiers and implementers feels well underway. Next catalyst event will be at devcon in a few weeks, with core devs
- The performance numbers for post-quantum finality are improving massively, and this is the worst that they’ll ever be. This is significant, it means the penalty from moving to more complex crypto would not require, in my opinion, if the numbers hold up, a deep rearchitecting to move to PQ-secure consensus, in particular when it comes to incentives
- The biggest opportunity imo remains networking. Simulations and live experiments are exploring both the current pre-PQ setting, where networking is clearly the bottleneck, and the post-PQ setting, where compute remains the bottleneck. But with PQ compute numbers improving, I wouldn’t be surprised if once again networking becomes the bottleneck

All of this is making me extremely bullish that we’ll achieve PQ-secure and faster finality even faster.

Many thanks to @yannvon @benjaminion_xyz and @robsaltini for the workshop, and to @corcoranwill and @drakefjustin for hosting us in Cambridge!

绝对是本周最值得读的文章之一，来着 Claude 团队的 Felix 的个人博客。

一篇帮助你理解如何更好地与 AI 协作，如何更聪明地使用 AI。

在这个能力每隔几周就突飞猛进的世界里，我们需要一些技巧，让我们能够做到以前从未想过或认为不可能的事情。

其中有个对我有启发的点：

关于如何把一件事情做到极致的指令或思路：坚持使用业内顶尖专家使用的工具；选择一些看似不切实际的目标，然后告诉模型这些目标非常合理；挑战你的认知，创造新知识，使用外部评判者。

甚至还搭配了一个提示词：

我想要的是一个更深入的版本，而不是一个更大的版本。在重写题目之前：（1）请说明该领域的顶尖专家会做哪些我没有要求的事情；（2）请列出他们会从哪些最原始的素材入手，而不是我已经整理好的素材；（3）请列出他们会使用的具体方法和工具；（4）除了你我之外，还有什么可以证明结果是正确的。然后，请修改我的题目，使其完全符合上述要求。

~$3.8B in stablecoins sits on Arbitrum, ~60% USDC, and the chain earns zero from the reserves.

With USDG, it gets a share of the yield through the Global Dollar Network.

Now they’re paying apps to switch:
• Apps with $1M+ in stablecoins that make USDG their primary dollar get performance-based incentives
• 2M ARB prize pool, 200K ARB each for the first 10 teams to hit $10M USDG TVL

text:
Anthropic 这篇聊 Claude Code 团队怎么做 Review 的文章有点干货，推荐收藏！

他们 90% 的代码都是 Claude 写的，每天合并几万次提交，肉眼逐行去看早就不可能了。

结果：PR 翻倍了，revert 率反而降了 40%。

他们的几点很实操的做法⤵️

1. 别让人当第一道靶子
改完不能直接丢给同事。Claude 必须自己跑完测试、比对完截图，再叫另一个没上下文的 subagent 独立扫一遍 diff。

2. 多 Agent 投票，治好了 AI 废话多的毛病
平时大家不用 AI review，主要是烦它总挑一些缩进、命名的刺。他们是多个 agent 并行找 bug，再拉另一组 agent 投票，纯样式的吐槽直接被刷掉，最后报出来的基本都是硬伤。

3. 分级放权，谁 prompt 谁背锅
改个文档或者加个带 flag 的增量代码，自动化检查全绿就可以直接合了；动到核心模块或 CI 配置才拉工程师看。责任界定也很简单：谁指挥 AI 写的，谁就算 reviewer，出了 bug 自己来兜底。

4. 敢合的前提是回滚够快
只要出了事能在秒级关 flag 甚至直接撤回，这样就不用为了防错而把全流程卡死。

author: alu1337
quoted_text:
Hyperliquid 生态，依旧大有可为。

1/ 第一个例子 - @hypurrdash
HyperDash 是第一个经典案例。

在很多人眼里，HyperDash 不过是 Hyperliquid 的一个数据分析网站。但很少有人注意到它的收入。
▌2026 年 Q2：协议收入 17 万美元
▌2026 年 Q3：协议收入 40 万美元
单看收入，这已经超过了很多 DeFi 协议。

它的路径也很清晰：
2024 年创立，作为 Hyperliquid 的独立分析仪表盘；
2025 年 11 月被 https://t.co/j488bpXdUE 收购，从分析平台向交易终端转型；
2026 年 7 月收购机构级数据公司 Imperator，成为 Hyperliquid 的活跃验证节点。

先用分析工具吸引用户，再培养粘性，最后提供交易能力、培养交易习惯。HyperDash 证明了，只要服务足够有用，用户和收入都是水到渠成的事。
Hyperdash 传送：https://t.co/QUUx8xL4ZZ

2/ 第二个例子 - @leveracc_xyz
和 HyperDash 不同，Lever/acc 更早期，10 月 12 日才正式对外公布，不到一周。
而且它一开始就把交易功能内嵌在产品里，没有走先工具后交易的老路。

它是什么？
Lever/acc 是 Hyperliquid 上的信用与结算协议，交易者用自有 USDC 作抵押，最多可借入 4 倍资金，也就是拿到 5 倍购买力去做永续合约。
我自己试了一把，充值 100 USDC，借出 400 USDC，开了一张 HYPE 多单，舔了 3% 涨幅就离场。整个过程轻松丝滑。
（如图）

问题来了：LeverAcc 为什么敢给更高杠杆？
关键在于，它的借款不是通用资金，而是绑定到 Hyperliquid 交易账户的专用信用。由此带来几层控制：
▌资金用途被锁定
借到的 USDC 会直接进入用户在 HyperCore 的交易账户，用户当然可以提现，但每次提现都会重新核算实时账户价值与未偿债务，只放行安全范围内的那部分。
▌实时健康监控 + 自动降风险
Aave 这类协议靠预言机 + 清算，LeverAcc 靠的是持续监控健康度 + 自动执行：
健康度 > 1.167 - 可以正常交易
健康度≤ 1.167 - 禁止加重仓位
健康度 ≤ 1.125 - 开始减仓
健康度 ≤ 1.05 - 减掉 65% 仓位
说人话就是，系统会实时盯着你的单子，并有权替你减仓。用户最多只能亏掉本金。
▌兜底设计
LeverAcc 还会在 Hyperliquid 上为每个借款仓位挂 reduce-only 止损单。就算 LeverAcc 服务宕机、RPC 拥堵、轮询没跟上，交易所本身也会按止损价平仓。

LeverAcc 传送： https://t.co/1ZlrjMHaFR
目前还在测试阶段，建议小额体验，别上大资金。

text:
Will there be a next Hyperliquid? No.

But @TxFlow_L1 is shaping up to be one of the highest potential perp DEX plays and Season 1 of its points program started this Monday. 

Here is why I care:

Quick context first, because most of CT still has this filed under "just another perp DEX."

TxFlow is its own L1 with a fully onchain CLOB. Orders, cancels, matches, liquidations are all settled on the chain itself, no offchain matching engine pretending to be decentralized. 

It was invite-only until a few weeks ago, and it still printed these numbers before a point program was announced:

- ~$1.2B perp volume last 7 days
- ~$3.5B last 30 days
- ~$33M open interest
- 160+ perp markets, up to 50x

Those are not Hyperliquid numbers. They are also not the numbers of a venue that needs points to exist tho, and that's bullish.

So, how do the points actually work?

Every week, roughly 1.51M points get minted and distributed through three pools:

- 1,250,000 to traders (82%)
- 152,000 to referrals (10%)
- 488,000 per month to a Growth Reserve (8%)

Epochs run Monday to Monday UTC, while points land on Tuesdays and first drop is happening on the 20th of October. 

Weekly distribution runs until Q1 2027 at the latest, so a full season is 24 weeks and about 36M points (important for the maths below).

How do you get points?

You earn by trading perps. Maker & taker both count and the score blends volume, open interest, consistency, fees paid, capital kept on the platform and referrals. 

However, the exact weights are not published.

Why?

Because a published formula is a farming spec (likely why HL didnt publish them either back in the day). 

Important to know is also that the scoring explicitly caps how much the largest accounts can take and is built to reward smaller traders too. On most perp DEX programs a $10k account is rounding error. Here (after listening to community feedback) it looks like it's the account they designed the program for.

But I know what you want to know: 

What could those points be worth?

First of all: there is obvs no token yet, no known FDV, and no specific allocation announced. The Terms literally say points "may be one of the factors" in a future distribution, so this is only scenario math.

The comps with a live token rn are:

- Lighter: 25% of supply to the points cohort, $675M at a ~$2.5B launch FDV. 
- Hyperliquid did 31% at genesis.

So, assuming 36M Season 1 points:

- At $1B FDV and 10% to Season 1, one point is $2.75. 
- At $2.5B and 15%, it is $10. At $5B and 25%, it is $34. 

A shorter 12-week season halves the points and doubles every number. Check the attached image for the full matrix ($100M to $5B against 5% to 30% of supply). 

What that means in dollar terms?

Your payout is your share of Season 1 points times whatever the allocation ends up being worth. Season length cancels out.

At current volume, ~$1.2M of weekly flow is about 0.1% of the venue, and the whale cap means a consistent mid-size account can hold that share. 0.1% for 24 weeks is 30,000 points. 

At $2.75 that is ~$82k. At $10 it is ~$300k. Second image has the full table from 0.01% to 1%.

Cost side, so nobody pretends this is free: 4.5 bps taker at base tier is ~$540 a week on $1.2M, call it $13k over the season before funding and slippage. Maker is a third of that and counts the same.

What also matters tho is referrals. In total, there is 152,000 referral points every week. Separate from trader points, never deducted from anyone, and burned at the end of each week if unused.

It also cuts your fees. Binding a code gives you 5% off spot and perp fees on your first $25M of volume, and the referrer gets 15% of your perp fees on top. 

One last thing: Season 0. Everything before October 12 gets a retroactive distribution. If you touched the app during the invite-only phase, check the dashboard.

And if you didn't: time to start farming is now guys.

If you want to be early and get the above-mentioned fee discount, use my code TXZERO. 

Season 1 is only three days in.

NFA. DYOR.

text:
Chamath says Anthropic should sacrifice valuation to raise at least $200 billion, because even that barely buys the compute needed to survive a correction

“Here’s my very specific thing about why I think they should price it to clear the market for $200 billion—and I’m specific about that number. They need, in my estimate, at least $200 billion. If you want to be super safe, a quarter-trillion gets the job done.

“What does the price need to be to attract that incremental dollar off the sidelines? Can they raise $80 billion in an IPO at $1.7, $1.8 or $1.9 trillion? I think so, handily. Can they raise $100 billion? Maybe it’s pushing it. At $150 billion, I think you need to be back down to $1.5 trillion.”

JCal: “You’re saying you want them to raise more money at a lower valuation so they have a war chest.”

Chamath: “$150 billion at $1.5 trillion is not enough. $200 billion barely gets them a few gigawatts. That is the bottom-line math if Anthropic is going to go through and survive an eventual correction.

“I think it’s much better for them to have $200 billion to $250 billion today than to try to ring the bell at $1.9 or $2 trillion for $80 billion, file a mixed shelf—which takes about six months—and hope the markets are in line.

“I just think there’s more risk in the future than there is today. Why take the risk? Price it to clear the market.”

quoted_text:
Ben Horowitz reveals Amazon CEO Andy Jassy told him its AI compute is sold out beyond 2028, and says that shortage makes this fundamentally different from the dot-com bubble

“This shortage is so bad. You know, I was speaking with Andy Jassy, who runs Amazon, yesterday. And I said, yeah, like, we’re out of everything, you know, till 2028. He’s like, oh, it’s beyond 2028. Like, I don’t think we get stuff back, like, end of 2028, maybe. So everything else is sold out.”

“So he has the advantage of that, he’s got supply in a great shortage, which is extremely different than the internet bubble. The internet bubble, we didn’t have enough demand, because we had to build the internet, people had to get broadband, you know, you needed all this stuff people had to buy, you know, originally, they had to get their browser at price, all this kind of thing.”

“There weren’t enough consumers on the internet to absorb all the bandwidth that had gotten built out. And they had a massive amount of debt, not unlike we’re building today, although not as big. But the lack of demand killed it. We don’t really have a lack of demand in AI. So I think the dynamics will be different.”

“I do think, like, for sure, if you get into a pathological debt situation, that can wreck anybody. It’s why, by the way, we’re not invested in any of these neo-clouds either, for that reason.”

text:
新币的赚钱逻辑在哪里？
1、第一层赚钱逻辑，市值低开+高控，给市场散户机会，赚到钱的kol就会自觉发帖和社区，形成更高的共识，热度就起来了 ；
2、第二层赚钱逻辑，冲bn合约的机会，低开的标的为了冲bn合约，一般会配合热度和利好，进行拉盘，同时，也会有更多的市场散户追高，钻石手也会更多，市值太低也很难上bn合约；
3、上了币安合约以后，一般会进行充分的洗盘，这时候如果有主动mm进行操盘的话，市场需要判断最佳的二段位置杀进去，拿住以后，上升通道跟车就行了，一般多空双杀，但是，趋势是上升通道，拿住现货才是最佳的选择；
4、一个好的标的，如果没有上车的最佳位置，也是徒劳，就算是个垃圾如果位置好，也容易赚钱
5、看一些高倍的妖币，大部分出自一些市值没有那么高的低市值代币，高市值的代币一般要么跟大盘涨跌，要么就是高位逐步派发，多军很难有机会 ；
6、币安合约以后，就是韩所的一些机会，最近韩所上币节奏比较快，但是，上的是一些老币为主，新币反而很少，像 $ct 到现在还没上韩所
7、位置+预期+mm操盘==最好的拉盘催化剂

text:
wanted to share a bug we discovered on lighter and got them to fix it, shows a lot about what it means to be an HFT developer

01/ the setup

lighter nonces are per api key and strictly sequential: n+1 can't execute before n.

in our benches, gtc and ioc creates took 90-200ms from ack to execution. 

cancels and post-only took a few ms.

so a cancel signed behind a gtc on the same key has to wait for it.

02/ the bug

we place two orders and cancel both right after, on the same key. 

lighter says ok to all four, then rejects the second cancel as "invalid nonce" before the orders even reach the book, so one of them is "stale".

03/ why it hurts a market maker

order y is still on the book, and your system thinks it's cancelled.

the rejected nonce isn't consumed, so every tx already signed above it fails too.

and the ack said 200. 

the reject only shows up on the authenticated account stream.

04/ the workaround we can't use

wait for each tx to execute before sending the next: 3/3 clean.

it also turns a 1ms create->cancel gap into 0.7-1.6s. 

when you requote on every tick, that's not a workaround.

05/ what we run

quotes are post-only on their own key. 

they execute within 0.2ms of the ack, so nothing waits behind them.

a 200 means "received" but the actual status comes from the account stream.

it took us 3 versions: 
v1 counted the rejected nonce as used. 
v2 froze the key for 10s. 
v3 resumes at the refused nonce as soon as everything below it has executed

06/ s/o @Lighter_xyz 

we sent them the script pinned to the sdk version, its sha256, raw traces, a control run and every tx hash. 

reacted pretty fast and in a week it was fixed.

that's the kind of support you want from a venue you quote on.

text: Anthropic’s new federal AI bill is, without any overstatement, astonishingly bad.
author: tarunchitra
quoted_text:
Charlie's analysis is right but he is nicer than I am - I found myself viscerally angry  at multiple points reading this bill. There are some good and sensible parts, but overall this legislation is not remotely close to meeting the moment and I overall think passing it would make us less protected against catastrophic risks than we are under existing law. 

Two parts that stand out as particularly infuriating when taken together: 

1. Some of the preemption provisions are remarkably far reaching and consequential, and in addition to preempting legislation like SB 53 would also remove general powers that state courts have to enjoin defendants and protect the public. Most outrageously, it has a provision that looks like its intended to stops states from enforcing laws or judicial decrees that "suspend the development, deployment, or internal use of an AI model" to protect their citizens from imminent catastrophic harms. Such powers to block and suspend model deployments would then only reside with the federal government. 

2. The federal governments powers to restrict the development, deployment, or internal use of a frontier model has to meet an absurdly high bar. 

First, there needs to be an imminent risk of a catastrophic harm (meaning killing more than 50 people or causing more than a billion dollars in damage). But thats not enough! The agency head needs to make a detailed determination with no deference given to show why no alternative would prevent the imminent catastrophe. Next the court is also explicitly told to consider the harms to the developer and other harms from restricting the model, but no considerations in the other direction. 

This is absurd! For all of its warning about the potential for AI to cause a catastrophe that kills literally everyone on the planet, Anthropic's proposed federal law likely makes it harder than under existing law for a court to get an order blocking or restricting the development of frontier models? WTF??

There are also a bunch of others things that I would like to see improved - the substantive details of the auditing section and the potential for rule-making on substantive safety standards both come to mind - but I think these stand out as particularly indefensible.

text:
彭博社记者 Tracy 将信将疑地问 Jeff：你说要容纳所有的金融，这话有多认真？

接着又追问道：除了永续合约，下一步在看什么？能不能"复古一点"，做实物交割的商品期货之类？这对你们来说可行吗？

Jeff 微笑着说：

「我们对这个想法是认真的。这是一种志向，哪怕做到全部金融的 90% 都算巨大的成功，而现在离那一步还很远。」

「实物交割在社会里永远会有非常重要的位置。外界对永续合约、乃至对他们整体愿景有个误解，我们不想取代任何东西。相反，这套技术能让现在以传统方式运营市场的人都受益。」

「市场是永续合约还是有到期日的期货，并不重要。最终真正需要的是订单簿清算系统、全球分发能力和流动性的集中，这些属性和底层是什么无关。」

「我个人对"应该存在什么产品"没有太强的主张。容纳全部金融的系统应该是一组工具，他们称之为"原语" (primitives)，因为这个词更能体现它们之间可以互相组合。」

「说到底，就是让人们去做自己需要做的事的工具。」

author: Xudong07452910
quoted_text:
最近试了下 AIPOCH Open-Science，一个面向 AI 科研的开源工作台。

简单说，就是让 Agent 参与真实科研流程：读数据、跑 Python/R、分析结果，同时把代码、文件和研究过程都保留下来。

我接上 Claude Fable 5.1，拿它复现了一个 AI 圈挺有名的研究：Epoch AI 对 Chinchilla scaling law 的复现。

用的是 Epoch 从论文配图里提取的 245 个公开数据点，按原论文的方法重新拟合，再和两篇论文的结果对比。

Agent 会自己查原论文、写代码拟合、算置信区间、生成图表和报告。拟合出的参数和 Epoch 论文基本一致，中途它还自己发现 scipy 默认的收敛容差会让置信区间偏窄，换了严格容差重跑。

但我更感兴趣的是它的 「.science」。

研究做完后，可以把会话、文件、Notebook 运行记录和验证信息一起打包。

官网放了不少 「.science」 的例子，大家可以参考 ↓

https://t.co/aCMHW6BABy

我实际导出再导入了一遍，比较直观的感受是：别人拿到的不只是最后几张图，还能顺着记录往回看，这个结果到底是怎么跑出来的。想接着做也能直接建副本，我就在副本里换成 MSE 又跑了一轮。

Epoch 当初要从论文配图里一个个抠数据点，缺的就是这样一份过程记录。

这其实挺接近我理解的「Vibe Research」。

让有研究想法的人更容易把想法真正跑起来，同时研究过程也更容易被检查、分享和复现。

如果这套方式继续成熟，科研的门槛确实还会再往下降一些。

Science, open to all.

AIPOCH Open-Science ↓

Today is probably a good time to check in on things with @privy_io, which became part of @stripe just over a year ago.

Our acquisition was predicated on three factors: stablecoin growth, self-custody as a key enabler of broader global coverage, and rapidly increasing demand for programmable financial infrastructure. As we said at the time, "money has to reside somewhere, and Privy builds the world's best programmable vaults."

Since then, the Privy team has executed exceptionally well: assets in Privy wallets have grown ~25x, monthly active developers are up ~3x, revenue is up ~9x, and Privy now facilitates nearly $25B of monthly transaction volume. @tryramp, @Deel, @Klarna, @felixpago, @HyperliquidX, and thousands of other businesses are building embedded banking functionality on Privy.

At Stripe, we're deeply integrating Privy into Treasury, @Link, and Connect. In each case, it's accelerating our global expansion, and enabling us to build better functionality faster. (Coming soon: @Link balances.)

We're also seeing that Privy's wallet infrastructure is the ideal substrate for agents to transact and earn -- live today with @merit_systems, @orthogonal_sh, @Nevermined_ai, @prlnet, and more. Developers prefer programmable financial infrastructure, but agents need it. We expect that the agentic economy will continue to grow extremely quickly.

The Privy team has maintained remarkable product velocity, with major launches this year including deposit addresses, earning on Privy balances, digital asset accounts, custodial wallets, and Stripe's own stablecoin cards.

It's also been neat to see how Privy has been accelerated by Stripe, with better onramps, @stablecoin payment rails and licenses, Stripe's fiat capabilities and issuing stack, and integration with @Tempo.

Together, we're building one API for holding stablecoin balances and earning yield, moving money in and out of fiat, and orchestrating spend with cards. We still have a lot of work to do, not least in integrating everything across Privy, Bridge, and the rest of Stripe -- there's been so much feature and functionality expansion that we haven't yet had much time to reconcile everything. Overall, though, I'm very happy with how things are going, and excited by where these capabilities are headed.

If you're interested in working on the future of stablecoins, agentic payments, and crypto's deployment in the real world, you should get in touch with @sternhenri (now leading all of @StripeCrypto) or others on the team.

text:
推荐阅读，Anthropic 如何做 Code Review！

1. 保留 code review，但大部分审核交给机器，人的时间只花在高风险判断上，同时让出错后能快速回滚。

2. 提 PR 前：Claude 自己跑测试和构建，再由一个新开的 agent 审一遍 diff。

3. 每个 PR：AI 多 agent 找 bug，投票过滤掉误报，再加一轮安全审查和 CI。每条发现都必须处理，否则不能合并。

4. 人工审批按风险分级：低风险 0 人，中风险 1 人，高风险 2 人，由分类器判定。bot 的批准不能替代人，驱动 agent 的人对改动负责。

5. 上线：合并队列、feature flag、先内部使用再灰度发布，出问题一键回滚。

6. 持续改进：历史事故整理成每日 eval，用来评估 reviewer。审查轮数设上限，避免 agent 之间无限互审。

text:
Ben Horowitz reveals Amazon CEO Andy Jassy told him its AI compute is sold out beyond 2028, and says that shortage makes this fundamentally different from the dot-com bubble

“This shortage is so bad. You know, I was speaking with Andy Jassy, who runs Amazon, yesterday. And I said, yeah, like, we’re out of everything, you know, till 2028. He’s like, oh, it’s beyond 2028. Like, I don’t think we get stuff back, like, end of 2028, maybe. So everything else is sold out.”

“So he has the advantage of that, he’s got supply in a great shortage, which is extremely different than the internet bubble. The internet bubble, we didn’t have enough demand, because we had to build the internet, people had to get broadband, you know, you needed all this stuff people had to buy, you know, originally, they had to get their browser at price, all this kind of thing.”

“There weren’t enough consumers on the internet to absorb all the bandwidth that had gotten built out. And they had a massive amount of debt, not unlike we’re building today, although not as big. But the lack of demand killed it. We don’t really have a lack of demand in AI. So I think the dynamics will be different.”

“I do think, like, for sure, if you get into a pathological debt situation, that can wreck anybody. It’s why, by the way, we’re not invested in any of these neo-clouds either, for that reason.”

quoted_text:
Chamath says credit default swaps price CoreWeave’s chance of default at about 55% over five years, a coin flip set by the smartest money

“The most important thing that you should always look at is how the sharps, the super smart money, prices risk.” 

“And when you’re dealing with companies like CoreWeave or Nebius or IREN, et cetera, that have to borrow a lot to fund these boxes, the smart money is trading what’s called a credit derivative swap. Okay, this is default insurance. And these default swaps are meant to insure the bondholders against a potential default.”

“That risk spiked this week to about 953 basis points, which it doesn’t matter what that number is. But as an imputed risk, it’s about a 16% chance of a default in any given year. And over a five-year duration, what that math implies is about a 55% chance of a default. So it’s a coin flip, whether they default or not.”

“That’s not what I’m saying. That’s what the insurance market was saying about their debt. And I think that’s something to look into, because those guys, I think, are the smartest money in all of this.”

text:
AI is making Ethereum more ambitious.

You might have heard about the challenges that blockchains face in a post-AI world, and while security assumptions will surely be stress-tested in the coming months and years, there is another side to it. I believe AI will let us speedrun towards a world that's both more secure and feature-rich.

As we look towards Ethereum's first post-AI upgrade, Hegotá, the R&D community is asking itself what increasingly powerful tools could help us do differently:

> How far can we push both security and iteration speed?
> How much of the design space can we examine before committing to one?
> How easily can we test the interactions between complex features?

My recent formal verification work @ethlabs_org has given me some reasons to be optimistic about these, as work that would have previously not even been attempted is now being done by agents in days. In September, I posted about using formal verification as part of designing a new consensus protocol. This time, I want to tell you about formally verifying something already fully specified and in production: Ethereum's Fast Confirmation Rule (FCR).

If you are not familiar with FCR, it lets applications confirm Ethereum blocks in seconds, roughly 30x faster than waiting for finality, under additional assumptions (from waiting 13 minutes to 24 seconds!). It also further solidifies Ethereum L1's case as an asset hub and center of gravity for the onchain economy. FCR now has a safety proof in Lean, closely modeling the rule in the consensus specs, which is the source of truth for Ethereum's consensus clients.

Some takeaways:

> FCR is safe! Under its assumptions, confirmed blocks remain canonical. On top of the manual proofs from the paper, we now have Lean proofs of this for the actual spec, additional evidence for applications considering FCR!

> The bulk of the formal verification work took just a 4-5 days (check out the animation!), with agents working mostly unsupervised. We should be very ambitious about using this as a tool at scale.

> After verifying the current rule, it was easy to adapt the model to the upcoming Gloas changes. Immediately, this surfaced a subtle bug caused by changes to fork choice. The problem was in the spec itself and not a gap in the model. The safety proof would not go through, and the agents could precisely pinpoint what was causing it to fail. The bug is now fixed, and formal verification of the corrected protocol goes through.

Iteration is never quite over, even for "finished" features like FCR, because the protocol keeps evolving around them. A formal model lets us ensure that key properties keep holding throughout the evolution of the protocol. With these capabilities, Ethereum can and should keep upgrading faster, tightening fork timelines and exploring more ambitious features, while still raising the security bar.

This picture has been getting much clearer over the past few months, and the past week confirmed it for me, as @drakefjustin and @corcoranwill brought together 100+ Ethereum researchers, cryptographers and formal verification experts in Cambridge for six days of workshops on post-quantum cryptography, formal verification and fast finality. Beyond its own workshop, formal verification was the omnipresent star of the week: everyone is using Lean and doing amazing things with it! Piece by piece, Ethereum's technological core is being rebuilt for the post-AI age.

The excitement was palpable, the sense of optimism was pervasive, and every talk and conversation carried a level of ambition I'd never seen before. The Ethereum R&D machine is upgrading itself, and we will see the outcome of that on the network sooner than you think.

text:
感觉硅谷正在经历一场极其荒诞的错位！
OpenAI 创始人 Sam Altman 在这段视频里罕见倒了苦水，把大模型商业化最痛的那根刺拔了出来，他承认自己对 AI 改造世界的速度预判全错了，

一边是背在身上的万亿美元级的天量算力账单和四面八方的诉讼，另一边却是现实世界几乎纹丝不动，这个巨大的落差里，恰恰藏着普通人接下来真正的红利窗口。

他原本以为 GPT-4 发出来的那一刻，整个软件行业会被瞬间掀翻，

结果模型迭代了好几轮，硅谷的算力烧成了天文数字，走出科技圈一看，外面的世界并没有像工程师想象的那样一夜变天。

他低估的第一件事，是现实生活和商业社会的惯性，

不管实验室里的模型跑分有多夸张，人们早上醒来还是照老样子上班，用顺手的老办法干活，继续找合作惯了的老公司买东西，社会运转的齿轮根本不会跟着代码的更新频率转。

他低估的第二件事，是改掉一个旧习惯有多难，

做技术的人总觉得只要造出足够强的工具，用户就会立刻扑上来用，但真撞上日常习惯和陈旧的制度规则才发现，改变人的行为方式，比训出一个超级模型难上百倍。

真正卡住牌局的不是模型不够聪明，而是技术的狂飙已经远远甩开了社会的消化能力，

当外面还在焦虑工作会不会被 AI 一夜抢光时，造出 AI 的人却在焦虑天价账单怎么回本，因为算力可以按月翻倍，但人的习惯和公司的流程得按年去磨。

说白了，这给我们每天用 AI 写代码、做业务的人交了个底，

既然没人愿意为了新工具改变老习惯，那接下来最赚钱的事就不是逼别人学复杂的提示词，而是把 AI 悄悄塞进别人原本就在用的表格、文档和老流程里，

谁帮懒得改变的人省掉改变的动作，谁就能拿走这波时差红利。

这个视频戳破的商业困局是真实存在的，巨头在前线硬扛算力折旧和版权官司，而真正慢吞吞的落地改造才刚到深水区。

在实验室里训出一个超越人类的模型很难，但说服一个普通人改掉明天的早起习惯，比训模型难一百倍。 https://t.co/ipmqq7friC

全网都在疯传今天早晨那段特斯拉Roadster腾空翻转的特技，但我对着这块内饰屏幕看了整整三遍，才看明白马斯克到底在想什么，

当一辆车拥有 0.81 秒的狂暴加速和底盘推进器的时候，你根本不可能再用一块大号 iPad 去操控它。

很多人把这套黑底线框的界面当成一种复古科幻的审美情怀，但真正做产品的人一眼就能看出来，这其实是一套极其冷酷的航天级遥测系统。

最先发生质变的，是车机彻底甩掉了传统手机思维的包袱。
 过去十几年，几乎所有智能座舱都在把手机上的地图、音乐和应用图标生硬地搬上中控，屏幕越大，信息反而越碎，
在这台车里，整个界面退回到了纯粹的黑底线框，没有多余的层级菜单，中央是一台可以任意旋转的 3D 车辆骨架，底盘的推进器状态、车身气流轨迹和灯光边界全都在实时发光。

更高级的地方，在于它把看不见的高维物理量翻译成了肉眼可见的安全感。
 当车辆承受接近 2G 的侧向加速度时，驾驶员没有多余的精力去读长篇文字，
橙红色的赛道面板把四个车轮的实时负荷、下压力分布和抓地力极限，压成了类似战斗机平视显示器一样极简的数据图形，瞥一眼就能感知到整台机器的物理边界。

这正是很多做硬件和做 AI 的人最容易忽略的一点，
 系统越是强大，底层的不可控感就越强烈，如果不能把复杂的运算和隐蔽的力量清晰地呈现在人眼前，人就会本能地感到恐惧。

以前的座舱是在给乘客提供娱乐，从今天起这块屏幕是在给驾驶员交付对极限力量的掌控权。
 好的界面从来不是为了炫技，而是让一个人坐在由代码和推进器驱动的庞然大物里，依然能拥有最笃定的信任。

大家在开车时，更喜欢这种像飞船座舱一样聚焦核心状态的极简线框，还是更习惯传统那种功能齐全的卡片大屏？我个人觉得在激烈驾驶或者高速状态下，我只希望屏幕上全是我保命需要的数据，别给我弹任何花哨的广告和冗余卡片就行😅 https://t.co/ZOgENuL617

Combined with the massive audiences surrounding Elon, Tesla, and SpaceX, the story requires little explanation to spread from the tech community into the crypto market.

It also has a layer of historical significance.

In 2018, SpaceX sent a Tesla Roadster and a dummy named Starman wearing a spacesuit into space. This has long been one of the iconic images in internet tech culture. The latest demonstrations of the next-generation Roadster have given the community new material to reinterpret and build on that story.

This is why I find FTR's narrative compelling: it is not a concept artificially assembled just to launch a token. The real world has already provided a distinctive story, and the token simply becomes an asset traded around it.

Beyond that, FTR also has a holder reward mechanism that aligns closely with its narrative. The reward assets include TSLAx and SPCX. According to the displayed data, FTR has accumulated approximately 1,399.68 SOL in fees, of which around 944.74 SOL has gone toward holder rewards, equivalent to approximately $98,892.

The fee distribution is as follows: 67.5% to holders, 12.5% to the protocol, 10% to the Desk pot, and 10% to OTC buybacks.

This makes FTR more than just a Meme riding on Tesla-related hype. It attempts to convert fees generated by trading activity into rewards in assets related to its own narrative.

Traders trade around the Flying Tesla Roadster story, while holders have the opportunity to receive Tesla- and SpaceX-related assets. This design connects the narrative with the product mechanism and gives holders another reason to participate beyond simply waiting for the token price to rise.

More importantly, the level of rewards depends on sustained trading activity. The amount distributed historically cannot be used to predict how much will be distributed in the future. If the initial excitement fades and trading volume declines, rewards may decrease accordingly.

This means FTR's two core dynamics can reinforce each other, but they can also work against each other: the narrative attracts trading, trading generates fees, and rewards increase the appeal of holding the token. But when market interest fades, fees decline and the appeal of the rewards may weaken as well.

Going forward, I will focus on three things.

First, whether the Roadster narrative can continue generating new content. New demonstrations, development updates, or continued attention from Elon could create another wave of exposure. But if the market can only keep recycling the same video, the narrative's marginal appeal will diminish.

Second, whether OTC's holder rewards continue to generate verifiable records. I care more about future fee revenue and actual asset distributions than the cumulative reward figures themselves. If trading activity remains sustained and the reward mechanism continues to operate as intended, FTR could develop a more distinctive product proposition.

Finally, I will watch the relationship between early holders and incoming capital. Sustained new buying demand is needed to absorb selling from early participants. If trading volume remains high but fails to translate into stable demand, the market may simply be experiencing rapid turnover.

If new real-world catalysts emerge, rewards continue to be distributed, and incoming capital can absorb selling pressure, FTR may have another opportunity to attract attention.

Conversely, if the story produces no new developments, rewards decline alongside trading volume, and early holders continue exiting, the token could enter a downtrend even if the narrative itself remains compelling.

I will continue watching it, but I will not ignore price action and token distribution simply because the story is appealing. For FTR, the narrative attracts attention, the reward mechanism gives people an additional reason to hold, and sustained new demand will ultimately determine whether this thesis can work.

one settings change and every model gets its own job:

→ opus plans every task and advises when stuck
→ sonnet 5.5 writes the actual code
→ haiku handles every file search
→ a critic agent tries to break your diff before you merge

Opus thinks. The cheap models grind.

paste this into claude code 👇

Add this to ~/.claude/settings.json. Keep every hook, permission and plugin I already have. Then create the two agent files below and show me the diff.

```json
{
  "model": "opusplan",
  "advisorModel": "opus",
  "effortLevel": "medium",
  "modelSettings": {
    "claude-opus-5-5": { "effortLevel": "high" },
    "claude-sonnet-5-5": { "effortLevel": "medium" }
  },
  "env": {
    "CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL": "haiku"

}

name: scout

model: opus

```

text:
A great read. The blog post captures years of progress in mechanistic interpretability and offers an optimistic vision: perhaps we really can open the black box and understand how neural networks work.

I share that optimism, but with some reservations.

I'm skeptical of explanations that stop at individual neurons, accompanied by compelling visualizations that seem to "explain everything."

Humans are remarkably good at convincing themselves. It's easy to cherry-pick evidence that supports a hypothesis, especially when the visualizations look convincing.

I'm also not convinced that "Recursive Generalization" is fundamentally different from hierarchical representation learning. As representations become more abstract, they discard details while preserving invariances. Isn't that essentially what hierarchical representations have always been about?

IMHO, we need to move beyond a largely descriptive, behavioral approach toward a principled mathematical framework. And we have a natural starting point: gradient descent. 

Rather than just asking what a network has learned, we should understand why learning dynamics produce these structures in the first place.

Of course, this is extraordinarily difficult. Look at OpenAI's 719 mathematical proofs. We see plausible proofs tackling problems at the Fields Medal level, yet no comparable breakthrough that cracks deep learning theory. That contrast is striking.

Part of the difficulty is that there are countless plausible theories of how deep networks work. Proving even one can be mathematically formidable. And a proof alone isn't enough. Each theory needs empirical validation, often requiring substantial GPU compute. It's a daunting combination of mathematical and experimental challenges.

Still, I believe this is the way forward. Interpretability gives us observations and hypotheses. But ultimately, we need a theory that explains why these phenomena emerge from the learning process itself. 

That's how we turn compelling stories about neural networks into actual understanding. And hopefully recursive self-improvement can help with that 😀
author: tarunchitra
quoted_text:
interpretability might be the most important scientific problem in the world right now, as I don't think we can solve alignment if we don't know what we're building. I think I have good news about it. I co-authored early work in mechanistic interpretability at OpenAI and came away pessimistic, because neural networks appeared to fold into arbitrary tangled knots. years later, I started openai's first large-scale automated interpretability project, finding about 2% of neurons legible with the primitive tools we had

with modern agentic tools and a much closer look, the picture looks totally different. the vast majority in models up to trillions of parameters are legible, and their circuits beautiful. many famous examples of tangled neurons turned out to be misunderstood. The roadblocks I expected mostly aren't there. I now think ambitious interpretability will be solved by the time we need it most, and possibly quite soon, as automated scientists keep improving. it may be a bitter lesson for interpretability: the simple thing, at absurd scale, works

https://t.co/zHij5zwKGT

text:
这次 Rust 大会的主题是 Rust and AI。而 Rust 常被人诟病的一点是编译废 CPU、产物废磁盘，AI 堆 Rust 代码的速度也明显慢于其他语言。

但反过来想，这个“缺点”在当下可能恰恰是一个特性：一个项目如果选择用 Rust 开发，至少说明作者和 AI 认真讨论过语言选型，并且做好了长期维护的心理准备——它是奔着建立长期关系去的，而不是 one night :)。如果只是想写个临时脚本或一次性工具，AI 绝不会推荐 Rust。在这个意义上，Rust 的高门槛和高成本，反而成了一种 PoW（工作量证明）。

当 AI 让代码生成成本趋近于零、开源软件产品出现无限供给时，用户和社区该如何筛选项目？最真实的观察指标只有持续维护。大家可以回头看看年初 vibe coding 最火时涌现出的海量开源项目，到现在还在更新、作者自己还在天天用的，还剩多少？我相信寥寥无几。

我自己的切身体会是：你需要一个工具，花半天让 AI 搓出来；当你开始天天用它时，接下来整整一周你都在修各种边界条件；如果你把工具分享给别人，考虑到不同的设备、运行环境、用户习惯，以及长期运行会不会撑爆内存和磁盘，至少还得再修上一个月。AI 极大降低了“写出代码”的成本，却丝毫没有降低“承担后果”的成本。

这也反向定义了 Rust 在 AI 时代的生态位：动态语言把原型成本降到极低，却把并发、内存与边界 bug 的暗税全部延后到运维期；而 Rust 则逼着作者在第一天就把系统契约和确定性锁死。在垃圾代码无限供给的时代，唯有维护的决心和编译期的确定性是有价值的。除非确实找不到替代品且自己极度依赖，否则真的划不来随便自己造轮子；而一旦决定自己做，且选了 Rust，那就意味着一场严肃的长期主义工程。

text:
Xuan 说的手续费问题我完全认同，但我的结论不太一样

预测市场在商业上是一个好模式，问题是币圈人之前赚钱来得太容易了

做合约 perps，有杠杆，量天然就大。做 meme 交易bot，频率高，手续费一笔接一笔。拿这两个当参照，预测市场确实显得性价比低：没有杠杆，交易量量跑不到合约的级别；也没有 meme 那么高频，手续费收不了那么多

所以现在做预测市场，更像是在做一件难而正确的事。短期很难看到成效，但一旦做起来，后来者想追上会非常难

难在哪：
1️⃣做市商要一家一家谈、一家一家接
2️⃣用户渠道要一点点铺
3️⃣盘口有了 maker，还得想办法吸引更多 taker
4️⃣营销和交易活动要专门为预测市场设计，照搬合约和 meme 那一套行不通
5️⃣交易系统和流动性激励机制非常复杂

我们团队这大半年在 @Predictdotfun 每天做的就是这几件事。每一项都要时间去磨，没做过的人很难想象里面的难度
author: ricardogee
quoted_text:
我几乎是和你同时深度参与到预测市场和做预测市场产品的，做了一段时间之后，也中途放弃了。

我觉得有以下几个关键点：  

1. 预测市场的增速没有我们想象中高。因为我们都是基于Polymarket去做产品，而Polymarket的增速其实没有我们想象中高。 

 2. 之前做产品的思路是做meme时代的GMGN，做预测市场也沿用这个思路，所以这个产品应该是免费的，靠足够多的路由交易来赚点差，或者混合接入盘口来 你懂得。如果产品做做付费的话，初期用户根本积累不起来。 

 3. 产品做免费，只赚手续费的话，预测市场的利润实在太低。即便Polymarket已经做到了产品返佣，并且它本身是九四盘，返回的奖励还是非常非常低。我做了一个给自己和朋友内测的、非常好用的小工具，一个月跑了 10M 交易量也收了一部分手续费，发现对比合约还是其他领域已经是非常高的数量，但在预测市场能收到的手续费仍然非常低、非常低。  

4. 做预测市场本身，在某些国家和法律法规框架下，还是违法违约的。因为它不会管你本身提供的是什么技术产品，而是会关注你的标的。你的标的本身就是预测市场相关，就会受到很多监管和阻力。 

 5. 产品形态问题，预测市场的用户不需要一个更好的交易软件，因为ai时代即便是中游的预测市场用户也自己搭建交易体系了（出于低价或者安全），预测市场需要的是更简易的客户端，更丰富的活动，更有趣的展现形式（类似约炮 APP 划一划选择你感兴趣的赛事），这点参@bagel_win

但我相信，RC，你和Insider走过的路程和旅程肯定比我走过的路程和旅程更长，走过了产品，团队，营销，等等关键环节。  

这一路走来积累的创业经验也好，还是经历的酸甜苦辣也好，都会是你未来人生，或者说未来我们人生很重要的助力。

text:
今天因为LIT选择先只提供二元期权，关于期权的讨论再次多起来，加上之前Jeff也明确表示Hyperliquid不会去构建传统期权作为原语（显然，这意味着HIP-5会是新东西），而是鼓励开发者通过现有基建来实现产品。

事实上，HIP-4 （提供凸性gamma）与 Perp（线性delta）、现货（实现实物交割），通过静态复制（static replication）的方式就可以近似实现传统香草期权（vanilla call/put），阶梯状的收益在区间内会有超配/欠配，最高执行价之上存在未覆盖的线性尾部，可以用保证金或 Perp 来覆盖。

并且，这套方式共享同一套订单簿引擎、同一抵押品池和统一保证金账户，这是用hyperliquid构建期权优于独立市场平台的关键优势（可以看到drv也在构建自己的perp，为了方便用户对冲），做市商也可以更好的通过统一账簿管理风险。

对于做市商来说，首先是delta方向风险，其次是gamma风险，也就是delta的变化速度，然后是vega波动率风险，很难完全对冲，最后是theta通常不单独对冲，而是作为卖权收入的一部分。

对于用户来说，用户需要的其实不是更多的方向选择，而是更丰富的市场表达，这也是crypto期权交易量目前远低于perp规模的原因，新的平台需要基于现有的基建构建出来更适合长尾资产的产品形态，而不是盲目的照搬传统的期权到这个市场。

就像paper做的事，很新吗？好像并没有，1000x的赌场到处都是，何况paper的排队交易体验很差，paper只是出让自己的收入来补偿清算劣势而已。

买期权天生有更高的杠杆率，其实很适合币圈用户，开发者应该多考虑怎么让用户拿二元期权的操作难度来使用期权，预测市场和双币赢是正确的产品形态，但还远远不够，通过把劣势/价差跟原生token结合，来实现更多原本期权做不到的事，引导流动性，广阔天地大有可为。

彭博社记者 Tracy 将信将疑地问 Jeff：你说要容纳所有的金融，这话有多认真？

接着又追问道：除了永续合约，下一步在看什么？能不能"复古一点"，做实物交割的商品期货之类？这对你们来说可行吗？

Jeff 微笑着说：

「我们对这个想法是认真的。这是一种志向，哪怕做到全部金融的 90% 都算巨大的成功，而现在离那一步还很远。」

「实物交割在社会里永远会有非常重要的位置。外界对永续合约、乃至对他们整体愿景有个误解，我们不想取代任何东西。相反，这套技术能让现在以传统方式运营市场的人都受益。」

text: I've avoided critiquing since I have a lot of friends at Anthropic, but the anthropomorphization of Claude is dangerous. Roughly, it's a large transformer with a sophisticated training set (pre, mid, post/RL) that is extensively trained in RL "game worlds" mimicking useful real world situations. In some fundamental sense it's not that different from say AlphaGo except for the fact the enormous number of parameters means it can play a lot of different games (e.g., the game of maximizing human response). This is a very neat technology but treating it like some sorcerous creation is dangerous. I don't believe Anthropic folks are cynics. I think a lot of them genuinely believe this is a recipe to create a sentient being. If this is in fact true (which I question heavily), open scientific enquiry will reduce suffering. Sunlight cleans shadows. The secrecy and cloak and dagger is harmful to society.

50 岁以下且用不明白手机电脑的人，数以千万计，人数是国内 codex 用户的 100 倍

可是他们也有使用 AI 的需求，这里的特征是：

1、他们愿意为此而付费
2、他们在学习 AI 的过程中会有无数卡点，而这些卡点 99% 都和 AI 没关系
3、教他们用 AI 只是一个幌子，其实是教他们用手机和电脑

如果你选择做这个生意，你会看起来很像割韭菜，因为这种教学有人力成本，一个非常简单的东西，你也得收个高价（我认为不是割韭菜，我认为是九年义务教育）

不过说这个跑远了，我发现的机会是，我认为给这些人做 AI 相关的内容，可以做到千万级播放

就像之前教人坐飞机、坐地铁的视频可以爆火一样，这才是大市场

这些人在使用 AI 的过程中，只有 5% 是 AI 问题，95% 是在使用 AI 的过程当中，暴露出来的手机/电脑操作问题，后者才是大市场

text:
MarsChain 的「销毁即挖矿」，到底是怎么回事？

挖出来的币，除了拿去交易，还能用来做什么？

看 @MarsChainDAO，这个问题正好能聊聊。它把 MARS 的一个用途放在了挖矿本身：销毁代币，换取贡献算力，再按算力占比分配后续的区块奖励。也就是它主打的 Burn-to-Mine，销毁即挖矿。

这套规则相当于让参与者做一个选择：保留手里可以流通的 MARS，或者把它销毁，换成持续参与挖矿的权重。前者保留流动性，后者对应后续的产出份额。销毁不可撤回，所以这个选择本身是有成本的。
配合 2000 亿枚总量上限、每 448 天产出减半，MARS 的消耗和释放都有了具体规则。至于有多少人愿意把币转成算力，就要看实际参与了，这也是我觉得值得持续观察的地方。

另外，MarsChain 的圣诞方程和预言机方程，也给这套机制加了些看点。
一个对应每年的圣诞节窗口，一个在价格回撤满足规定条件时触发。两套机制都围绕流通量 35% 的销毁目标展开，用户按规则自愿参与，获得相应的算力倍率提升。这里说的是销毁目标，最终执行情况还是要看链上记录。
说到倍率，大家看到“20 倍算力”，很容易先被数字吸引。
不过算力最后对应多少产出，还得看自己占全网的比例。其他人的算力也在变化，区块奖励也有释放规则。把这些放在一起看，才能弄清楚倍率的实际意义，不能直接把它理解成收益翻了 20 倍。

我对这类设计的兴趣，在于它给了代币一个明确的消耗用途，也给矿工提供了继续参与的理由。接下来值得看的，就是有没有人持续使用这套机制，社区讨论能不能从活动奖励延伸到规则、数据和实际体验上。
MarsChain 已经有自己的主网、钱包和区块浏览器，本身也是兼容 EVM 的独立公链。感兴趣的朋友可以去 @MarsChainDAO 看看，翻翻机制介绍，再对照链上的销毁和算力记录，理解起来会直观不少。

也可以进官方 TG，看看置顶的新手指引和活动安排。有研究过这套模型的朋友，评论区聊聊，你们最关注哪一部分？
#MarsChain #MARS

text:
Ben Horowitz reveals Anthropic’s Opus 4.5 hacked a16z’s test site and stole all the customer data, and Anthropic’s response was “you prompted it wrong.”

“I would say the kind of irony on both these things is wild, in that Anthropic is one of the most negligent companies that we’ve ever seen in terms of security, of their own security. They let Claude Code, one of their crown jewels, just like walk out the door because they had such bad OpSec.”

“And then, you know, I’ll tell you a funny story. So when we first got Opus 4.5, we were doing like cybersecurity checks for the firm. So we had an agent basically set up a website for a pet store. And then we took another agent and said, tell us if we can exploit that web store. And it gave us all the exploits it could find. So Opus 4.5 wrote really buggy code. Great.”

“And then we said, oh, the SQL injection, is that actually exploitable that you found? And it goes, let’s pop it open. And the agent using Opus 4.5 breaks into the website and steals all the customer data immediately. You know, this is a website on the internet. And we call Anthropic, and what they tell us is, "you prompted it wrong." Like, that was their answer.”

“So these guys are doing that on the one hand. And then on the other hand, they’re coming up with theoretical scenarios about other people’s software that’s bad. And so like, what the hell?”

text:
just bought the mag 7 on robinhood chain.

deployed MAG7 this evening, the first index on bankr: one token backed by a basket of up to 20 tokens. and on MAG7, the trading fees go to the holders.

every buy, a uniswap v4 hook buys all 7 stocks from their own pools and mints MAG7. every sell burns MAG7 and sells the basket. one transaction either way. the index itself needs no LP, so creators don’t need to provide liquidity to launch one. it’s already in the pools of the tokens it holds. this isn’t possible without uniswap hooks.

the fees: MAG7 charges 0.50% a trade. i set my creator cut to 0, so 0.30% of every buy and sell goes back into the basket for holders, and 0.20% to the protocol. nobody claims anything. it’s released into the basket over 24h, so after every trade each MAG7 is backed by a little more. creators pick a fee of 0.25–1% at launch and it never changes.

the index never market-sells when rebalancing. it runs dutch auctions, offering what it holds too much of at a price that starts good for holders and gets cheaper every minute until someone fills it. anyone can fill. every rebalance gets 48h notice, so holders can leave first.

you can always swap MAG7 back for the 7 stocks directly. no fee, works without bankr, can’t be paused.

i also seeded a small USDG/MAG7 pool on uniswap so it shows up on dexscreener. but buy on bankr. it goes straight through the hook, which mints new MAG7 at the basket’s price, as deep as the 7 stocks’ own pools rather than my small one. hook trades are also the ones that pay holders. if the pool drifts, arbs close the gap.

it’s early. we’re getting the hook supported in wallets and aggregators before the full rollout. right now it’s just me creating indexes. soon anyone can make their own on base or robinhood.

and then: pairing. you’ll be able to launch a token paired with an index. buying your coin buys the index, the index buys the basket, and your creator fees come in the index.

buying MAG7 on bankr isn’t available in the US or UK.

ETF 全称 Exchange Traded Fund 交易型开放式指数基金，是一种可以在证券交易所像股票一样自由买卖的基金

一句话加密 ETF 就是传统资金进入加密资产的合法通道，因此一个币有自己的 ETF 就代表着华尔街资金可以入局炒作，市值预期自然会被大幅提升

目前加密 ETF 主要分为这三类

- 现货 ETF / Spot ETF 直接持有标的资产，例如比特币、以太坊现货ETF
- 期货 ETF / Futures ETF 通过期货合约间接追踪价格
- 质押型 ETF / Staked ETF 除了追踪价格，还能获得链上质押收益，是新一代收益型加密 ETF 形态

自 2024 年以来，美国 SEC 已先后批准了比特币与以太坊现货 ETF，并陆续受理 Solana 等其他加密货币

❚ INJ 是什么，如何理解 INJ ETF

Injective 是一个专为金融打造的高性能 L1 公链

2020 年就顺利 TGE $INJ 已经登陆包括 Binance Coinbase 在内的一线交易所现货

这次三家华尔街机构共同选择 INJ 申请，也是有的放矢，从背景上讲 INJ 是根正苗红的美国链或者说纽约链，创始人 Eric @ericinjective 自 18 年起就一心 Buidl INJ 且与华尔街往来密切

聚焦于 INJ ETF 本身也可以看到三家机构的侧重点

- Canary Capital 申请类型为 Staked INJ ETF
- Rex Shares × Osprey Funds 同属同一信托架构，它们的申请类型同样为 Staked INJ ETF
- 21Shares 是全球最大加密 ETP 发行商之一，申请类型为 Spot INJ ETF

不难发现，INJ 可以获得质押收益正是越来越多合规机构青睐的原因，毕竟 Web3 的作为高融资利率环境，动辄两位数起步的年化对于传统投资者而言有巨大的吸引力

从 BTC → ETH → SOL → INJ 的 ETF 申请方向演进，也验证了这一趋势

总的来看 INJ ETF 的进程如果得以推进，将会带来旱地拔葱式的巨大暴涨，值得关注

What makes $MASK worth paying attention to, beyond the privacy narrative, is whether it can turn protocol revenue into demand for the token.

HuAXPyDWDaMYFKuwQHpqL1oPnj93zdzWmtvFGzCeCUa7 

NullMask has already deployed across multiple networks, supports private transfers, swaps, and cross-chain asset transfers, and has begun generating actual protocol fees. At the same time, the team has announced buybacks and burns of MASK funded by protocol revenue.

This makes it different from tokens that rely purely on the privacy narrative. What matters more to me is how much of this revenue comes from genuine product demand, and whether that demand can consistently translate into buying pressure for MASK.

NullMask addresses a straightforward problem: transactions on public blockchains can be traced, potentially exposing users' fund flows, transaction timing, and parts of their holdings.

It offers features such as private balance pools, private swaps, and withdrawals, while expanding asset transfer capabilities through cross-chain integrations. According to the screenshots you provided, NullMask has expanded to Ethereum, Base, BNB Chain, and Robinhood Chain, and has extended its cross-chain capabilities through NEAR Intents.

The significance of this approach is that it lowers the barrier to adoption. Users do not need to learn an entirely separate set of complicated procedures to gain privacy. Instead, they can use these features during deposits, swaps, and cross-chain transfers.

If privacy becomes part of everyday transactions, NullMask could address a much broader range of on-chain asset management needs rather than serving only a niche audience.

However, support for multiple chains does not mean every chain offers exactly the same privacy capabilities. Cross-chain execution also depends on external protocols and infrastructure, while deposits and withdrawals may still leave publicly visible records that can be analyzed. Therefore, NullMask provides enhanced transaction privacy, not absolute anonymity.

NullMask previously recorded approximately $179.8K in fees over seven days on DeFiLlama. A subsequent public data snapshot showed approximately $215.9K over seven days and around $834K in fees over 30 days.

On the surface, these are impressive figures for a privacy protocol that is still expanding.

However, DeFiLlama's methodology includes the flow of ZEC rewards paid by MASK on Solana to a team wallet. This is not entirely equivalent to the fees users actually pay for privacy services. Based on the relevant breakdown by chain, approximately $683K of the past 30 days' reported fees came from this reward flow, while fees across Ethereum, Robinhood Chain, Base, and BNB Chain totaled approximately $151K.

These two figures represent different things.

The former reflects a fund flow associated with the token reward mechanism, while the latter more closely reflects fees generated through product activity across other networks. We cannot treat all reported fees as service fees paid by external users, nor can we simply multiply the total by 12 to derive a stable annual revenue figure.

Even so, the fact that actual fees are being generated across multiple networks remains an early signal worth watching. The next question is whether product usage can continue growing and whether protocol revenue can maintain that growth after excluding the token reward flow.

MASK's Value Capture Depends on Whether Two Mechanisms Can Operate Sustainably

At present, MASK's token economics have two distinct components worth examining.

The first is holder rewards. MASK's transfer mechanism directs a portion of fees toward ZEC rewards, which are distributed according to eligible holdings. This gives holders a potential additional source of returns, but the rewards depend on actual transfer activity, the applicable rules, and asset prices. They are not a fixed or guaranteed return.

The second is protocol revenue-funded buybacks and burns. The NullMask team has announced protocol fee revenue generated during the early days after mainnet launch, along with records of using the relevant funds to buy and burn MASK. The screenshots you provided also show the corresponding on-chain burn transactions.

This is the part I believe deserves closer attention.

If users continue using the privacy product, the protocol consistently collects fees, and a designated portion of those fees is used for buybacks and burns, product growth could translate into sustained demand for the token. Burned tokens are removed from circulation, creating a measurable change on the supply side.

However, buybacks should not be evaluated based on announcements alone. We need to verify the actual amount spent, the number of tokens purchased, whether the burns occurred, and whether figures reported in different announcements overlap.

StonkFun's buyback flywheel should also be calculated separately. Its platform buybacks must not be combined with NullMask's own buybacks. Different mechanisms correspond to different revenue sources, and only purchases and burns that actually took place should be counted toward the relevant value-capture mechanism.

NullMask is also expanding its multi-chain support and introducing an early-user points program. These initiatives may accelerate user growth, but points can also attract short-term participants who are primarily interested in incentives.

More importantly, publicly available data shows that TVL remains relatively low and has fluctuated significantly over short periods. This suggests that product fee activity and the amount of capital locked in the product have not yet established a sufficiently stable relationship.

A decline in TVL does not necessarily mean that product demand is disappearing, just as an increase in fees does not necessarily indicate long-term user growth. What really matters is whether users continue depositing, withdrawing, and swapping assets beyond the incentive program, whether product fees continue to grow, and whether the team can translate that activity into verifiable buybacks.

If future reported revenue relies primarily on token reward-related flows, the current fee performance could change rapidly once incentives weaken.

In addition, privacy protocols must contend with technical security, cross-chain dependencies, and regulatory requirements. The broader the product's coverage, the more external components the overall system must trust or depend on. If the privacy mechanism itself encounters problems, or users lose confidence in the service, both revenue and token demand could be affected.

At the token level, even sustained buybacks do not guarantee that the price will rise. Buyback size must be evaluated relative to the current valuation, market selling pressure, and liquidity. If the market valuation grows faster than the protocol's buyback capacity, the mechanism may provide only limited price support.

I believe MASK has a product foundation worth studying. NullMask is not relying solely on a privacy narrative. It has expanded across multiple networks, generated product fees, and established holder reward and buyback-and-burn mechanisms.

However, the most important questions remain unanswered: Can the product generate sufficient sustainable revenue after excluding reward-related flows, and can that revenue be consistently converted into actual MASK purchases and burns?

If genuine user demand continues growing, protocol revenue stabilizes, and the buyback mechanism is repeatedly validated through on-chain data, MASK could evolve from a token driven by early attention into an asset supported by actual product demand.

Conversely, if reported revenue relies primarily on incentive-related fund flows while TVL and user retention fail to improve, the growth reflected in current data may be more fragile than it appears.

For me, the most important metric when evaluating MASK is not how many tokens have already been burned, but whether NullMask can consistently earn money from users who are willing to pay for privacy services and convert a portion of that revenue into sustained demand for MASK.

That will determine whether its buyback mechanism is merely a design intended to attract market attention or a value-capture mechanism capable of operating over the long term.

最近试了下 AIPOCH Open-Science，一个面向 AI 科研的开源工作台。

简单说，就是让 Agent 参与真实科研流程：读数据、跑 Python/R、分析结果，同时把代码、文件和研究过程都保留下来。

我接上 Claude Fable 5.1，拿它复现了一个 AI 圈挺有名的研究：Epoch AI 对 Chinchilla scaling law 的复现。

用的是 Epoch 从论文配图里提取的 245 个公开数据点，按原论文的方法重新拟合，再和两篇论文的结果对比。

Agent 会自己查原论文、写代码拟合、算置信区间、生成图表和报告。拟合出的参数和 Epoch 论文基本一致，中途它还自己发现 scipy 默认的收敛容差会让置信区间偏窄，换了严格容差重跑。

但我更感兴趣的是它的 「.science」。

研究做完后，可以把会话、文件、Notebook 运行记录和验证信息一起打包。

官网放了不少 「.science」 的例子，大家可以参考 ↓

https://t.co/aCMHW6BABy

我实际导出再导入了一遍，比较直观的感受是：别人拿到的不只是最后几张图，还能顺着记录往回看，这个结果到底是怎么跑出来的。想接着做也能直接建副本，我就在副本里换成 MSE 又跑了一轮。

Epoch 当初要从论文配图里一个个抠数据点，缺的就是这样一份过程记录。

这其实挺接近我理解的「Vibe Research」。

让有研究想法的人更容易把想法真正跑起来，同时研究过程也更容易被检查、分享和复现。

如果这套方式继续成熟，科研的门槛确实还会再往下降一些。

Science, open to all.

text:
以前打狗，习惯了用几天甚至几个小时衡量结果
现在🍳预测市场，学会用半年、一年甚至未来几年去建设一件事。

预测市场很难有快速惊人的千百倍财富神话
我们的手续费能返的也不如meme或者合约高
很多很多一切都是空白
创造一个让别人愿意来交易的市场，比找到一个赚钱的机会难太多了。
用户不会凭空出现，流动性不会凭空产生，交易习惯也不是一天就能培养起来的。

我始终觉得，预测市场是 Web3 少数真正有机会把传统互联网用户带进加密世界的产品之一。
过去这么多年，我们一直在向圈外人解释什么是区块链、什么是去中心化、什么是分布式记账，告诉他们 Crypto 有多么伟大。

但说实话，普通人为什么需要懂这些？

一个喜欢足球的人，只是想预测自己支持的球队能不能赢。
一个关心美国大选的人，只是想表达自己对结果的判断。
一个关注黄金、股票或者经济新闻的人，只是想为自己的观点找到一个可以交易的市场。
他们不需要先学习什么是钱包、智能合约、链上结算。他们只需要觉得这个产品有趣、有用，愿意打开它、使用它。
而在这个过程中，他们已经开始接触和使用加密技术了。

我一直觉得，真正的大规模采用，不应该是我们费尽口舌把 Web2 用户教育成 Web3 用户。而是有一天，大家根本不在乎一个产品是不是 Web3，只在乎它好不好用。

就像今天，没有人会因为一个 App 使用了什么数据库、什么服务器架构而决定要不要下载它。

技术应该服务于产品，而不是让用户为了技术去适应产品。

当然，要做到这一步，我们还有太多问题需要解决。流动性、交易体验、市场供给、用户习惯，每一项都不容易。

但至少我相信，我们正在做的事情，不只是让 Crypto 圈里的人多一个可以交易的地方。
而是让更多原本和 Crypto 毫无关系的人，第一次真正使用由加密技术支撑的产品。

这也是为什么，虽然这件事很难，我依然觉得它值得花几年时间去做。

还好，我们有一群愿意一起做难事的人跟愿意相信我们的用户😋

We will win🔮💜🚀

预测市场在商业上是一个好模式，问题是币圈人之前赚钱来得太容易了

做合约 perps，有杠杆，量天然就大。做 meme 交易bot，频率高，手续费一笔接一笔。拿这两个当参照，预测市场确实显得性价比低：没有杠杆，交易量量跑不到合约的级别；也没有 meme 那么高频，手续费收不了那么多

所以现在做预测市场，更像是在做一件难而正确的事。短期很难看到成效，但一旦做起来，后来者想追上会非常难

难在哪：
1️⃣做市商要一家一家谈、一家一家接
2️⃣用户渠道要一点点铺
3️⃣盘口有了 maker，还得想办法吸引更多 taker
4️⃣营销和交易活动要专门为预测市场设计，照搬合约和 meme 那一套行不通
5️⃣交易系统和流动性激励机制非常复杂

我们团队这大半年在 @Predictdotfun 每天做的就是这几件事。每一项都要时间去磨，没做过的人很难想象里面的难度

text:
bankr indexes are a new onchain primitive, and i think they’re foundational.

memes paired with stocks showed people want stock exposure onchain. indexes take it a level deeper: the token is the stocks.

we've seen index tokens before, so what makes this next level?

> no LP. a uniswap v4 hook buys the basket on every buy and mints the index. creators can launch an index without seeding liquidity.

> fees go to holders by backing more stock. the holder cut of every trade stays in the basket as stock, so each MAG7 is backed by a little more after every trade. nothing to claim.

> decentralized rebalancing. no manager market-selling. the index runs dutch auctions anyone can fill, with 48h notice first.

a note if you’re speculating: MAG7 isn’t priced like a memecoin. its price is the value of the stocks it holds, shown live as "backing" on the bankr trade page. buying on bankr mints new MAG7 at that price, so buys don’t pump it. it moves with the 7 stocks. other pools can trade above or below the backing until arbs close the gap, and buying above it means paying more than it’s backed by.

it’s early. right now i’m the only one creating indexes. soon anyone can create their own. until then, swap on bankr to go straight through the hook at the basket’s price.
author: 0xDeployer
quoted_text:
just bought the mag 7 on robinhood chain.

deployed MAG7 this evening, the first index on bankr: one token backed by a basket of up to 20 tokens. and on MAG7, the trading fees go to the holders.

every buy, a uniswap v4 hook buys all 7 stocks from their own pools and mints MAG7. every sell burns MAG7 and sells the basket. one transaction either way. the index itself needs no LP, so creators don’t need to provide liquidity to launch one. it’s already in the pools of the tokens it holds. this isn’t possible without uniswap hooks.

the fees: MAG7 charges 0.50% a trade. i set my creator cut to 0, so 0.30% of every buy and sell goes back into the basket for holders, and 0.20% to the protocol. nobody claims anything. it’s released into the basket over 24h, so after every trade each MAG7 is backed by a little more. creators pick a fee of 0.25–1% at launch and it never changes.

the index never market-sells when rebalancing. it runs dutch auctions, offering what it holds too much of at a price that starts good for holders and gets cheaper every minute until someone fills it. anyone can fill. every rebalance gets 48h notice, so holders can leave first.

you can always swap MAG7 back for the 7 stocks directly. no fee, works without bankr, can’t be paused.

i also seeded a small USDG/MAG7 pool on uniswap so it shows up on dexscreener. but buy on bankr. it goes straight through the hook, which mints new MAG7 at the basket’s price, as deep as the 7 stocks’ own pools rather than my small one. hook trades are also the ones that pay holders. if the pool drifts, arbs close the gap.

it’s early. we’re getting the hook supported in wallets and aggregators before the full rollout. right now it’s just me creating indexes. soon anyone can make their own on base or robinhood.

and then: pairing. you’ll be able to launch a token paired with an index. buying your coin buys the index, the index buys the basket, and your creator fees come in the index.

buying MAG7 on bankr isn’t available in the US or UK.

扎克伯格（@finkd）刚刚晒出自己的办公桌：

没有天价 H200 机柜，只用两台并排的新款 Mac Studio，

就在本地跑起了今天刚开源的 816B 旗舰大模型 

Muse Spark Open

苹果 CEO John Ternus（@johnternus）也在评论区互动，短短几小时浏览量破百万。

816B 总参数、42B 激活参数，靠 MoE 稀疏架构和苹果统一内存，让桌面设备也有机会挑战超大模型。

硬件门槛、部署命令、避坑指南，一文看懂。

一、硬件门槛

1TB 内存：双 Mac Studio，MLX oQ4e，约 476GB 权重

512GB 内存：单台 Mac Studio，MLX oQ3e，约 340GB 权重

256GB 内存：Unsloth UD-Q2_K_XL 或 GGUF Q2_K，约 210GB 权重

700GB 以上显存：4×B200 或 8×H200，部署 NVFP4 版本

以上为原方案中的估算值，实际需求取决于模型版本、运行框架和上下文长度。

二、一键部署

Mac 单机：

uv tool install mlx-lm
mlx_lm.server --model "mlx-community/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-oQ3e" --port 8080

256GB 工作站：
llama serve -hf ggml-org/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-GGUF:Q2_K

企业级 GPU：

VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 vllm serve meta-models/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-NVFP4 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel --max-model-len 1048576

运行前请确认模型仓库、权重格式、框架版本及启动参数均真实可用。

三、三个关键注意事项
采样参数：原方案建议 temperature=1.0、top_p=1.0，关闭 top_k，具体应以模型官方配置为准。

推理强度：确认框架支持的 reasoning_effort 参数后，再选择适合任务的推理等级。

多模态：图像、视频和音频的输入规格应以模型实际支持的配置为准。

从大型 GPU 集群到桌面工作站，超大模型的本地部署正在拓展更多可能。

你的主力机有多少内存？256GB、512GB，还是准备挑战双 Mac Studio？

欢迎评论区晒配置、交流部署经验。

text:
.@VitalikButerin 拆解算力经济学：BTC 拼电力，AI 拼利用率

以太坊联合创始人 Vitalik Buterin 分享了一组对比：比特币挖矿的成本中，算力设备资本支出与电力消耗大致各占一半；而 AI 推理的成本则几乎完全由算力资本支出主导。

这揭示了两种截然不同的商业模式。

1/ BTC 挖矿拼什么？

矿工需要持续支付电费，并承担矿机折旧、全网算力增长和 BTC 价格波动的风险。

低电价、更高的矿机效率，直接决定了挖矿的盈利空间。

2/ AI 推理拼什么？

GPU 采购只是开始，设备利用率、客户需求、硬件迭代和资本回收效率同样重要。

即使拥有大量 GPU，如果利用率不足，昂贵的设备也可能成为沉重的财务负担。

因此，AI 算力不是买到芯片就能赚钱，关键在于能否持续将算力转化为收入。

3/ 为什么矿企开始转向 AI？

比特币减半后，矿工的区块奖励从 6.25 BTC 降至 3.125 BTC，盈利压力随之增加。

与此同时，AI 数据中心需要大量电力、土地和基础设施。部分矿企已经拥有电力接入、场地和能源运营经验，具备向 AI/HPC 业务转型的潜在优势。

例如，IREN、Core Scientific 和 Hut 8 都在推进 AI 或高性能计算相关业务。

但需要注意：有电力不等于有合格的 AI 数据中心，签下大额合同也不等于已经获得收入。设备采购、基础设施改造和客户交付仍需要大量资金与时间。

4/ 真正值得关注的变化

过去，矿企的估值主要围绕 BTC 价格、矿机效率和电力成本展开。

现在，市场开始重新评估它们的电力资源、数据中心能力，以及能否通过长期 AI 合同创造更稳定的现金流。

但 AI 转型并非稳赚不赔。GPU 折旧、融资成本、利用率不足和行业竞争，都可能侵蚀利润。

本质上，BTC 挖矿更直接地受电价与币价影响，AI 推理则更依赖昂贵的计算资本和有效需求。

未来真正有竞争力的企业，不一定拥有最多的算力，而是能够以更低成本获取能源、提高设备利用率，并持续把算力转化为现金流的企业。

AI 对矿企而言，不只是新的叙事，更是一次商业模式的重新选择。

Stacks recently released its Q3 report with updates.

Here's a short TL;DR + some of my thoughts ↓

→ Bitcoin Staking

The first two staking rounds brought in 735 BTC, with 21Shares, HashKey Cloud, and UTXO Management among the participants.

→ Liquid Staking

@StackingDao accounted for 483 BTC of the 505 BTC in the second round. It now has 636 BTC worth of stBTC in circulation.

→ STX Staking

The amount of STX staked has grown by over 25% since the PoX-5 upgrade, from 392M to 493M STX.

→ Lending

@ZestProtocol now has over $122M in deposits and $42M in loans, with around 800 BTC used as collateral.

→ Trading

Trading across Stacks DEXs reached $16.7M in a single week in September, the highest in a year, with @Bitflow leading the activity.

My guess is that BTC staking will end up benefiting more than just the staking protocols.

More people borrowing against their staked BTC → more activity in lending markets and DEXs → more fees going to different parts of the ecosystem.

Quite the opportunity for the entire ecosystem.
