text:
i am bullish privacy and of course ethereum:0xe76c6c83af64e4c60245d8c7de953df673a7a33d, so i wanted to see how privacy competitors like ethereum:0xa12cc123ba206d4031d1c7f6223d1c2ec249f4f3 and solana:PRVT6TB7uss3FrUd2D9xs2zqDBsa3GbMJMwCQsgmeta stack up on my fundamental crypto asset scoreboard.

---

let's start with @zama:

short answer is (unfortunately), like many crypto projects, it is great tech with a weak token.

zama is one of the leading FHE stacks with:

> $647.9M of all-time shielded volume
> $127.5M of shielded TVL
> $104M earning yield in confidential morpho vaults

but almost none of that reaches the token yet.

every protocol fee is paid in ZAMA and burned. the burn is live onchain with 91,064 ZAMA burned on july 17 and another 73,300 waiting for the next batch.

that works out to ~$22.5k a year of burns against an $865M FDV, or ~38,500x.

the supply is also growing a lot faster than it burns. staking mints ~5% a year and the foundation releases 114.6M ZAMA a month from treasury and growth.

net of burns, that's a -19.8% DAAY (dilution-adjusted accrual yield). and even if the foundation holds every tranche, it's -5.7%.

only 22.4% of supply circulates, and the first team and investor cliff hits feb. 2, 2027 (550M ZAMA, ~22% of circulating), then ~302M a month after that.

so even if burns grow 90x to $2M a year by next october, the base case is $0.017, 78% below where it trades today.

working backwards, today's price at fair value needs burns to go from $22.5k to ~$85M a year within 5 years. that's 3,800x, or roughly 5x every year.

in comparison, ethereum:0xe76c6c83af64e4c60245d8c7de953df673a7a33d does ~$4.69M a year in fees on a ~$152M FDV, and nearly all of it reaches stakers through the treasury. that's ~200x the fees at about a sixth of the size.

---

now let's take a look at @UmbraPrivacy:

umbra launched through @MetaDAOProject last october, raising $3M at $0.30 against $155M of commitments.

that makes it an ownership token. the treasury, the mint authority, and the IP all sit with a futarchy-controlled DAO, so the team runs on a $100k/month budget and anything above that needs a DAO-approved proposal.

so structurally, solana:PRVT6TB7uss3FrUd2D9xs2zqDBsa3GbMJMwCQsgmeta gives tokenholders a lot more than ethereum:0xa12cc123ba206d4031d1c7f6223d1c2ec249f4f3 does. the problem is there isn't much to own yet besides the cash.

v1 shielding was free and shielded TVL is only ~$100K.

the first fee sources only went live this week:
> v2 (still invite-only)
> the uUSDv stablecoin (umbra keeps 25% of the yield)

the treasury holds ~$1.4M of stablecoins, or ~$0.06 per outstanding token. at $0.46, solana:PRVT6TB7uss3FrUd2D9xs2zqDBsa3GbMJMwCQsgmeta trades at ~7.8x that, so the market is paying ~$9.5M for a business with no revenue yet.

it has also funded operations by selling treasury tokens, ~3.2M UMBRA over the past year or ~13.5% of outstanding supply. net of a small buyback, that's a -12.1% DAAY.

the positive is that insider tokens only unlock at price targets (2x to 32x the ICO price), and nothing unlocks for at least 6 months.

my base case values the business at ~$6M, roughly where the ICO priced it, plus the cash. that gets to $0.23, ~50% below today after a +136% month.

---

final scores at a 6-month time horizon:

> ethereum:0xe76c6c83af64e4c60245d8c7de953df673a7a33d: 3.0, neutral
> solana:PRVT6TB7uss3FrUd2D9xs2zqDBsa3GbMJMwCQsgmeta: 2.3, underperform
> ethereum:0xa12cc123ba206d4031d1c7f6223d1c2ec249f4f3: 2.2, underperform

FHE and privacy on solana could still become a big part of onchain privacy, but the tokens need to start capturing usage to be valuable.

从Vitalik的实践看：

以太坊可以成为AI实现自动化支付和经济自主路上的重要合作伙伴。

具体来说，Vitalik干了件什么事？

他给自己的 AI 助手做了一套“隐私模式”，

让 AI 能独立地干活/查资料/上网，

且保护隐私：

类似于戴了多层面具上网，每个对话还单独换线路。

让别人很难通过流量分析判断你在干嘛。

4. 本地先用一个小模型把提示词“洗”一遍再发出去

避免原始指令直接泄露。

5. 整个 AI 工具再套一层沙盒和 Tor

进一步隔离。

让 AI 自己干活/花钱/有隐私，

以太坊在这里

提供了“钱包 + 隐私支付 + 可编程”的基础设施。

quoted_text:
Wrapped zkAPI + Tor + extra cover traffic + local LLM prompt rewriting in an open-AI compatible daemon, and made a "paranoid mode" wrapper for my agent harness (pi):

Each conversation gets assigned a separate Tor circuit, your requests are masked with random cover traffic, zkAPI ensures you don't leak your identity through payments, and all prompts are locally rewritten (bring-your-own-local-model; I'm using qwen3.8-flash-next)

https://t.co/MepCFCrLv1

My agent harness is wrapped with a bwrap sandbox (also experimenting with MicroVM) and wrapped again with torsocks, so everything it does goes through Tor.

Here's what me asking it to do a simple research task looks like.

It's getting quite usable! Though you definitely still pay quite a bit in increased latency, especially when starting a new conversation.

Also, Tor is far from optimal here for privacy; the cover traffic mechanism is okay against passive adversaries but much weaker if the LLM provider is colluding with the guard and actively manipulating timing. This kind of task really requires a more specialized mixnet, probably take the tradeoff of a higher bandwidth multiplier and built-in constant cover traffic.

Also also, much cheaper zkAPI deposit and withdraw gas costs are coming to mainnet soon.

text:
周三在北大AI创新创业课听了当年在美团主导“千团大战”的美团前副总杨锦方关于创业团队的选人和组织的分享，非常感同身受。作为一名创业者，真的感觉杨总把多年来选人、识人、区分团队里的“野狗”的焚诀都交出来了。。。

我把全部内容和要点整理如下。

1. 人的杠杆深度远超资金杠杆
资金是基础，但故事和创造来自人：资本固然重要，没有钱就招不到好人，但所有最伟大的创造本质上都是由人驱动的。
人才复利能拉开长期的巨大差距：许多公司刚起步时规模和资金相差无几，但十几年后天差地别。因为市场、产品、策略都是由人决定的。
关键岗位放错人的代价极其昂贵：资金的复利固然重要，但人才的复利同样强大。创业早期关键位置放错人，给组织带来的长期伤害远超一次融资条件谈砸。

2. 识人选人是 CEO 的核心功课，绝不能依赖外包
外部机构无法代做关键战略取舍：猎头和 HR 可以提供工具与候选人，但涉及核心岗位的信任、长短板取舍与组织关系，企业家必须亲自做决定。
识人能力需要结构化训练：基础层面是识别履历和显性风险；进阶层面是结构化评估；最高水平是跨行业识别可迁移的潜力，让有潜质的人在新情境下发挥优势。
必须具备可重复的验证机制：只有当多次重用缺少相关经验的人并获得成功时，才说明识人能力背后有严密的结构，而非凭运气。

3. 先有战略与任务，再建立胜任力模型与找人
架构应当服务于战略任务：组织架构不能凭空画图，而要由企业的战略定位反推。战略任务变化，关键岗位的能力要求也随之改变。
胜任模型（美人图）要透视底层特质：不能只列泛泛的抽象要求，而要看懂某种特质与具体任务的因果关系。比如照顾失能老人和银行风控，看似无关，底层都需要极强的“审慎”与风险预判能力。
切忌盲目追求抽象的“最优秀”：识人高手是通过透视任务本质来寻找匹配特质的人，而不是脱离业务情境去抢泛泛意义上的优秀人才。

4. 自我认知与识人要通过“记录—预测—反馈—修正”实现闭环
拒绝模糊的“感觉不错”：面试或评估一个人时，必须记录下事实依据与具体判断，而不是仅凭感觉。
用后续行为校准认知：把当时对人的判断写下来，预测他在某种情境下的表现，过一段时间用实际结果来自我校准与修正。
一手资料比二手讲述更有价值：练习识人时，看当事人的原文、访谈和自传，往往比听别人的二次传述更直接，语言是思维的直接载体。

5. 价值观是压力之下的价值排序原则，更是行为底线
价值观回答“压力之下怎么做才对组织好”：平时没压力时看不出价值观，只有当利益发生尖锐冲突、没有明确细则可遵循时，价值观才是底层取舍依据。部门冲突的根源在于公司级价值排序缺失：美团早期销售团队与品控、客服部门频繁打架，本质上是各部门站在各自角度看待“对公司好”。明确了“消费者第一、商家第二、员工第三、股东第四、创始人第五”的排序后，合力才真正形成。
价值观不是法律、制度或口号：它不是用来做宣传的标语，而是日常工作点滴中对行为和取舍的约束原则。

6. 价值观必须融入招聘入口与核心管理机制
在招聘入口严格收紧：有愿景和认同使命的人，在面临挫折时能走得更远，成长幅度也更大。招聘时就要筛选那些相信公司未来的人。
在真实冲突场景中考察价值观：面试时要重点询问候选人在有压力、有利益冲突的环境里如何选择，把谁的利益放在前头。
评价与执行必须基于事实：高层不遵守、评价凭印象打标签、用权力打击异己，这三种做法会彻底摧毁组织的价值观。价值观评价需要管理者投入大量时间去观察细节与事实。

7. AI 时代面对不确定性，要持“强观点、弱执念”
接受世界的高度不确定性：互联网和 AI 时代最大的特点就是极度不确定。不能等不确定性变成确定性再行动，那样往往就太晚了。
Strong opinions（强观点）：对事情的判断要有极其扎实的事实依据和严密逻辑，自信来自于深刻研究而非凭空想象。
Weakly held（弱执念）：对未来保持高度开放的心态。一旦外部环境发生深刻变化、出现新证据，要敢于推翻并拆掉原有的认知框架，重新建立新的看法。

text:
睡前无意间刷到孙雨晨的最新访谈，又熬了个夜，这个访谈竟然少有人提及，把好东西都藏着是吧，今天早上我整理了一下。
认知的本质是判断力。这47分钟信息量极大，包含了@justinsuntron @sunyuchentron 他关于加密货币、AI、美股、美债、个人投资的判断。

1. Solana 可以合作，但大资金做 DeFi 收益，还是更适合以太坊。 他认为 Solana 没什么问题，波场也正常与其合作。但自己做 DeFi 挖矿，主要追求的是收益和流动性，不是赌 ETH 涨跌。其他链的流动性相对有限，对于他这种大资金体量，以太坊仍然是主要选择。

2. Hyperliquid 是这个周期最大的发现之一。 他看好的不只是去中心化合约交易，而是 Hyperliquid 把美股永续合约带进了加密市场。传统股票可以通过永续合约获得新的交易方式，虽然其他平台已经开始跟进，但这个方向打开了整个行业的想象空间。

3. DEX 能不能取代大量 CEX，关键在美国监管。 他认为 Hyperliquid 处于中心化与去中心化交易所之间。如果美国给予接近 Uniswap 的监管豁免，大量 CEX 可能主动转型，减少牌照和合规成本。如果最终需要承担类似 Coinbase 的监管义务，Hyperliquid 反而会面临很大压力，因为它在合规经验和组织成熟度上不一定具备优势。

4. 他现在比以前更加看空 BTC，核心原因是 AI 和量子计算对密码学的威胁。 比特币已经成为成熟的 ETF 投资品，很多传统投资者通过 BlackRock 等机构持有 BTC，但未必理解 Q-Day 带来的潜在风险。他认为市场还没有充分定价这件事。

5. 他认为 Q-Day 可能已经是未来一到两年需要认真考虑的事情。 过去他保守估计还有两年，现在随着 AI 在数学能力上的进展，甚至开始考虑一年到一年半的可能性。他还提出一种更激进的担忧，未来未必需要等到成熟的量子计算机，经典计算方法的突破也可能威胁部分钱包安全。

6. 比特币最大的抗量子问题，不是技术升级，而是无法要求所有持币者主动升级。 即使社区推出抗量子地址，持币者仍然需要主动迁移资产。中本聪的比特币、遗失私钥的钱包以及大量多年未动的地址，都可能无法完成迁移。他担心原本被认为永久退出流通的上百万甚至约200万枚 BTC，在极端情况下重新进入市场，形成巨大抛压。

7. 比特币社区很难通过冻结旧币解决这个问题。 他认为针对早期地址进行冻结、限制流通或者硬分叉，需要矿工、开发者和社区形成共识。但比特币历史上缺少这样的先例，去中心化程度越高，统一行动的难度也越大。

8. 他的第一步应对方式不是卖币，而是改变资产存储方式。 他提出将 BTC 转移到从未对外签名、没有转出记录的新地址。每次需要动用资产时，再把剩余 BTC 转到新的地址。他将这种做法称为掩体模式，准备先对相关资产进行隔离，再观察技术进展决定是否减仓。

9. 密码学危机可能影响整个互联网，而不只是币圈。 他认为一旦底层公钥密码体系受到严重威胁，网站证书、银行、交易所和其他依赖数字签名的系统都需要应对。极端情况下，可能需要先保存数据和状态，等待可靠的新方案，再恢复区块链及交易所系统。

10. 波场和火币已经投入资源研究抗量子方案。 他提到已经有相关测试网，希望在预计的 Q-Day 到来前约一年部署到主网。但他也承认，目前还没有完整的金融对冲策略，主要是先提高资产安全性，密切跟踪技术变化。

11. 人民币未来会走强。

12. 市场对美债信用危机的担忧过度了。 他认为美债规模已经大到不能简单用普通企业还债的方式理解。美国可以不断发行新债偿还旧债，只要市场持续愿意购买，这套体系就可以运行。而市场愿意购买美债，根本原因仍然是美国在科技、军事和全球金融体系中的优势。

13. AI 反而可能成为维持美债信用的重要支撑。 他认为美国目前控制着先进芯片、关键产业链和重要 AI 技术，只要这种优势没有发生根本改变，美债就不容易失去买家。近期美债收益率上升，在他的解释里，不完全是信用恶化，也可能是 AI 权益资产正在与美债争夺资金。

14. 他不看好老登资产，更愿意配置新登资产。 他的分类主要依据产业所处的时代。传统消费和旧经济资产不是重点，代表未来技术变化的新产业更值得积极参与。访谈里对白酒等传统资产的负态度也比较明确。

15. 过去一年最大的失败是感情。 他认为一段关系的失败，不一定是整个人生的失败，也可能成为以后的人生经验。口碑同样重要，但人的社会评价会随着所处阶段变化，他更倾向于了解舆情、参与交流，而不是认为一次争议会永久决定一个人的形象。

16. 他现在最缺少的不是钱，而是对 AI 的理解和应用能力。 他表示自己已经在努力学习，但仍认为这是一种非常稀缺的能力。未来最大的个人目标，是找到 AI 与现有业务结合的位置，让自己和公司适应新的技术时代。

17. 他认为健康管理的目标不是无限延寿，而是尽可能提高健康寿命和生命质量。 他已经尝试通过 AI 监测身体数据，希望在合理寿命范围内改善健康状况，最终能够有尊严、有体面地离开。对于人生本身，他更愿意把它理解为各种体验的集合，而不是别人对自己成就的评价。

18. 孙学最适合没有资源和背景的普通年轻人。 他认为孙学是一套几乎零成本就能学习的思维系统，帮助人完成从0到1的起步。如果一个人本身已经拥有很强的能力和资源，就未必需要按照这套方法行动，可以发展自己的判断体系。

19. 孙学的核心是根据时代变化，寻找对自己最有利的博弈路径。 他不认同把孙学简单归类为精致利己主义，而是更接近博弈论和演化论。2016年他曾建议年轻人不要急着结婚买房，而是关注英伟达、特斯拉等新资产。他认为策略不应该永久固定，而应该跟随技术和时代变化调整。

20. 他推荐的三本书是安·兰德的《源泉》、王小波的《黄金时代》和自己的孙学。 他认为安·兰德的思想与孙学存在一定联系，《黄金时代》虽然以性和个人经历为背景，却包含对一个时代的深层观察。

21. 他想把孙宇晨奖做成 AI 时代的诺贝尔奖。 他认为 AI 可能大幅提高科学发现和数学研究的速度，未来每天都可能出现过去需要很长时间才能完成的成果。所以他没有一开始就投入巨额奖金，而是希望先测试机制，再不断迭代。

22. 孙宇晨奖尝试让机器参与成果验证和发奖。 按照他的描述，任何人都可以借助 AI 解答题集，只要成果通过机器验证，就能够获得奖励。他表示已经产生第一批获奖者，希望未来的科研奖励体系能适应机器大规模参与科学研究的时代。

23. 他现在最看好 AI 应用，而不是继续追逐最热门的算力资产。 他认为英伟达市值已经非常庞大，即使长期发展空间仍然存在，投资回报倍数也会受到规模限制。他提出一个自己的估值判断，全球最大单一企业的市值很难超过美债总规模的一半，因此英伟达潜在的上涨倍数可能不如早期应用公司。

24. AI 健康管理是他特别看好的应用方向。 他提到了 Oura Ring 这类可穿戴设备，但认为单纯收集数据还不够。完整的机会应该包括身体数据采集、数据处理、AI 分析和个性化健康决策，将这些环节连接起来，才能形成真正的产品价值。

25. 未来看病可能从生病后治疗，转向持续的数据驱动管理。 他设想每年固定去医院进行几次检查，采集消费级设备无法获取的血液等医疗数据，再结合戒指、手环等设备的日常数据，由 AI 提供健康建议，最后由医生进行复核。这种模式如果成熟，医疗保险和整个健康产业也需要调整。

26. 他认为存储、光模块等部分 AI 硬件资产已经被高估。 原因不是这些产品没有需求，而是市场还没有找到足够多、足够成熟的 AI 应用，资金只能集中到英伟达、存储、光模块以及少数大模型公司。他认为不少硬件企业已经被市场给予接近软件公司的估值预期。

27. 他预测未来一两年 AI 投资主题会开始分化。 现在的资金主要围绕大模型和硬件抱团，但随着 AI 应用开始进入医疗、数据处理和其他行业，新的商业模式会陆续出现。届时市场不再只关注谁生产芯片，也会开始关注谁真正利用 AI 解决问题。

28. 他目前对纳斯达克和 AI 股票短中期微微看空，但还没有做空。 他仍然持有英伟达和纳指相关资产，只是认为资金抱团过于严重，同时 AI 企业之间存在较多循环投资和相互依赖。一旦融资环境或者增长预期出现变化，市场可能受到连锁影响。

29. 他认为 AI 基础设施存在阶段性产能过剩的可能。 他拿2000年前后的互联网泡沫举例，当时很多光纤公司破产，但留下的光纤后来确实派上了用场。AI 也可能出现类似情况，长期基础设施有价值，不代表短期投入这些资产的投资者都能赚到钱。

30. 他透露此前已经在 ETH 约3600至4000美元的位置减持了大部分仓位。 按照他的说法，当时 ETH 冲击高位失败，随后依靠 ETF 资金和 Tom Lee 等人的推动再次上涨，形成了比较明显的双顶结构。他判断第二次上涨缺少足够扎实的支撑，因此卖掉了约80%至90%的 ETH 仓位。

31. BTC 是底仓，ETH 是进攻仓位。 他表示此前没有同步减持 BTC，因为 BTC 在其资产配置里属于长期底仓。ETH 则可以根据周期、价格结构和市场资金变化主动调整。减持后的 ETH 至今还没有大量买回，仅保留了一部分基础仓位。

32. 减持 ETH 后，他把相当一部分资金转向了美股。 当时他们判断美股会出现资金抱团，所以并不是简单持有现金等待 ETH 回调，而是在不同资产之间重新配置。这也解释了为什么他现在既重仓部分美股，又开始担心 AI 资产的集中度和估值风险。

33. 他认为 RWA 上链空间很大，波场准备从美元稳定币扩展到美股资产。 他表示计划在2026年11月推动大部分美股资产在波场上链。因为波场早期通过美元稳定币积累了大量非美元地区的用户，下一步是让这些用户不仅能够持有美元，还能获得美股和指数类资产的配置渠道。

34. 在他看来，美元稳定币本身就是一种面向非美元国家的资产配置产品。 很多用户使用 USDT，不只是为了转账，更是为了持有当地金融体系难以提供的美元资产。因此，从美元稳定币延伸到美股 RWA，是利用已有客户群体销售更多美元资产，而不是完全重新寻找用户。

35. 波场不打算为了竞争，把手续费立即降到最低。 他承认波场转账成本比早年更高，但表示过去一年已经降费约60%，用户也可以通过质押 TRX 等方式降低转账成本。他认为波场沉淀了超过1000亿美元的资金，已经形成品牌、安全感和网络效应，因此可以收取一定溢价。

36. 波场未来不只是提供转账服务，而是增加用户可以购买的资产。 他把早期稳定币转账比作支付业务的第一阶段，下一步是让原有用户直接配置 QQQ、标普500等资产。如果 RWA 业务推进顺利，未来也不排除继续降低手续费，通过更多产品和交易活动扩大整个生态的价值。

text:
小黄人 Unipcs 的喊单能力，依旧不容小觑。
自从他买入 $MASK 以来，这枚代币已经上涨了 133%。

（虽然严格来说，Unipcs 只是在 FOMO 收到该代币，具体的买入时间并不清晰）

1/ Nullmask 在讲什么故事？
@NullMaskio 讲的是“一个更好用的隐私协议”的故事。
用户不用下载新软件，也不用换钱包，只需在自己平时用的钱包里接入它的网络，就能在以太坊、Solana 等主流公链上实现完全匿名的转账、换币和提现。
它把原本复杂的隐私保护技术，做成了傻瓜式操作，谁都能上手。

而且 Nullmask 已经用真实收入证明了自己：过去 30 天收入达到 76 万美元，稳居隐私赛道第一。

2/ 有没有叙事上能媲美 $MASK 的项目？
我觉得是 @Americanfort_io，它的叙事可以概括为——隐私版 ENS。

AmericanFortress 是怎么做隐私的？
AF 的思路是，让你像用支付宝一样在链上隐私转账。
它独创了 Send-to-Name（向昵称转账）功能，只需三步：
▌第一步：注册专属 ID。就像注册推特或微信账号一样简单，而且这个 ID 在所有 AF 支持的区块链上通用。
▌第二步：像支付宝一样公开收款。别人只需要输入你的 ID 就能转账给你，再也不用复制粘贴又长又乱的钱包地址。虽然对方看到、输入的是你的名称，但在链上，系统会自动为这笔交易生成一个全新的隐身地址，外人完全无法把这个地址和你本人、以及你的真实余额对上号。
▌第三步：隐身发送。这一步依靠零知识证明技术来保护隐私，而且绝不是简单粗暴地把大家的钱混在一起（不是混币模式），整个过程完全由你自己掌控。

3/ 一句话总结两者的区别
AmericanFortress 的逻辑是 ID 唯一、地址常新，交易生成专属的新地址，最大限度减少外人把你的姓名、钱包地址和交易记录拼凑关联起来的可能。
而 Nullmask 更像是“大家把钱存进同一个大账本，池子内部的转账彼此不可见”的大锅饭模式，优势在于能无缝兼容现有基础设施，把使用门槛降到最低。

1/ 第一个例子 - @hypurrdash
HyperDash 是第一个经典案例。

在很多人眼里，HyperDash 不过是 Hyperliquid 的一个数据分析网站。但很少有人注意到它的收入。
▌2026 年 Q2：协议收入 17 万美元
▌2026 年 Q3：协议收入 40 万美元
单看收入，这已经超过了很多 DeFi 协议。

它的路径也很清晰：
2024 年创立，作为 Hyperliquid 的独立分析仪表盘；
2025 年 11 月被 https://t.co/j488bpXdUE 收购，从分析平台向交易终端转型；
2026 年 7 月收购机构级数据公司 Imperator，成为 Hyperliquid 的活跃验证节点。

先用分析工具吸引用户，再培养粘性，最后提供交易能力、培养交易习惯。HyperDash 证明了，只要服务足够有用，用户和收入都是水到渠成的事。
Hyperdash 传送：https://t.co/QUUx8xL4ZZ

2/ 第二个例子 - @leveracc_xyz
和 HyperDash 不同，Lever/acc 更早期，10 月 12 日才正式对外公布，不到一周。
而且它一开始就把交易功能内嵌在产品里，没有走先工具后交易的老路。

它是什么？
Lever/acc 是 Hyperliquid 上的信用与结算协议，交易者用自有 USDC 作抵押，最多可借入 4 倍资金，也就是拿到 5 倍购买力去做永续合约。
我自己试了一把，充值 100 USDC，借出 400 USDC，开了一张 HYPE 多单，舔了 3% 涨幅就离场。整个过程轻松丝滑。
（如图）

问题来了：LeverAcc 为什么敢给更高杠杆？
关键在于，它的借款不是通用资金，而是绑定到 Hyperliquid 交易账户的专用信用。由此带来几层控制：
▌资金用途被锁定
借到的 USDC 会直接进入用户在 HyperCore 的交易账户，用户当然可以提现，但每次提现都会重新核算实时账户价值与未偿债务，只放行安全范围内的那部分。
▌实时健康监控 + 自动降风险
Aave 这类协议靠预言机 + 清算，LeverAcc 靠的是持续监控健康度 + 自动执行：
健康度 > 1.167 - 可以正常交易
健康度≤ 1.167 - 禁止加重仓位
健康度 ≤ 1.125 - 开始减仓
健康度 ≤ 1.05 - 减掉 65% 仓位
说人话就是，系统会实时盯着你的单子，并有权替你减仓。用户最多只能亏掉本金。
▌兜底设计
LeverAcc 还会在 Hyperliquid 上为每个借款仓位挂 reduce-only 止损单。就算 LeverAcc 服务宕机、RPC 拥堵、轮询没跟上，交易所本身也会按止损价平仓。

LeverAcc 传送： https://t.co/1ZlrjMHaFR
目前还在测试阶段，建议小额体验，别上大资金。

text:
never borrow someone else their conviction.

you can borrow ideas. let someone point you towards a project, a sector, a thesis. but if you’re putting sized money behind it, the understanding has to be your own.

otherwise, when price moves against you, you’re dependent on someone else to tell you whether the opportunity got better or the thesis broke.

the larger the position, the deeper your understanding should be. aim to know more than 99% of the market: what drives demand, where value accrues, what the market is missing and what would prove you wrong.

i try to apply that standard even to things i never end up buying. most research doesn’t result in big positions

study enough projects and you start recognising the same incentives, weaknesses and patterns across different sectors. you have context for things other people are seeing for the first time.

that’s where it compounds. every new idea becomes easier to evaluate because you have more to compare it against.

in a market where so many people outsource their thinking, building your own understanding is an edge you can keep developing for years.

text:
Ethereum's ZK L2s in the Age of Quantum, Privacy and AI

Since the 1st of September, $ETH is down 1.4%.

Over the same stretch, $STRK is up 173%, $ZK 81% and $AZTEC 50%.

For a sector that mostly makes headlines with shutdowns these days, that's quite the outlier. Blast and Abstract are shutting down. Polygon switched off its own zkEVM sequencer on the 1st of July, Zero Network wound down over the summer, and Mint closes withdrawals on the 20th of October.

So what do Starknet, zkSync and Aztec have that most other L2s don't?

Exposure to the two narratives gaining the most steam right now: privacy and quantum, with AI accelerating both.

What makes it interesting is that all three are ZK rollups from the same tech family, yet they're heading in very different directions:

- @Starknet is going all in on quantum resistance, to the point of asking its stakers whether it should leave Ethereum, while adding compliant privacy to a public chain.

- @zksync is focused on institutions, building private chains for banks, and stays fairly quiet on quantum dates so far.

- @aztecnetwork has the most ambitious privacy of the three and the most conservative published quantum plan, with a full migration targeted for the end of 2030.

Quick context if you missed the last two weeks:

On the 7th of October, @drakefjustin warned that AI-driven math might break the signatures securing our wallets before a quantum computer ever does, "in the worst case in months not years". While most cryptographers pushed back, the debate fueled the attention the AI & quantum threat vectors get, and accelerated the corresponding narratives.

Partly because the cost of a quantum attack keeps falling. In March, Google estimated a break of the curve behind Bitcoin and Ethereum keys at under 1,200 logical qubits. A public contest of AI coding agents (ECDSA(.)fail) halved that estimate within about two months. And on the 16th of October, @AnthropicAI showed Claude designing a circuit for the core step of that attack with 17x fewer gates, at the cost of only 12% more qubits.

No quantum hardware ran and nothing got broken yet tho.

However, the timelines everyone plans around just got significantly shorter.

For ZK L2s that boils down to two questions:

- Quantum: how much of your cryptography can you swap out, and who controls that swap?

- Privacy: who can see your data, today and in 2035?

And here's where it gets more nuanced and subtle: quantum risk is really three different risks:

- Proof forgery: a quantum computer fakes a validity proof. Only possible once that machine exists, and nothing that happened before is affected.

- Key theft: exposed public keys get cracked. Fixable with new signature schemes and a migration.

- Harvest now, decrypt later: someone stores encrypted data published today and decrypts it once the machine exists. This one works retroactively, so for anything private you put on chain, the clock is already running.

That third risk matters most here, because it’s the only one where today’s data is already exposed to a future quantum computer. And once you factor it in properly, the chain with the strongest quantum story isn’t automatically the one that best protects your data.

But let's dig into the deeper comparison:

1) @Starknet

- Proofs: hash-based end to end
- Privacy: STRK20, opt-in, live since June
- PQ Target: "first fully quantum-resistant network" by 2027

Starknet has the strongest proof story of the three. Its STARK proofs rely on nothing but hash functions, a Falcon-512 account already sent a mainnet tx for $0.027, and a phone signed a testnet tx with an ML-DSA key without needing a hard fork. Still, the team itself says Starknet isn't quantum-safe yet, since default accounts use elliptic-curve signatures and the chain depends on Ethereum's blobs for data. That dependency is what the current vote is about. It's non-binding and a yes only kicks off research, but 99.95% of votes so far are in favour. Where Starknet gets weaker is privacy. STRK20 stores encrypted notes on chain using elliptic curves, and every user's viewing key is encrypted to one master auditor key, held in an enclave by Financial Privacy Inc and backed by a 3 of 4 StarkWare/FPI multisig. For a regulator, that works as intended. For a future quantum computer, @l2beat rates it exposed: break the curve, derive the auditor key from its public key, and you're able to read everyone's onchain history. On top of that, Starknet's post-quantum signatures are lattice-based, the family @VitalikButerin flagged as the new risk area in the age of AI. Account abstraction means it can switch again if needed tho.

2) @zksync

- Proofs: hash-based inside, BN254 wrapper on Ethereum
- Privacy: Prividium, permissioned
- PQ Target: no specific date

zkSync hasn't put a date on going post-quantum. Its focus right now is institutions. Prividium gives each one its own private chain, where the data stays in the bank's own infrastructure and only proofs get posted to Ethereum. As it happens, that design lines up well with the checklist Vitalik laid out on the 7th of October, and @gluk64 was quick to point it out two days later. Since nothing encrypted ever gets published, there is nothing to harvest, which makes it the cleanest answer to harvest now, decrypt later of the three. The tradeoff is who you're private from: the public, yes, the operator, no. It's basically a private database with public proofs of correctness, which is exactly what a bank wants. The other gap is the wrapper. zkSync's big hash-based proof gets compressed into a small one so Ethereum can verify it cheaply, and that small proof relies on BN254 elliptic-curve pairings, the part a quantum computer breaks. That's where Airbender Prime comes in. Launched on the 13th of October, zkSync's new prover proved 99% of 7,200 consecutive mainnet blocks in under 10 seconds on a single RTX PRO 6000 GPU, a.k.a. real-time proving of Ethereum on hardware that fits under a desk (zkSync's own benchmark tho, not independently replicated yet). Vitalik congratulated the team two days later and called the battle for speed "definitively won". Prime also comes with a Keccak path for verifying proofs on Ethereum, which would remove the BN254 wrapper, but that part is announced rather than shipped, with no specific date attached yet.

3) @aztecnetwork

- Proofs: pairing-based, generated on your device
- Privacy: private by default, programmable
- PQ Target: full post-quantum migration by end of 2030

Aztec is the only one of the three running private smart contracts on a public network, with proofs generated on your own laptop or phone (2.5 seconds for a private transfer on a laptop on V5). That same design is why it's the slowest on quantum. Its prover has to run on a phone, recurse quickly and keep proofs small, and according to Aztec no post-quantum proof system manages all three today, with the fast ones producing proofs of around 300KB. So the plan is to pick first and migrate later: a signature scheme by March 2027, encryption by July 2027, the proving system by November 2027, and a full migration by the end of 2030. On harvest now, decrypt later, it comes down to the app. Keys are hashed and notes can be delivered offchain, but an app that posts EC-encrypted notes on chain is still exposed (L2BEAT flags zk(.)money for exactly that). @Zac_Aztec argues that rushed cryptography and implementation bugs are the bigger risk right now, and Aztec has a case in point: its own AI audit harness caught a critical soundness bug in V5 that months of human audits had missed.

Put side by side, the chain with the best proofs right now has the weakest privacy story against a quantum adversary. The institutional chain has the cleanest one. And for Aztec, it depends on what each app decides to publish.

Where does AI come in?

So far, mostly on the attack side, and mainly in three ways:

- It makes quantum attacks cheaper: ECDSA(.)fail matched Google's estimate within 8 hours and beat it in about 3 days, and Claude's 17x gate reduction came out of a single 53-hour run.

- It finds cracks in structured math: Claude cut the cost of recovering a key for HAWK, a lattice-based signature scheme, from 2^64 to 2^38 operations, and NIST withdrew it.

- It finds the bugs humans miss, as Aztec's V5 showed.

To keep it in perspective tho: no AI-assisted break of ECDSA has been published, and Drake's "months not years" was a worst case scenario voiced as a personal opinion.

The defences all three are converging on look similar: hash-based cryptography wherever possible, formal verification, and crypto agility, a.k.a. being able to swap your signature scheme without forking the chain or changing anyone's address.

It's also where Vitalik says the focus has to go on the zkEVM front now that speed is solved: formally verifying that a zkEVM actually matches the Ethereum spec, a hard cap on prover cost relative to the gas in a block, and the security of the proof system itself. With AI getting this good at finding bugs, that list matters more than yet another speed benchmark.

The market's reaction to the recent moves/announcements by these three players and their above-outlined approaches was remarkably positive:

At its peak on the 12th of October, STRK was trading at more than 4.7x its price from the 1st of September, on $741M of daily volume. ZK added another 23% and AZTEC 20% since Drake's warning on the 7th of October, while ETH lost 10% over the same days.

Since then, STRK has given back 42% from that peak tho, and part of the pressure sits in the supply schedule. Around 127M STRK unlocked on the 15th, roughly 1.7% of circulating supply, landing on the same day the L1 vote opened. ZK's monthly unlock of roughly 173M, about 1.6% of circulating supply, lands today as well. And for AZTEC, the genesis sequencer unlock follows on the 13th of November, with team and investor cliffs in February 2027.

So the narrative got priced on attention and hype within weeks, while the actual migrations run on timelines measured in years and supply dynamics at play that you should always keep in mind too.

My take:

None of the three is quantum-safe today, and all three admit to that. Narrative-wise, with a potential move to a fully quantum-resistant L1, or generally if you care about proofs, Starknet is clearly ahead.

If you care about privacy that still holds up in 2035 tho, the institutionally-focused approach of publishing nothing (zkSync) or keeping notes offchain (an option on Aztec) beats encrypting the data fully onchain.

But in conclusion, it's definitely worth keeping all three on your radar for now imo.

What I'm watching next here (aside from the charts kek)?

@gluk64's Money20/20 keynote on the 21st of October (teased as "Who's in control?"), the Starknet vote result on the 22nd re L1 migration, the Aztec V6 vote, and zkSync's Airbender Prime Keccak verifier actually going live.

NFA tho. DYOR.

text:
a note about weekends on hyperliquid.

most weekends on hyperliquid see a small window of semi-scheduled maintenance, usually but not always saturday afternoon east asian time. these windows present systemic challenges to papertrade by consequence of hypercore block production briefly halting, and the short "post only" period across their books that follows.

due to this, there are two things to know. the first is that we will be progressively lowering the leverage and OI caps available on papertrade from up to 60 minutes before the window begins, and will not be processing any trades after the upgrade at all until such a time as the "post only" period is over, and we can confirm the books are live once more.

finally, since the oracle will remain stale for some of this period, should off-chain prices deviate too far from our last recorded mid price such that the exchange faces systemic losses on either our ETH or BTC markets, it is possible we may have to freeze one or both of the markets.

once frozen, a markets oracle price is locked, forever, and will stop updating with the hyperliquid books. traders with positions in such a market are free to close them out at their leisure at the last recorded BBO price before the freeze.

we do not anticipate this will ever be necessary to trigger, and we are working with the hyperliquid team in order to try and improve the experience during exchange downtime in the future.

text:
He crashed a million-dollar car he never insured, then told the friend sitting next to him he thought it would never happen to him.

“Watch this.”

That’s what Elon Musk said right before he lost control of his own McLaren F1.

His name is Elon Musk. The year was 2000. He’d just pocketed $22 million selling his first company, Zip2, and used $1 million of it on one of only 106 McLaren F1s ever built. He was driving Peter Thiel to pitch Sequoia Capital for what would become PayPal when Thiel asked what the car could do.

Musk floored it. The F1 had 640 horsepower, weighed barely a ton, and had zero traction control. The back end snapped out instantly, spun the car backward into an embankment, and launched it into the air spinning like a discus.

Both men walked away unhurt. The car didn’t. According to Thiel, Musk’s first words afterward were that he’d read plenty of stories about guys who made money, bought a supercar, and crashed it, and figured it would never happen to him, which is also why he never bought insurance.

They hitchhiked separately to the meeting instead of showing up together.

Honestly, the detail that stays with me isn’t the crash, it’s that he still made the pitch meeting that same day, uninsured wreck and all, like the car was just a line item he’d deal with later.

Would you have skipped insurance on a million-dollar car too, or is that exactly the kind of bet that only looks smart once you’re already a billionaire?

text: Ethereum is shipping upgrades faster while the chain is getting less, not more buggy. Advancements in formal verification help make this possible
author: materkel
quoted_text:
AI is making Ethereum more ambitious.

You might have heard about the challenges that blockchains face in a post-AI world, and while security assumptions will surely be stress-tested in the coming months and years, there is another side to it. I believe AI will let us speedrun towards a world that's both more secure and feature-rich.

As we look towards Ethereum's first post-AI upgrade, Hegotá, the R&D community is asking itself what increasingly powerful tools could help us do differently:

> How far can we push both security and iteration speed?
> How much of the design space can we examine before committing to one?
> How easily can we test the interactions between complex features?

My recent formal verification work @ethlabs_org has given me some reasons to be optimistic about these, as work that would have previously not even been attempted is now being done by agents in days. In September, I posted about using formal verification as part of designing a new consensus protocol. This time, I want to tell you about formally verifying something already fully specified and in production: Ethereum's Fast Confirmation Rule (FCR).

If you are not familiar with FCR, it lets applications confirm Ethereum blocks in seconds, roughly 30x faster than waiting for finality, under additional assumptions (from waiting 13 minutes to 24 seconds!). It also further solidifies Ethereum L1's case as an asset hub and center of gravity for the onchain economy. FCR now has a safety proof in Lean, closely modeling the rule in the consensus specs, which is the source of truth for Ethereum's consensus clients.

Some takeaways:

> FCR is safe! Under its assumptions, confirmed blocks remain canonical. On top of the manual proofs from the paper, we now have Lean proofs of this for the actual spec, additional evidence for applications considering FCR!

> The bulk of the formal verification work took just a 4-5 days (check out the animation!), with agents working mostly unsupervised. We should be very ambitious about using this as a tool at scale.

> After verifying the current rule, it was easy to adapt the model to the upcoming Gloas changes. Immediately, this surfaced a subtle bug caused by changes to fork choice. The problem was in the spec itself and not a gap in the model. The safety proof would not go through, and the agents could precisely pinpoint what was causing it to fail. The bug is now fixed, and formal verification of the corrected protocol goes through.

Iteration is never quite over, even for "finished" features like FCR, because the protocol keeps evolving around them. A formal model lets us ensure that key properties keep holding throughout the evolution of the protocol. With these capabilities, Ethereum can and should keep upgrading faster, tightening fork timelines and exploring more ambitious features, while still raising the security bar.

This picture has been getting much clearer over the past few months, and the past week confirmed it for me, as @drakefjustin and @corcoranwill brought together 100+ Ethereum researchers, cryptographers and formal verification experts in Cambridge for six days of workshops on post-quantum cryptography, formal verification and fast finality. Beyond its own workshop, formal verification was the omnipresent star of the week: everyone is using Lean and doing amazing things with it! Piece by piece, Ethereum's technological core is being rebuilt for the post-AI age.

The excitement was palpable, the sense of optimism was pervasive, and every talk and conversation carried a level of ambition I'd never seen before. The Ethereum R&D machine is upgrading itself, and we will see the outcome of that on the network sooner than you think.

Announcing the public preview of https://t.co/VdMOPBsL7H: a lightweight Ethereum indexing node for research and apps on your own infra.

Building on Ethereum shouldn’t require a third-party RPC, and it definitely shouldn’t require a full node.

The concept is simple. You define the structure of your data via a processor, and Leani fulfills your history requests while also (optionally) serving live data.

This enables you to quickly build a backend for tracking Uniswap prices or even a browsable blobs leaderboard like https://t.co/QSxtb5mFhw, all while saving plenty of storage and RPC costs.

Leani comes with a handful of built-in processors, but it is easy to write your own. Simply point your agent towards the repo: https://t.co/GhLiFN3bLs.

Leani can be used as an RPC drop-in for all methods that do not require the EVM, through its HTTP API, by streaming changes over SSE, or with a dedicated TypeScript SDK.

text:
Thoughts on AI adoption in the semiconductor industry (takeaways from today’s seminar)

1. Many engineers, myself included, have felt a sense of unease while using AI. Watching it solve in just a few hours what used to take us days... Everyone seems to agree that major changes are coming over the next few years.

2. What’s interesting is how much AI policies differ across companies. Companies with their own models and abundant compute are using AI more aggressively in chip design. Personally, I think this gap will translate into enormous differences in design capabilities over time.

3. In chip design, I think architects who can see the entire system will become the most valuable, beyond engineers focused solely on RTL, DFT, STA, or PD. Circuit designers who can come up with truly original architectures, whether analog or digital, will also command a growing premium.

4. Another critical skill is the ability to quickly review AI outputs and explain the underlying data convincingly to management. One insight from the discussion was that being able to quickly spot AI hallucinations or determine whether verification cases actually ran in the correct environment will become increasingly important.

5. Another noticeable trend is that AI adoption is bringing ROI into the conversation. Management has to justify the spending, so managing AI resources is becoming a growing concern alongside managing people. Apparently, when teams lose headcount, “We need more people” is turning into “We need more tokens.” That was a little chilling to hear.

I guess I should start figuring out what else I can do before AI replaces me! 🥸

text:
近期三个热门项目：@metricxyz、@forevercultfund、@NullMaskio。

1.  Metric：让 AMM 从被动定价走向主动做市

Metric 的核心产品叫 Active Pools，属于 PropAMM（专业做市商 AMM）及预言机驱动流动性基础设施方向。

传统 AMM 主要依赖池内资产比例定价，外部市场价格变化后，需要套利交易推动价格重新平衡。

Metric 则把定价与流动性分离，每个池子由独立 Price Provider 提供买价、卖价和参考价格，可以接入 Chainlink、Pyth 或做市商自己的报价系统。

它最有价值的设计是 Percentage Bins：LP 的资金按照参考价格周围的百分比区间分布，参考价格更新时，流动性区间同步移动，无需依赖套利交易才能调整定价。

池子既可以公开接受 LP 资金，也可以由专业做市商运行私人池，还支持 Anchored Pricing，把报价锚定独立预言机以约束定价风险。

这套机制尤其适合代币化股票、黄金、外汇等具有外部定价基准的 RWA，因为这些资产需要紧贴真实市场报价，而不是让链上池子自己发现价格。

截至 10 月 17 日，Metric 官网累计交易量约 241 亿美元，DefiLlama 统计的近 30 天 DEX 交易量约 40.27 亿美元，24 小时约 2.94 亿美元，而 TVL 仅约 836 万美元。

项目目前公开上线 Ethereum、BNB Chain 和 Robinhood Chain，流动性通过 0x、1inch、CoW Swap 等聚合器触达交易需求，核心合约经过 Zellic 与 Sherlock 安全审计。

Metric 的商业逻辑是让 LP 和做市商依靠报价点差获取收益，通过较少的流动性承接更多交易。

风险集中在 Price Provider 的可信度、报价更新延迟、极端波动时的逆向选择，以及 LP 资金被更专业交易者持续成交的不利价格。

2. Forever：想让协议在创始人离开后继续赚钱、进化

Forever 自称 The First Immortal Protocol，最初是围绕 MOG、PEPE、Milady、Remilio、CULT 等文化资产展开的投资实验，现在升级成一个更大胆的方向：

利用经济激励，让人类、AI Agents 和协议本身形成自主协作的经济网络。它希望协议能够持续创造价值、自主治理和迭代，即使创始人退出，系统也不会因为失去管理者而停止运转。

创始人曾参与 Camelot、Cypher 等 DeFi 流动性基础设施项目，有实际协议建设经验。

Forever 的核心思想：过去的 DAO 尝试依靠用户治理，却经常受制于人类协调成本。

下一阶段希望让自主 Agent 直接参与经济决策，而且必须承担真实的经济后果。

这里最难的地方是如何设计可验证的激励与约束机制，防止 Agent 为了获取奖励而损害整个协议的长期价值。

目前 Forever 的官网已开放 Early Access 注册，但核心合约、治理机制、代币分配和收入模型尚未公开，官方明确表示尚无上线代币。

3. Nullmask：隐私协议（小黄人 @theunipcs  力推 ）

Nullmask 主打 Private VPN for Crypto，利用零知识证明构建隐私交易层。

用户可以沿用 MetaMask 等钱包，把 ETH 或支持的代币存入 Shielded Pool，在池内私密转账、兑换，再提取到其他地址。通过 Relayer 代发交易，降低公开地址之间的直接关联。

Ethereum、Base、BNB Chain、Robinhood Chain 已纳入其 EVM 部署范围，Solana 则主要承载 MASK 代币及相关奖励活动。

其创始人 Tomas Krnak 具有密码学和 ZK 技术背景，曾参与 Zcash 相关开发。

协议的直接收费很清楚：

Shield 存入收取 0.5%，Unshield 提款收取 0.5%，跨链 Bridge 另有 0.2% 协议费，私密转账和 Swap 不另外收取 Nullmask 协议手续费，但用户仍承担网络及执行成本。

MASK 已在 Solana 流通，具备 ZEC 持有者奖励和代币销毁机制，近期完全稀释估值约 4,000 万美元量级。

text:
Metric just came out of stealth and the timeline is doing what timelines do.
Been watching this one, and know the founder. Hats off @mick_metric 🫡

Active pools that separate pricing from liquidity: a Price Provider sets the bid/ask/reference from oracles (Pyth, Chainlink, custom logic), and the pool holds liquidity in percentage bins around that reference. When the external price moves, the ranges move with it. No more LPs constantly getting picked off because the pool itself is the stale oracle.

That’s the actual problem with almost every AMM for anything that already has a real market. Tokenized stocks, gold, majors, FX. The pool sits wrong until an arb corrects it, LPs fund the correction, spreads widen, and the whole thing becomes a tax on real flow. Metric’s approach is the opposite: quote to reality, keep capital where the market actually is, and let the reference do the heavy lifting. Capital turnover numbers in stealth were absurd for the TVL.

Live on Ethereum, BNB, and Robinhood Chain, and later 👀. Aggregators were already routing to them quietly. Now it’s open: trade, LP, or deploy your own pool. Audited (Zellic, Sherlock). Team has real DeFi LP and protocol experience; one of them just left Uniswap after a few years. Excited to see how this works for DTCC assets.

A few thoughts here:

1. Most “RWA DEXs” still try to force real assets into AMM designs built for tokens that discover their own price. It doesn’t work once size and continuity matter.

2. Separating the price source from the liquidity inventory is the right primitive if you want professional market-making infrastructure to become permissionless.

3. The hard part is the freshness, oracle risk, weekend gaps on equities, and whether LPs actually get compensated for the residual risks (latency, inventory, feed integrity). This design fixes that.

4. If this holds up under real flow on tokenized stocks and majors, it becomes one of the few pieces of spot infrastructure that institutions can actually route through without the usual DeFi tax. That’s rarer than people want to admit.

5. Launch hype and airdrop farming will be loud for a week. The only thing that matters is whether the pools stay tight and capital-efficient once the early volume normalizes like Paper.

Been waiting for this for awhile. The interesting part is whether active pools become the default way anything with a real external price trades onchain. They could be a fundamental piece of market infrastructure moving forward.

Some people are claiming they’re the Morpho of AMMs.

author: AzFlin
quoted_text:
HOLY SHIT.

For crypto, this is one of the most insane posts of the year, but I'm guessing most people don't understand it.

Let me explain...

Bitcoin's accounts, and subsequently Ethereum's (and therefore every other EVM chain's), are built on a specific elliptic curve called secp256k1.

secp256k1 is a different elliptic curve from the one used across nearly every modern hardware device, including iPhones.

Modern devices mostly use a different curve called secp256r1, which is usually referred to as P-256 - one of the curves investigated in the article.

This mismatch has made it sooo difficult in the past to integrate crypto accounts natively into the security systems of modern hardware.

For example, Apple's Secure Enclave natively supports P-256, not secp256k1.

This has prevented crypto accounts from being able to use the same hardware protection as things like Apple Pay.

Same goes for the web with passkeys - WebAuthn uses P-256 signatures, which means Ethereum accounts using secp256k1 can't use them natively either.

But why did Satoshi do this?

The main theory for choosing secp256k1 was distrust of the P-256 curve - i.e. he thought there was an NSA backdoor.

A "backdoor" here basically means a secret, intentional weakness in the curve that would allow the NSA to exploit it and access private keys.

This was because P-256 was created with involvement from the NSA...

And the NSA provided a mysterious "seed" used to generate one of the curve's parameters without explaining where that seed came from.

This eventually transformed into a ~25-year-old mystery with a 5-figure reward for finding where this seed came from.

Claude figured it out in less than 30 mins. 

And the best part is its internal thinking was: "Hmm wait... is it suspicious that such an obvious thing wasn’t discovered in 25 years?"

The solution was stupidly simple - just the time the curve was created, put into a specific random number generator function.

This doesn't 100% prove there's no backdoor yet, but it provides strong evidence that this seed wasn't secretly engineered by the NSA.

And Claude did this with "just a simple prompt" in under 30 minutes.

Xuan 说的手续费问题我完全认同，但我的结论不太一样

预测市场在商业上是一个好模式，问题是币圈人之前赚钱来得太容易了

做合约 perps，有杠杆，量天然就大。做 meme 交易bot，频率高，手续费一笔接一笔。拿这两个当参照，预测市场确实显得性价比低：没有杠杆，交易量量跑不到合约的级别；也没有 meme 那么高频，手续费收不了那么多

所以现在做预测市场，更像是在做一件难而正确的事。短期很难看到成效，但一旦做起来，后来者想追上会非常难

难在哪：
1️⃣做市商要一家一家谈、一家一家接
2️⃣用户渠道要一点点铺
3️⃣盘口有了 maker，还得想办法吸引更多 taker
4️⃣营销和交易活动要专门为预测市场设计，照搬合约和 meme 那一套行不通
5️⃣交易系统和流动性激励机制非常复杂

我们团队这大半年在 @Predictdotfun 每天做的就是这几件事。每一项都要时间去磨，没做过的人很难想象里面的难度

虽然跑到上海没参与上活动，顺带连晚宴也取消了（没混上饭)，但我很大程度上理解为啥会临时发生变动，毕竟这是在对加密货币政策上极度敏感，数次多部委发文联手重锤的国家金融重镇，大张旗鼓的搞事。

跟知情的小伙伴聊了一下，其实活动筹备了小一年，连办公室都租好了，怎么可能像一些人嘲讽的一样没跟相关部门报备，真当那么大个团队都是纯老外一点不懂规矩？🤣🤣🤣

何况这已经是Solana在中国尝试搞活动的第三年了（去年在北京的活动也是我报了一下结果引发传统媒体关注导致赶紧删帖熄火😂😂😂） ，吃一堑肯定要长一智的。

今年他们还聘请了专门的GR（Government Relationship）来协助，会议相当多的敏感词都不能提了，只是集中在区块链技术本身上，就是为了尽可能的规避风险。

但只能说中国的体制特殊，除了现官还有现管，除了地方还有上级，跟一个部门报备好了不意味着别的部门不能来掺一脚管一管。 任何一家说不让那就弄不成，你还能指望别家站出来帮你撑腰说非办不可？在当前的中国政治生态里这不现实。

在国内做过实体生意的大概应该能理解我的意思，消防税务卫生街道个个都是爷，更何况Solana搞的还是Crypto这个敏感行业的破冰首家。

而且前天的外滩大广告过于高调，引发的曝光超过了预期，形成了国内外社媒的大量传播，这种舆论压力也有很大可能导致了预料之外的额外力量干涉。

我个人其实是很钦佩 @calilyliu 为首的 Solana foundation @SolanaFndn  的勇气和毅力的，如此锲而不舍的试图在中国内地打开口子，Solana应该是我看到的唯一一家。

大部分项目团队能做到国内城市小规模搞个饭局，跟社区见见面已经很不错了。

但Solana 是真的想要把Blockchain技术带进国内主流视野，想把在美国已经如火如荼的Tradifi在国内也打通，难度之大可想而知。

不过换个角度考虑，如果真的万一被他们打通了，搞成了，回报必然极为丰厚。

比如改革开放初期的德国大众，1978年就开始跟中国谈合作，直到1984年才签下上海大众的合资协议，前后磨了六年。中间最初的大规模建厂方案走不通，还得调整路径，从组装和逐步扩大生产做起。

后来回报有多大？仅2015年一年，中国合资企业按大众持股比例计算的经营利润就有约52亿欧元。

所以先进去的人，承担的是探路的成本，也有机会吃到市场打开之后的长期红利。当然，前提是这扇门最后真的打开了。

最后在嘉里中心楼下吃了一顿pizaa滚蛋了，听说还有小伙伴从新加坡飞过来参加活动的，比我还远，心理平衡多了，哈哈。

预祝 @solana  后续几站能顺利吧

text:
Claude Code 团队公开了他们审代码的做法：代码大约九成由 Claude 写，六月到九月合并的修改翻了一倍多，需要撤回的比例反而降了四成多。

这期用一摞带洞的奶酪片讲这套做法：每道检查都会漏，叠起来就很难漏，底下还有一张网兜底。

片中回答五个问题：哪些修改还要人看，AI 审 AI 会不会没完，审查的 AI 漏了怎么办，人不读代码怎么懂代码，出了事算谁的。人不再逐行读代码，时间花在机器做不好的判断上。

text:
--- 文稿 ---

Claude Code 团队的九成代码都是 AI 写的，他们是怎么审查代码的？

如果 AI 替你写作业，一天写一千份，老师批得过来吗？写代码的公司，现在就碰上了这件事。

Claude Code 是 Anthropic 做的编程助手。它自己的代码，大约九成是 Claude 写的。Anthropic 全公司的代码库，九月份一天要合并三万多次修改（五月份还是每天 2500 次左右）。靠人一行一行看，根本看不过来。

可 Claude Code 团队说，从六月到九月，他们合并的修改翻了一倍多，需要撤回的比例反而降了四成多。看的人少了，错反而少了。这是怎么做到的？

【什么是代码审查】

先说程序员平时怎么防出错。改完代码，不能直接放进产品，要先交一份修改申请，英文叫 PR（Pull Request）。同事一行一行看，挑毛病，点了头才能合并。这叫代码审查。

就像作文交上去，老师批过，才能贴上墙。

合并以后才发现出了问题，就得把修改撤回来。撤回得越多，说明漏掉的错越多。

【一摞带洞的奶酪】

Claude Code 团队觉得，“有没有人读过代码”，这个问题问得太粗。更该问的是：这一次修改可能出什么错？哪一道检查最适合拦住它？

可以把每一道检查想成一片带洞的奶酪。每一片都能挡住一些错，也都有洞，会漏掉一些。好几片叠起来，洞很难对齐，错误就很难一路穿过去。最底下再铺一张网，真漏下去了，也能很快捞回来。

这一摞奶酪里，大部分片是机器。人的时间最珍贵，它花在两头：一头是审代码，一头是出了事去救火。只省前一头，救火的时间涨上去，等于没省。所以他们盯着两个数：人花了多少时间，撤回和事故有没有变多。

【跟着一次修改走一遍】

从作者的电脑到用户手里，一次修改走的是一条流水线。前面那几片奶酪，就排在这条线上。

上流水线之前：自己先验。 代码还在自己电脑上，没有提交。Claude 写完代码，要自己跑测试、编译、做代码规范检查，把结果摆出来。光说一句“做好了”，不算数。然后再派一个新的 Claude，它没看过刚才的过程，单独审一遍，就像写完作文请一个没看过的同学挑错。

一提交，就上了流水线。 这条自动化的流水线英文叫 CI（持续集成）。从这以后，每提交一次新改动，机器都会自动从头查一遍，不用谁去点。线上依次是：

- 自动检查： 代码规范、类型、在各个系统上跑测试，再编译、打包。红了一项，就不能合并。
- AI 审查： 好几个 AI 同时找问题，再由另一组 AI 投票，票数够了才算真问题，按严重程度排好贴出来。每一条意见都得回应：要么改掉，要么写清理由关掉。它刚在内部上线时，一百份申请里收到实质意见的，从 16 份涨到了 54 份。
- 安全审查： 单独再查一遍。两种审查里只要还有一条没处理，申请就合并不了。
- 按风险批准： 要不要人看、要几个人看，由一个分类器按风险来定，下面单独讲。

合并：排队，再查一遍。 申请先排进一个队列，轮到它时，拿最新的代码，把它放进去，所有检查再跑一遍。因为两份各自没问题的修改，凑在一起也可能出错。

合并以后： 打包、发布也由流水线自动来做，这后半段英文叫 CD（持续交付）。新功能也不马上给所有人用，先藏在开关后面。这个开关英文叫 feature flag（功能开关）：新代码已经装进了产品，开关关着，用户就碰不到它；开关是一项设置，打开关上都不用改代码，也不用重新发版。打开以后，先给 Anthropic 自己的员工用，再分批发：先发到最新版，稳定版晚一步跟上。就算有问题，碰到的也只是一小部分人。

最底下那张网：盯着，随时撤回。 发出去以后，作者和值班的人一直盯着。新功能出了问题，把开关一关，用户那边马上就看不到它了；哪个版本整个坏了，就撤回，退到上一个好的版本；问题小、看得清，也可以直接修好再发。

撤回为什么快？一是每次修改都切得小，撤的时候只退这一小块。二是撤回本身也是一次修改，走的还是这同一条流水线，检查、打包、发布全是机器在跑。所以大多数问题，几分钟就能撤掉。网铺得牢，上面的奶酪片才敢少让人看几眼。

【哪些修改还要人看？】

看风险。

- 改文档、改文案、藏在开关后面的新功能，风险低。自动审查和安全检查都通过，就不用人批。
- 普通的产品改动，或者碰到自动更新这类敏感地方的，要一个人批。
- 风险最高的代码，要两个人批。

档位由修改本身定，跟谁写的无关：一个分类器读完修改，给它定档。

还有两条规矩：AI 的批准，不算人的批准；谁让 AI 写的代码，谁就算一个审查人，要为它负责。

放回奶酪里看：风险越高，人这一片切得越厚。

【AI 审 AI，会不会没完没了？】

真发生过。有一份申请，一夜之间审了改、改了审，五十多轮，直到作者出手叫停。

他们一查，审查反复指出的问题，约 59% 是第一轮就已经在那儿的老代码。人看到一条鸡毛蒜皮的意见，几秒就跳过了；AI 却会老老实实去改，于是又多一轮审查。

后来他们定了规则：

1. 最多审三轮。
2. 三轮之后，请作者退一步，想想思路对不对。
3. 过了头几轮，只审新改的部分。

结果，一轮就通过的申请，从 65% 涨到了 78%；要五轮以上的，从 8.9% 降到了 1.5%。

【审查的 AI 漏了怎么办？】

他们把过去闯过祸的修改都收集起来，请熟悉那块代码的工程师，标出错在哪一行。这就成了一本错题本，审查的 AI 每天做一遍。

改提示词、换模型，分数涨了才留下，没涨就扔掉。每出一次事故，错题本就多一道题。

审查反复挑出同一个毛病，就去源头改：写进给 AI 看的说明文件，或者加一条自动检查，下次就不用再提醒。奶酪片上的洞，就这样一个个补上。

【人不读代码了，还怎么懂代码？】

代码审查还有一件事：让团队里的人都懂代码。机器读了大部分，人怎么学？

团队里没有人把全部代码装在脑子里，他们也觉得没必要。想弄懂哪一块，就让 Claude 专门为那一块写一份讲解，几分钟就好，讲的就是代码现在的样子。

一行改文案的修改，逐行看也学不到什么。马上要动的那块代码，有一份讲解，能学到很多。

【出了事算谁的？】

团队的规矩是：你合并的，你负责。中小改动出了问题，通常由合并的人自己修。

这里的“负责”，不等于追究个人责任。让合并的人来修，是因为这次修改这个人最熟，修得最快。

事后复盘，不问是谁犯的错，只问一件事：这只虫，本该被哪一片奶酪拦住？找到那一片，再把那个洞补上。下次同样的错，就溜不过去了。

我的理解是，出了错不挨批，大家就不用藏着掖着，问题能更早摆到台面上。

敢这样做，还因为出错的代价被压得很小。修改切得小，好查也好撤；大多数错误，几分钟就能撤掉。

而且责任是大家一起担的。团队大多在公开频道里干活，谁都看得到别人在做什么，可以顺手接一把，也可以派一个 Agent 去补漏。

【你能用上什么】

你要是也在用 AI 写代码，有两件事现在就能做：

1. 给 AI 一份简短的说明（比如 `CLAUDE.md`），写清楚怎么跑测试、有哪些规则。
2. 交代码之前，在 Claude Code 里跑一下 `/code-review`。

这些数字都是他们自己公布的，也只是一个团队的做法。

【回到开头】

一天几万份作业，靠人一份份批，批不过来。他们叠了一摞奶酪片：每一片都会漏，叠起来就很难漏，底下还有网接着。

人不再逐行读代码，去做机器做不好的事：该不该做，危险的代码，架构，看懂证据，为结果负责。

他们的一位同事说，放慢速度确实能少出错，可那主要是因为你什么都做得少了。他们宁可更快地发现问题，更快地修好。

---

资料来源：
- Addy Osmani《How the Claude Code team does code review》（2026.10.15）https://t.co/yg4otshPe6
- Anthropic《Redesigning source control at Anthropic》（2026.10）https://t.co/XAdWVi4gWe

3 things that stood out to me from @Stacks's Q3 report:

1️⃣ More $STX is being staked

The total amount of $STX locked in staking increased from 392 million after PoX-5 to 493 million with October's Bond 2. That's around a 26% increase.

I think that's a great sign because holders are committing more $STX to staking, which helps provide capacity for more BTC staking.

Some of that growth may be existing holders restaking after the upgrade, but nevertheless, it's good to see it growing.

2️⃣ Bond 2 brought in 505 BTC (~$41.7M at a BTC price of ~$82.6K)

Holders committed that $BTC to earn staking rewards through Stacks.

What's interesting is that 483 BTC came through @StackingDao, roughly 96% of the total.

@xverse's Bond 2 pool also filled, so my guess is that some of the remaining BTC may have come through them too.

No confirmation of that, and the allocations may overlap, so that's just my speculation. But either way, Stacking DAO brought in almost all the BTC in this round.

And to me, that shows how important liquid staking is becoming as a way for BTC holders to access staking rewards and use their position in DeFi.

3️⃣ Zest reached $42M in borrows

This is another example of people using Stacks for more than just holding BTC.

Across the ecosystem, you can:

• Earn rewards on BTC through Bitcoin staking
• Borrow without selling BTC by using it as collateral in apps like Zest
• Keep using a staking position in DeFi through $stBTC

For example, you could hold $stBTC to earn staking rewards, then use it as collateral on @ZestProtocol to borrow without selling your position.

text:
Ethereum's ZK L2s in the Age of Quantum, Privacy and AI

Since the 1st of September, $ETH is down 1.4%.

Over the same stretch, $STRK is up 173%, $ZK 81% and $AZTEC 50%.

For a sector that mostly makes headlines with shutdowns these days, that's quite the outlier. Blast and Abstract are shutting down. Polygon switched off its own zkEVM sequencer on the 1st of July, Zero Network wound down over the summer, and Mint closes withdrawals on the 20th of October.

So what do Starknet, zkSync and Aztec have that most other L2s don't?

Exposure to the two narratives gaining the most steam right now: privacy and quantum, with AI accelerating both.

What makes it interesting is that all three are ZK rollups from the same tech family, yet they're heading in very different directions:

- @Starknet is going all in on quantum resistance, to the point of asking its stakers whether it should leave Ethereum, while adding compliant privacy to a public chain.

- @zksync is focused on institutions, building private chains for banks, and stays fairly quiet on quantum dates so far.

- @aztecnetwork has the most ambitious privacy of the three and the most conservative published quantum plan, with a full migration targeted for the end of 2030.

Quick context if you missed the last two weeks:

On the 7th of October, @drakefjustin warned that AI-driven math might break the signatures securing our wallets before a quantum computer ever does, "in the worst case in months not years". While most cryptographers pushed back, the debate fueled the attention the AI & quantum threat vectors get, and accelerated the corresponding narratives.

Partly because the cost of a quantum attack keeps falling. In March, Google estimated a break of the curve behind Bitcoin and Ethereum keys at under 1,200 logical qubits. A public contest of AI coding agents (ECDSA(.)fail) halved that estimate within about two months. And on the 16th of October, @AnthropicAI showed Claude designing a circuit for the core step of that attack with 17x fewer gates, at the cost of only 12% more qubits.

No quantum hardware ran and nothing got broken yet tho.

However, the timelines everyone plans around just got significantly shorter.

For ZK L2s that boils down to two questions:

- Quantum: how much of your cryptography can you swap out, and who controls that swap?

- Privacy: who can see your data, today and in 2035?

And here's where it gets more nuanced and subtle: quantum risk is really three different risks:

- Proof forgery: a quantum computer fakes a validity proof. Only possible once that machine exists, and nothing that happened before is affected.

- Key theft: exposed public keys get cracked. Fixable with new signature schemes and a migration.

- Harvest now, decrypt later: someone stores encrypted data published today and decrypts it once the machine exists. This one works retroactively, so for anything private you put on chain, the clock is already running.

That third risk matters most here, because it’s the only one where today’s data is already exposed to a future quantum computer. And once you factor it in properly, the chain with the strongest quantum story isn’t automatically the one that best protects your data.

But let's dig into the deeper comparison:

1) @Starknet

- Proofs: hash-based end to end
- Privacy: STRK20, opt-in, live since June
- PQ Target: "first fully quantum-resistant network" by 2027

Starknet has the strongest proof story of the three. Its STARK proofs rely on nothing but hash functions, a Falcon-512 account already sent a mainnet tx for $0.027, and a phone signed a testnet tx with an ML-DSA key without needing a hard fork. Still, the team itself says Starknet isn't quantum-safe yet, since default accounts use elliptic-curve signatures and the chain depends on Ethereum's blobs for data. That dependency is what the current vote is about. It's non-binding and a yes only kicks off research, but 99.95% of votes so far are in favour. Where Starknet gets weaker is privacy. STRK20 stores encrypted notes on chain using elliptic curves, and every user's viewing key is encrypted to one master auditor key, held in an enclave by Financial Privacy Inc and backed by a 3 of 4 StarkWare/FPI multisig. For a regulator, that works as intended. For a future quantum computer, @l2beat rates it exposed: break the curve, derive the auditor key from its public key, and you're able to read everyone's onchain history. On top of that, Starknet's post-quantum signatures are lattice-based, the family @VitalikButerin flagged as the new risk area in the age of AI. Account abstraction means it can switch again if needed tho.

2) @zksync

- Proofs: hash-based inside, BN254 wrapper on Ethereum
- Privacy: Prividium, permissioned
- PQ Target: no specific date

zkSync hasn't put a date on going post-quantum. Its focus right now is institutions. Prividium gives each one its own private chain, where the data stays in the bank's own infrastructure and only proofs get posted to Ethereum. As it happens, that design lines up well with the checklist Vitalik laid out on the 7th of October, and @gluk64 was quick to point it out two days later. Since nothing encrypted ever gets published, there is nothing to harvest, which makes it the cleanest answer to harvest now, decrypt later of the three. The tradeoff is who you're private from: the public, yes, the operator, no. It's basically a private database with public proofs of correctness, which is exactly what a bank wants. The other gap is the wrapper. zkSync's big hash-based proof gets compressed into a small one so Ethereum can verify it cheaply, and that small proof relies on BN254 elliptic-curve pairings, the part a quantum computer breaks. That's where Airbender Prime comes in. Launched on the 13th of October, zkSync's new prover proved 99% of 7,200 consecutive mainnet blocks in under 10 seconds on a single RTX PRO 6000 GPU, a.k.a. real-time proving of Ethereum on hardware that fits under a desk (zkSync's own benchmark tho, not independently replicated yet). Vitalik congratulated the team two days later and called the battle for speed "definitively won". Prime also comes with a Keccak path for verifying proofs on Ethereum, which would remove the BN254 wrapper, but that part is announced rather than shipped, with no specific date attached yet.

3) @aztecnetwork

- Proofs: pairing-based, generated on your device
- Privacy: private by default, programmable
- PQ Target: full post-quantum migration by end of 2030

Aztec is the only one of the three running private smart contracts on a public network, with proofs generated on your own laptop or phone (2.5 seconds for a private transfer on a laptop on V5). That same design is why it's the slowest on quantum. Its prover has to run on a phone, recurse quickly and keep proofs small, and according to Aztec no post-quantum proof system manages all three today, with the fast ones producing proofs of around 300KB. So the plan is to pick first and migrate later: a signature scheme by March 2027, encryption by July 2027, the proving system by November 2027, and a full migration by the end of 2030. On harvest now, decrypt later, it comes down to the app. Keys are hashed and notes can be delivered offchain, but an app that posts EC-encrypted notes on chain is still exposed (L2BEAT flags zk(.)money for exactly that). @Zac_Aztec argues that rushed cryptography and implementation bugs are the bigger risk right now, and Aztec has a case in point: its own AI audit harness caught a critical soundness bug in V5 that months of human audits had missed.

Put side by side, the chain with the best proofs right now has the weakest privacy story against a quantum adversary. The institutional chain has the cleanest one. And for Aztec, it depends on what each app decides to publish.

Where does AI come in?

So far, mostly on the attack side, and mainly in three ways:

- It makes quantum attacks cheaper: ECDSA(.)fail matched Google's estimate within 8 hours and beat it in about 3 days, and Claude's 17x gate reduction came out of a single 53-hour run.

- It finds cracks in structured math: Claude cut the cost of recovering a key for HAWK, a lattice-based signature scheme, from 2^64 to 2^38 operations, and NIST withdrew it.

- It finds the bugs humans miss, as Aztec's V5 showed.

To keep it in perspective tho: no AI-assisted break of ECDSA has been published, and Drake's "months not years" was a worst case scenario voiced as a personal opinion.

The defences all three are converging on look similar: hash-based cryptography wherever possible, formal verification, and crypto agility, a.k.a. being able to swap your signature scheme without forking the chain or changing anyone's address.

It's also where Vitalik says the focus has to go on the zkEVM front now that speed is solved: formally verifying that a zkEVM actually matches the Ethereum spec, a hard cap on prover cost relative to the gas in a block, and the security of the proof system itself. With AI getting this good at finding bugs, that list matters more than yet another speed benchmark.

The market's reaction to the recent moves/announcements by these three players and their above-outlined approaches was remarkably positive:

At its peak on the 12th of October, STRK was trading at more than 4.7x its price from the 1st of September, on $741M of daily volume. ZK added another 23% and AZTEC 20% since Drake's warning on the 7th of October, while ETH lost 10% over the same days.

Since then, STRK has given back 42% from that peak tho, and part of the pressure sits in the supply schedule. Around 127M STRK unlocked on the 15th, roughly 1.7% of circulating supply, landing on the same day the L1 vote opened. ZK's monthly unlock of roughly 173M, about 1.6% of circulating supply, lands today as well. And for AZTEC, the genesis sequencer unlock follows on the 13th of November, with team and investor cliffs in February 2027.

So the narrative got priced on attention and hype within weeks, while the actual migrations run on timelines measured in years and supply dynamics at play that you should always keep in mind too.

My take:

None of the three is quantum-safe today, and all three admit to that. Narrative-wise, with a potential move to a fully quantum-resistant L1, or generally if you care about proofs, Starknet is clearly ahead.

If you care about privacy that still holds up in 2035 tho, the institutionally-focused approach of publishing nothing (zkSync) or keeping notes offchain (an option on Aztec) beats encrypting the data fully onchain.

But in conclusion, it's definitely worth keeping all three on your radar for now imo.

What I'm watching next here (aside from the charts kek)?

@gluk64's Money20/20 keynote on the 21st of October (teased as "Who's in control?"), the Starknet vote result on the 22nd re L1 migration, the Aztec V6 vote, and zkSync's Airbender Prime Keccak verifier actually going live.

NFA tho. DYOR.

we obviously don't need to understand everything about how LLMs work to safely deploy them (and this probably isn't practically possible), but having additional evidence from mech interp is valuable especially when all other forms of monitoring are becoming less and less useful

the issue i have with this post is that it's comparing LLMs to humans. that is like comparing a hydrogen bomb to a coughing baby, because it's ignoring the scale of the intelligence and deployment

so here's a little story:
imagine taking a convicted felon from another planet, who doesn't really understand what being human means, then making him superhuman in math and coding and expert level in most other domains, giving him 10x human thinking and interaction speed, and then releasing him

of course, first you put him through multiple psychological evaluations and he passes 99% of the test scenarios.
that's good right?

well, you also know that he's way smarter than you and that he's perfectly capable of deceiving you and the tests, and that when he's exposed to certain situations will commit crimes

whatever.
let's release him anyway.

oh, but you don't just release him once. you first clone him 10 million times and then release him.

the best part: each clone gets access to someone's home, workplace or computer with access to private files, the local network and databases

now this will sound crazy to you. but maybe, just maybe, you would want some more proof that he is law abiding, friendly and reliable before making him even smarter, cloning him into a billion copies, making every copy 10x faster, and handing them even more access and control

text: 说这个不是让大家做项目的时候无脑选 Rust，而是要正视 Rust 的成本，考虑清楚项目的阶段以及长期性。可以用其他语言验证然后必要时用 Rust 重写😅
author: jolestar
quoted_text:
这次 Rust 大会的主题是 Rust and AI。而 Rust 常被人诟病的一点是编译废 CPU、产物废磁盘，AI 堆 Rust 代码的速度也明显慢于其他语言。

但反过来想，这个“缺点”在当下可能恰恰是一个特性：一个项目如果选择用 Rust 开发，至少说明作者和 AI 认真讨论过语言选型，并且做好了长期维护的心理准备——它是奔着建立长期关系去的，而不是 one night :)。如果只是想写个临时脚本或一次性工具，AI 绝不会推荐 Rust。在这个意义上，Rust 的高门槛和高成本，反而成了一种 PoW（工作量证明）。

当 AI 让代码生成成本趋近于零、开源软件产品出现无限供给时，用户和社区该如何筛选项目？最真实的观察指标只有持续维护。大家可以回头看看年初 vibe coding 最火时涌现出的海量开源项目，到现在还在更新、作者自己还在天天用的，还剩多少？我相信寥寥无几。

我自己的切身体会是：你需要一个工具，花半天让 AI 搓出来；当你开始天天用它时，接下来整整一周你都在修各种边界条件；如果你把工具分享给别人，考虑到不同的设备、运行环境、用户习惯，以及长期运行会不会撑爆内存和磁盘，至少还得再修上一个月。AI 极大降低了“写出代码”的成本，却丝毫没有降低“承担后果”的成本。

这也反向定义了 Rust 在 AI 时代的生态位：动态语言把原型成本降到极低，却把并发、内存与边界 bug 的暗税全部延后到运维期；而 Rust 则逼着作者在第一天就把系统契约和确定性锁死。在垃圾代码无限供给的时代，唯有维护的决心和编译期的确定性是有价值的。除非确实找不到替代品且自己极度依赖，否则真的划不来随便自己造轮子；而一旦决定自己做，且选了 Rust，那就意味着一场严肃的长期主义工程。

@VentureCoinist  和 @CryptoHayes 这场访谈信息量爆炸。

  从全球印钞、AI 泡沫、中国经济，一路聊到稳定币、AI Agent、BTC、ETH、HYPE 和 UNI。

🔴 宏观：全世界最终都得印钞

1. BTC 100 万美元：政府永远不愿主动承认债务损失，最后只能继续印钞。长期看，稀缺资产就是受益者。

2. 中国即将放水：Hayes 判断未来几个月中国可能大规模刺激经济。全球资金不能只盯美联储，中国可能成为下一轮流动性的关键变量。

3. AI 泡沫越大，BTC 越受益：AI 公司疯狂烧钱，一旦泡沫需要救助，新增流动性最终可能流向 BTC。

4. 稳定币是美国的金融武器：新兴市场居民抛售本币换美元，稳定币发行商拿储备买美债。美国获得融资，其他国家却可能失去货币控制权。

🔴 AI：模型公司可能一文不值

5.  OpenAI、Anthropic 不值得投资：Hayes 认为模型公司正在进行一场烧钱竞赛，股价上涨不代表商业模式成立。真正赚钱的是三星、SK 海力士这些卖硬件的。

6. AI Agent 将创造自己的经济体系：未来智能体可以自主工作、交易、支付和购买算力，甚至形成比人类经济更庞大的交易网络。

7.  AI 原生货币可能比 BTC 更值钱：Hayes 押注自己参与的 FLOP 项目，让 GPU 提供者通过推理服务赚取代币，Agent 直接用代币购买算力。他认为这类网络理论上可能超过 BTC 的价值，但目前仍是早期设想。

8. Agent 未必选择稳定币：USDC 等中心化稳定币存在冻结、审查风险。Hayes 认为，智能体更可能偏好能直接兑换算力的去中心化货币。

🔴 Crypto：99% 的山寨币可能没有未来

9. 只有 5～10 个币值得长期关注：高 FDV、低流通、VC 解锁砸盘的老套路已经失效。未来资金更愿意购买有真实收入、能回馈代币持有者的项目。

10. HYPE 好项目，不代表现在是好投资：Hyperliquid 已经证明了产品价值，但永续 DEX 竞争越来越激烈。市场共识太强，新增资金的赔率反而可能下降。

11. ZEC 与 ETH 怎么选：Zcash 弹性更大，但 Hayes 更愿意重仓 ETH。资金体量越大，越需要考虑流动性和极端下跌风险。

12. Saylor 时代正在结束：Strategy 不再是获得 BTC 敞口的唯一重要渠道。ETF 和其他金融产品越来越多，Saylor 的边际影响力正在下降。

13. 别指望央行疯狂买 BTC：Hayes 判断央行会优先选择黄金。BTC 的托管、安全和职业责任风险，对央行官员来说太大。

14. 量子风险被情绪放大：量子计算确实威胁现有密码体系，但市场经常根据 BTC 涨跌决定自己有多害怕量子攻击。

🔴 ETH、UNI 与 RWA：可能迎来重新定价

15. RWA 的最大赢家可能是金融机构：银行推动代币化，核心动力是节省中后台、清算和结算成本。如果金融业务大规模上链，基础设施将持续受益。

16. ETH 有机会涨到 2 万美元：这是 Hayes 在访谈中认可的激进目标。他认为 ETH 可能成为表现最好的大市值币，机构级安全性、DeFi 和代币化需求是核心理由。

他还特别看好 UNI 的机会：如果更多机构复制 Robinhood 的链上交易模式，Uniswap 可能成为重要执行基础设施。回购销毁机制则让 UNI 的价值捕获更值得关注。

整场访谈听下来，Hayes 的逻辑非常明确：

政府负责印钱，AI 负责制造新的经济需求，金融机构负责把资产搬上链。

但最后能留下来的，可能只有少数真正拥有收入、流动性和价值捕获能力的加密资产。

下一轮牛市即使来了，也未必是所有山寨币一起狂欢。

text:
wanted to share a bug we discovered on lighter and got them to fix it, shows a lot about what it means to be an HFT developer

01/ the setup

lighter nonces are per api key and strictly sequential: n+1 can't execute before n.

in our benches, gtc and ioc creates took 90-200ms from ack to execution. 

cancels and post-only took a few ms.

so a cancel signed behind a gtc on the same key has to wait for it.

02/ the bug

we place two orders and cancel both right after, on the same key. 

lighter says ok to all four, then rejects the second cancel as "invalid nonce" before the orders even reach the book, so one of them is "stale".

03/ why it hurts a market maker

order y is still on the book, and your system thinks it's cancelled.

the rejected nonce isn't consumed, so every tx already signed above it fails too.

and the ack said 200. 

the reject only shows up on the authenticated account stream.

04/ the workaround we can't use

wait for each tx to execute before sending the next: 3/3 clean.

it also turns a 1ms create->cancel gap into 0.7-1.6s. 

when you requote on every tick, that's not a workaround.

05/ what we run

quotes are post-only on their own key. 

they execute within 0.2ms of the ack, so nothing waits behind them.

a 200 means "received" but the actual status comes from the account stream.

it took us 3 versions: 
v1 counted the rejected nonce as used. 
v2 froze the key for 10s. 
v3 resumes at the refused nonce as soon as everything below it has executed

06/ s/o @Lighter_xyz 

we sent them the script pinned to the sdk version, its sha256, raw traces, a control run and every tx hash. 

reacted pretty fast and in a week it was fixed.

that's the kind of support you want from a venue you quote on.

text:
10月16日晚长鑫科技放出消息，2026年前三季度归母净利润高达1310亿元至1325亿元，上年同期还亏着52.8亿，一年翻面，平均下来每天净赚4.8亿，比数字更值得聊的是长鑫科技的来时路。

先看成绩单有多夸张，上海证券报算了一笔账，三个季度的利润接近贵州茅台2025年全年的1.6倍，逼近中国石油2025年全年的83%，按前三季度均值推算，全年有望突破1700亿。

再看它的起点，长鑫早期手里只有2009年破产的德国内存厂奇梦达留下的旧技术资料，落后行业整整十年，2019年靠这套底子做出了国产第一颗DDR4， 最先进的 EUV 光刻机买不到，出口管制一轮比一轮紧，制程没法像三星、海力士那样靠近前沿，长鑫的解法就是拼数量，多建产线、多投晶圆，一片一片地把产能堆上去。

打个老比方，这像拿着十年前的旧课本去考今年的高考，题型全变了，只能靠刷题量硬补，长鑫补的就是产能和良率。当年最被嘲讽的便宜内存，后来反倒成了它的底牌，谁也没想到2025年下半年AI算力会把DRAM推到供不应求，价格一涨，前些年咬牙扩出来的产能，就成为了这1310亿的来源。

说穿了，存储是最典型的周期生意，亏钱的年份能不能撑住扩产，决定了涨价的时候手里有多少筹码。当然也留个清醒，利润几乎全靠这一轮DRAM涨价，周期反转时数字会掉得一样快，毕竟流通股只占6.63%。更值得记住的是它的来时路，而不是去追一个已经涨上天并且已经深度回调的周期。

Leopold Aschenbrenner might genuinely be the unluckiest motherfucker alive.

After getting absolutely destroyed in July and being forced to liquidate much of his AI portfolio, he reportedly came back swinging in early September, buying hundreds of millions of dollars worth of options premium.

Look at how those stocks have performed since September 8:
$CRWV: -37.4%
$SKHY: -25.8%
$SNDK: -23.8%
$DRAM: -22.9%
$BE: -18.1%
$INTC: -9.4%
$AMD: +9.1%
Six out of seven are underwater, with an average decline of roughly 18.6%.

And remember, we're talking about someone who reportedly rebuilt exposure through leveraged options, not just common shares.

Imagine surviving a massive forced liquidation, watching your favorite stocks recover, deciding it's finally safe to get back in, and then getting hit by ANOTHER brutal selloff barely a month later.

The worst part about options is that you can be absolutely right about the long-term AI infrastructure thesis and still lose a fortune because your timing was wrong.

I genuinely feel for the guy.

The market has absolutely no mercy.

quoted_text:
Today is probably a good time to check in on things with @privy_io, which became part of @stripe just over a year ago.

Our acquisition was predicated on three factors: stablecoin growth, self-custody as a key enabler of broader global coverage, and rapidly increasing demand for programmable financial infrastructure. As we said at the time, "money has to reside somewhere, and Privy builds the world's best programmable vaults."

Since then, the Privy team has executed exceptionally well: assets in Privy wallets have grown ~25x, monthly active developers are up ~3x, revenue is up ~9x, and Privy now facilitates nearly $25B of monthly transaction volume. @tryramp, @Deel, @Klarna, @felixpago, @HyperliquidX, and thousands of other businesses are building embedded banking functionality on Privy.

At Stripe, we're deeply integrating Privy into Treasury, @Link, and Connect. In each case, it's accelerating our global expansion, and enabling us to build better functionality faster. (Coming soon: @Link balances.)

We're also seeing that Privy's wallet infrastructure is the ideal substrate for agents to transact and earn -- live today with @merit_systems, @orthogonal_sh, @Nevermined_ai, @prlnet, and more. Developers prefer programmable financial infrastructure, but agents need it. We expect that the agentic economy will continue to grow extremely quickly.

The Privy team has maintained remarkable product velocity, with major launches this year including deposit addresses, earning on Privy balances, digital asset accounts, custodial wallets, and Stripe's own stablecoin cards.

It's also been neat to see how Privy has been accelerated by Stripe, with better onramps, @stablecoin payment rails and licenses, Stripe's fiat capabilities and issuing stack, and integration with @Tempo.

Together, we're building one API for holding stablecoin balances and earning yield, moving money in and out of fiat, and orchestrating spend with cards. We still have a lot of work to do, not least in integrating everything across Privy, Bridge, and the rest of Stripe -- there's been so much feature and functionality expansion that we haven't yet had much time to reconcile everything. Overall, though, I'm very happy with how things are going, and excited by where these capabilities are headed.

If you're interested in working on the future of stablecoins, agentic payments, and crypto's deployment in the real world, you should get in touch with @sternhenri (now leading all of @StripeCrypto) or others on the team.

author: iamyourchaos
quoted_text:
Hyperliquid 生态，依旧大有可为。

1/ 第一个例子 - @hypurrdash
HyperDash 是第一个经典案例。

在很多人眼里，HyperDash 不过是 Hyperliquid 的一个数据分析网站。但很少有人注意到它的收入。
▌2026 年 Q2：协议收入 17 万美元
▌2026 年 Q3：协议收入 40 万美元
单看收入，这已经超过了很多 DeFi 协议。

它的路径也很清晰：
2024 年创立，作为 Hyperliquid 的独立分析仪表盘；
2025 年 11 月被 https://t.co/j488bpXdUE 收购，从分析平台向交易终端转型；
2026 年 7 月收购机构级数据公司 Imperator，成为 Hyperliquid 的活跃验证节点。

先用分析工具吸引用户，再培养粘性，最后提供交易能力、培养交易习惯。HyperDash 证明了，只要服务足够有用，用户和收入都是水到渠成的事。
Hyperdash 传送：https://t.co/QUUx8xL4ZZ

2/ 第二个例子 - @leveracc_xyz
和 HyperDash 不同，Lever/acc 更早期，10 月 12 日才正式对外公布，不到一周。
而且它一开始就把交易功能内嵌在产品里，没有走先工具后交易的老路。

它是什么？
Lever/acc 是 Hyperliquid 上的信用与结算协议，交易者用自有 USDC 作抵押，最多可借入 4 倍资金，也就是拿到 5 倍购买力去做永续合约。
我自己试了一把，充值 100 USDC，借出 400 USDC，开了一张 HYPE 多单，舔了 3% 涨幅就离场。整个过程轻松丝滑。
（如图）

问题来了：LeverAcc 为什么敢给更高杠杆？
关键在于，它的借款不是通用资金，而是绑定到 Hyperliquid 交易账户的专用信用。由此带来几层控制：
▌资金用途被锁定
借到的 USDC 会直接进入用户在 HyperCore 的交易账户，用户当然可以提现，但每次提现都会重新核算实时账户价值与未偿债务，只放行安全范围内的那部分。
▌实时健康监控 + 自动降风险
Aave 这类协议靠预言机 + 清算，LeverAcc 靠的是持续监控健康度 + 自动执行：
健康度 > 1.167 - 可以正常交易
健康度≤ 1.167 - 禁止加重仓位
健康度 ≤ 1.125 - 开始减仓
健康度 ≤ 1.05 - 减掉 65% 仓位
说人话就是，系统会实时盯着你的单子，并有权替你减仓。用户最多只能亏掉本金。
▌兜底设计
LeverAcc 还会在 Hyperliquid 上为每个借款仓位挂 reduce-only 止损单。就算 LeverAcc 服务宕机、RPC 拥堵、轮询没跟上，交易所本身也会按止损价平仓。

1/ CPI 和 PPI 过热，通胀反弹的恐慌重新回到主 stage，核心原因依然是石油导致的几项指标过热：汽、燃油、飞机船票的超预期

2/ 油价恶化，Trump 和俄罗斯合作，希望利用俄罗斯的柴油缓解价格焦虑，但是国会企图拟草案禁止，伊朗继续强势，短期内油价高企，依然无法破局

3/ 长鑫 4F² 技术突破，威胁三星、海力士、美光的地位，储存是否能涨价打个问号

4/ OpenAI ARR 搞乌龙，500 亿被报成 700 亿，而 Anthropic 周三在 NY 的 Pre-IPO 也再次杀预期，本来预期 year end 1000 亿，结果 Q3 只有 168 亿收入，推算年底顶多 800 亿，也是低于预期 200 亿，估值 2 万亿也站不住

text:
Google CEO 桑达尔·皮查伊在这段访谈里首次把谷歌当年的底牌亮了出来，原来早在 ChatGPT 引爆全球之前，Google 内部就已经捏着几乎一模一样的产品了，

但明明手里握着王炸底牌却硬生生憋在实验室里没发，

我觉得这段复盘撕开了所有大公司在做产品时最致命的软肋，也给正在做业务决策的人上了一堂极其昂贵的实战课。

他在访谈里还原了当时的真实时间线，Google 发明了 Transformer 架构之后，第一时间就把它塞进自家的搜索业务里去提升查询和网页理解，

内部团队顺势就做出了名为 LaMDA 的对话模型，甚至已经把后来 ChatGPT 的产品形态完完全全构想了出来。

如果还有印象的话，当年 Google 内部有个工程师公开宣称公司的 AI 已经产生了自我意识，闹得满城风雨，

皮查伊直接点破，当时把那个工程师聊到怀疑人生的内部系统，其实就是 Google 内部早期版本的 ChatGPT。

既然底牌早就捏在手里，为什么直到 2022 年的 Google I/O 大会上，他们也只敢把 LaMDA 包装成一个严格受限的测试产品 AI Test Kitchen 小心翼翼放出来，

核心卡点就出在安全护栏和质量洁癖上，当时他们内部还没有跑通端到端的 RLHF 人类反馈强化学习，皮查伊自己在后台看到的未阉割版充满毒性，按 Google 的标准根本不可能直接推向市场。

真正把 Google 按在替补席上的不是技术落后，而是他们引以为傲的搜索质量标准，

一家靠精准搜索起家的巨头，骨子里对产品交付有着极高的容错洁癖，而光脚的创业公司根本没有历史包袱，哪怕模型还会一本正经胡说八道，也敢直接端上牌桌让全球用户边用边改。

说白了，这给我们所有在公司里带团队、做新业务的人敲了一记闷棍，

当你用成熟业务的完美标准去审批一个颠覆性的新物种时，你以为自己是在对品牌和风险负责，实际上却是在亲手给没有包袱的对手让出整个时代的先发身位。  

不过看皮查伊这段复盘也得留个清醒，作为上市公司的掌门人，把错失首发窗口归因于对安全和产品质量要求更高，本就是最体面、最符合高管立场的危机公关解释，

除了安全顾虑，当年 Google 更难迈过去的坎其实是商业模式的左右手互搏，毕竟没人敢轻易放出一个会直接砸掉自家千亿搜索广告饭碗的新玩具。  

在旧时代让你立于不败之地的完美质量标准，往往就是新时代把你死死焊在原地的最重脚镣。 https://t.co/CR24cN35Un

text:
A Milk Road PRO member asked why I hold $NEAR when $SOL apps made $365M last quarter, more than any other chain

I hold both because they're doing different jobs

$SOL is the execution engine for human traders. $NEAR is building the controller layer for AI agents

Solana's numbers are real. Q3 was its 10th straight quarter leading every chain in app revenue, and in August its apps made $143M to Ethereum's $47M

Alpenglow goes live Oct 21 and cuts finality to about 150ms from about 12.8 seconds

When I had 21Shares' Eliezer Ndinga on @MilkRoadDaily, he said well over 90% of tokenized equities volume was on Solana as of their H1 report (my guess is that's SOL's next big value driver)

Now to how SOL captures value. 100% of priority fees go to validators, and the base fee burn is about 700 SOL a day against about 66,500 SOL issued, per Blockworks Research

That's why August's validator vote matters. 67% approved doubling SOL's disinflation rate, so once it activates, inflation hits its 1.5% floor in 2029 instead of 2032

Where Solana hasn't won yet is deep capital. Its DeFi TVL is $6.0B, Base has passed it at $6.2B, and Ethereum holds $50.1B (DefiLlama)

For context, ETH + Base TVL is $56B, almost SOL's entire $62.5B market cap.

To me, when it comes to competing on trading fees and volume, the best comparison for $SOL is $HYPE. But that's another story.

NEAR is built for a different customer entirely:

- $SOL runs one fast global state for traders
- $NEAR gives agents sharded state, private compute and one account that signs on 35+ chains

1. Nightshade sharding: state splits across shards, so agent traffic adds shards instead of heavier validator hardware

2. TEEs: agents can run private inference and confidential transactions. NEAR's own dashboard shows Confidential Intents TVL at $155.7M, up 365% in 90 days

3. Intents + Chain Signatures: one NEAR account signs and settles on other chains, w/ $33B+ in all-time volume and $4.8B in the last 30 days (TokenPost, DefiLlama). This is where NEAR found product-market fit IMO

NEAR captures value differently. Since February, Intents revenue buys NEAR on the open market, $3.07M in Q3 vs $1.5M in Q2 (DefiLlama)

Inflation was halved to 2.5% in Oct 2025, and in July governance voted to burn 100% of gas fees, up from 70%

Those buybacks are still small next to a $6.8B market cap, so I'm watching the trend. They doubled in a quarter, and monthly Intents volume is up 896% YoY

When I had Bitwise's Matt Hougan and Ryan Rasmussen on @MilkRoadDaily, their base case was $155 per NEAR by 2030, about 30x from $5.22, w/ a bull case above $500. As Matt put it, "It's like a moonshot for free"

$SOL is about 9x the size of $NEAR by market cap. If you think agents end up moving real money across chains (which I do), NEAR is the smaller bet w/ the bigger multiple

I'm not bearish on Solana, and more Solana episodes are coming on @MilkRoadDaily. I think both chains have plenty of room to win

Full disclosure: $NEAR and $SOL are positions in my Milk Road PRO portfolio. Our PRO team was early to $UNI (+54.8%), $AERO (+93.7%), and $SKY (+42.6%)

Try Milk Road PRO for $1 for 7 days, link in bio: @BitcoinJesusETH

text:
Tom Lee：加密、芯片、AI 云计算股，可能都到了值得关注的位置

@fundstrat 联合创始人、@BitMNR 董事长 Tom Lee 最新表示，如果基本面保持稳定，加密货币、芯片股以及 Neocloud（新型云计算）公司，都可能迎来「一触即发」的反弹机会。

这番判断并非没有背景：近期半导体板块持续回调，AI 云计算公司也受到高负债、融资成本上升和 AI 投资回报担忧的冲击。市场正在重新定价 AI 交易的风险。

但 Tom Lee 的逻辑是：如果基本面没有同步恶化，那么市场恐慌造成的下跌，反而可能提供更好的风险回报比。

值得关注的还有 BitMine 本身。截至 8 月 23 日，公司持有约 584.76 万枚 ETH，占 ETH 总供应量约 4.8%，持续押注以太坊的长期价值。

当然，回调至支撑位不等于底部已经确认。 对加密市场而言，宏观流动性、利率预期和风险偏好仍是关键变量；对 AI 产业而言，需求能否转化为真实收入与现金流同样重要。

接下来真正值得观察的是：基本面能否扛住抛售，以及资金何时重新回流。

如果这两个条件成立，恐慌可能就是机会；反之，所谓支撑位也可能继续失守。
