text:
AI spends hundreds of billions on GPUs that mostly multiply matrices. Bitcoin spends its entire security budget on hashes nobody can reuse.

@prlnet makes them the same computation, and could become the Bitcoin of the AI age.

Finally longed pearl-2:native in the recent (smol) dip via @entropyIO on Hyperliquid.

Here's why ↓

Proof of useful work has been an open problem since Bitcoin launched.

A key challenge is that in a permissionless chain, the miner picks its own inputs. Say the work is "multiply two matrices." A cheater just submits all-zero matrices, does no real compute, and farms tickets for free.

So earlier designs mostly had two bad options: let someone else choose the inputs (not permissionless, and miners can't bring their own AI jobs), or pick some niche task nobody actually needs (e.g. Primecoin hunting prime chains).

The breakthrough?

Komargodski and Weinstein (Pearl's founders) published a PoUW mechanism for arbitrary matrix multiplication with 1+o(1) overhead in April 2025:

- Miner commits to A and B, the chain seeds low-rank noise into both
- The GPU runs its normal kernel on the noised operands
- Every output tile doubles as a lottery ticket, hashed against the difficulty target
- A winning tile gets a Plonky2 zkSNARK that nodes verify cheaply
- The noise is low-rank, so the miner strips it and keeps A·B at FP8-level accuracy

One forward pass, two outputs: the AI result and a shot at the block.

Why can't miners cheat?

The noise is seeded by the chain itself, so nothing can be precomputed, and a jackpot policy rejects "easy" crafted inputs. The only way to get a ticket is to actually run the full multiplication.

And the team keeps pushing it further.

The September whitepaper:

- Moves mining to FP8, the low-precision format modern inference runs on across Nvidia's Hopper and Blackwell GPUs
- Extends it to mixture-of-experts models, the architecture behind most large open models today
- Uses Hawkeye, which replays the GPU's exact math on a normal CPU so anyone can check a proof bit for bit (co-authored by Dan Boneh, accepted at MLSys 2026)

"But if the work is useful, can't an attacker sell the output and attack for free?"

That's the classic objection, and Rafael Pass (Cornell Tech cryptographer, known for the first formal security proofs of Bitcoin's consensus) took it head on. 

His model shows that once the market adjusts, a majority attack still costs the full block reward, same as Bitcoin. What changes is where the reward ends up: instead of paying for wasted hashes, it subsidises inference. Same security, but cheaper tokens.

Everything else is plain Bitcoin: UTXO, longest chain, Taproot, a 2.1B hard cap and a smooth emission curve instead of halvings. Plus a post-quantum path, since the mining is hash-based and XMSS signatures are already in consensus.

So where's the demand?

Most people still point to the Together AI endpoint (Together is one of the biggest inference providers for open models), which was pulled from serverless on the 27th of August. 

The more interesting signal tho imo is that Pearl now runs its own inference platform: 7 open models behind an OpenAI-compatible API, served on GPU capacity across the Pearl network.

And it's cheaper. On all four models it shares with Together's serverless lineup (input / output per 1M tokens):

- DeepSeek V4 Pro: $1.10 / $3.30 on Pearl vs $1.32 / $3.96 on Together
- GLM-5.3: $1.10 / $3.50 vs $1.40 / $4.40
- GLM-5.3 Flash: $0.07 / $0.24 vs $0.15 / $0.50
- DeepSeek V4.1 Flash: $0.14 / $0.42 vs $0.30 / $1.20

Still worth keeping in mind tho that this is launch pricing, and Pearl doesn't say how much of the discount PRL is funding. But it's the direction the Pass model predicts: block rewards flowing back to users as cheaper inference.

Ok, cool but how and where does this thing trade?

At $1.70 and a ~$594M mcap, PRL is ~19% off its $2.10 ATH from the 14th of October rn.

Spot is basically two small CEXs, BigONE and SafeTrade, with ~$5M of combined daily volume. The books are paper thin: per CoinGecko it takes ~$4K of buys to push BigONE up 2%, and ~$9K on SafeTrade.

That's why the perp matters. @entropyIO listed PRL as a HIP-3 market on Hyperliquid on the 14th of Oct, and it's filling up fast:

- ~$3.05M OI, already 61% of Entropy's $5M OI cap for the market
- ~$2.05M daily volume, around 40% of all spot volume
- Funding averaged ~0.03-0.04% an hour over the last 3 days, longs paying
- Lighter runs a smaller PRL perp too, ~$0.56M OI

There is a catch tho:

Until a properly liquid venue lists PRL, io:PRL prices 90% off SafeTrade, so the perp inherits the spot book's fragility.

Why am I long?

Bc the hard part is (mostly) done. The math is public, the verification work is accepted at MLSys, the chain is live, and Pearl already sells inference cheaper than Together AI, one of the largest providers of open-model APIs, while awareness of what they're actually do still seems low across CT / my timeline.

What's missing tho is proof that paid demand actually runs through the mining. Until Pearl publishes the share of mining that serves paid workloads and unless there is real adoption, PRL will trade like a mining coin and has to absorb ~1M new PRL a day (float +87% over the next year), and two thin spot books. The trade is definitely not without risk.

That above gap is also the discount I see rn tho, and it's why I bought into this (still smol compared to recent run) dip. 

Bitcoin turned electricity into security. And if Pearl succeeds at turning GPU cycles into security and inference at the same time, it could indeed be smth like the "Bitcoin of the AI age", and with that, nothing short of huge.

NFA ofc tho. Always DYOR.

Once you have and want to trade pearl-2:native too, join me on Entropy (my ref link):

https://t.co/XHXh2dwzi2

text:
Time to share a bit more about @StacysBrain – my new product that (I hope) will enter the market over the next couple of weeks.

What will it be?
MVP = an open, graded database of marketing insights and benchmarks – each with its own sample, methodology, age, and vendor interest data.

I told you about the pain (and I’m sure you know it yourself): AI often relies on outdated numbers or just hallucinates, and lots of marketing articles have zero proof or research behind them.

It’s like a circle jerk where people cross-cite each other. But once you try to find who was the first one to say something, it turns out there’s no source at all.

In some fields it’s probably fine.

In marketing, it’s a huge problem, because we invest money based on decisions that are often backed by low-quality research (or no research at all).

So I see Stacy's Brain as the fix.

We’ve been building this for the last 3 months, and the database will have 500+ insight cards (checked and vetted by my team) at release.

Very excited tbh.
Stay tuned <3

author: PhyrexNi
quoted_text:
MSTR 盘中跌逾 8%，MSCI 指数资格开始影响融资预期

$MSTR 这次跌得明显比 bitcoin:native 多。截止到目前已经下跌超过 9%，同期 Bitcoin 也只跌了 1% 左右。两者差了约 8 个百分点，主要下跌的原因就是这次 MSCI 指数资格带来的。

MSCI 在 15 日美股收盘后宣布，将实施针对非经营性公司的新筛选规则，最终受影响名单会在 11月11日 公布，调整于 11月30日 收盘生效。这次的规则会检查公司的经营性资产和财务指标，判断公司是否更接近持有投资资产的工具。此前用 5 月数据做模拟时 Strategy 已经被列为潜在剔除对象。

Strategy 一直反对这套规则，认为自己把 Bitcoin 业务作为经营分部披露，也在主动进行融资和资本管理。但 MSCI 还是决定实施，接下来就要看 Strategy 是否出现在最终名单里。

按照 Strategy 此前的披露，跟踪相关 MSCI 指数的基金大约持有 1,300 万股 MSTR，占当时基本股本的 3.1%。用这次 138 美元的盘中价格粗算，这批股票价值约 18 亿美元。如果最终被剔除，相关基金就需要按新指数调整仓位，即便基金经理仍然看好 BTC，也得处理不再符合指数要求的 MSTR。

总的来说，11月11日 最终名单公布后，如果 MSTR 被剔除，就会有基金经历在规则的情况下不得不去减仓 MSTR 的股份，所以现在已经开始有投资者离场了。才造成了差价的拉大。

text:
Metric just went public, and it’s already doing ~20% of Robinhood stock-token DEX volume today, with close to $2M of liquidity sitting in its pools.

Metric isn’t a traditional AMM. It’s the infra layer for active AMMs, PropAMMs included. Easiest mental model: the Morpho of DEXs. Here is how it's structured:

1️⃣ Public or private pool?
🔹 Public: join as an LP, or run the pool as a curator. Carcosa is the largest verified curator right now
🔹 Private: usually a market maker trading its own capital. Pair it with your own pricing logic and you’ve got a PropAMM

2️⃣ How does the pool price?
🔹 Oracles like Chainlink or Pyth
🔹 Your own proprietary price logic

The big LP pain point has always been re-adjusting your range every time price moves. Metric removes that. You set your liquidity bin once and it follows the reference price.

3️⃣ Plug in up to 7 extensions per pool (think Uniswap v4 hooks)
🔹 Deposit allowlist
🔹 Trading-hours limits
🔹 Points system
🔹 Priority fee cap
🔹 Velocity Guard against oracle manipulation
🔹 Stop Loss to cap LVR losses

Each one is another lever for LP protection and profitability.

4️⃣ Set the economics. There are 3 fees
🔹 Half-spread fees, split between LPs, the curator and Metric
🔹 Bin fees, split the same way
🔹 Notional fees, off by default, paid to Metric

LPs never claim anything. Fees compound straight into your position.

There’s a lot more under the hood. If people want it, I’ll do a deeper teardown in a future article.

最可能被破解的是ECDSA

全称：Elliptic Curve Digital Signature Algorithm
中文正式名称：椭圆曲线数字签名算法

不是sha256

sha256被破解才是全球密码学的灾难但是这个可能性远远低于ecdsa被优化

text:
Why are these new privacy primitives essential? Going forward, AI inference will only play a more and more integral part of daily life. Once that regular dependence on a technology sets in, access becomes essential. A free society cannot persist when intermediaries retain the threats of censorship and surveillance. It is naive to assume their prolonged benevolence.

But even with responsible gatekeepers, AI hacks have already shown non-privacy to be untenable. It's not about trusting model providers not to read or sell identity-linked data, but the indefinite lingering question "How safe is that data?" Improving the security of those systems is not enough. We would rather exit the AI-cybersecurity arms race than trust a frontier paced on our behalf. This is the end goal of all efforts in private communications—don't create in the first place a digital footprint that can be held against you. This is why privacy must be a default primitive. And that is why the EF will continue collaborations like this one with @OpenAnonProject to further our mandate.

Thanks @l2beat for the shout

text:
为什么我比较相信台积电对AI需求的判断？

因为这家公司经历过的半导体危机，实在太多了。

2001年互联网泡沫破裂，台积电第三季度产能利用率一度跌到41%。

2008年金融海啸，资本支出同比减少26%。

2023年半导体库存调整，资本支出又从363亿美元降到304亿美元。

但即使在行业低谷，台积电也没有停止先进制程的研发和升级。

经历了这么多轮周期，它应该比谁都清楚产能过剩的代价。

所以，当台积电计划2026年投入600–640亿美元，而且预计2026–2028年的资本支出还将显著高于过去三年时，我觉得这个信号值得认真研究。

不知道大家有没有注意到魏哲家10月15日法说会上的一段话？

台积电不只向客户了解需求，还会找客户的客户核实，甚至派自己的团队去美国，实地了解数据中心建设进度和电力供应。

云厂商的资本支出、融资能力，以及其他关键零组件的供应情况，也都是它评估需求的重要依据。

我觉得台积电还有一个经常被低估的能力，就是它多年积累的产业情报和需求分析体系。

从芯片设计、客户产品规划，到先进制程导入和未来量产安排，它掌握的产业信息，可能比大多数外部研究机构都要完整。

而且，这些信息还可以交叉验证。

以前做过多年供应链跟电子制造，我很清楚客户的Forecast和真正落地的订单是两回事。

尤其是半导体这种重资产行业，设备买回来、厂房建起来，客户就算推迟订单，折旧也不会跟着停下来。

所以，我不太相信台积电只是听客户讲了几个AI故事，就敢拿出这么多真金白银扩产。😂

如果一家经历过这么多轮半导体周期、拥有如此多一线产业信息的公司，经过反复验证后仍然决定大规模投资，我觉得这个判断很值得重视。

AI股票有没有泡沫？当然可能有。

但AI股票估值过高，和AI需求本身是不是泡沫，我觉得还是应该分开讨论。

比起市场每天冒出来的各种泡沫故事，我还是更愿意多看看产业链的实际变化。

这只是我的个人观察，也欢迎大家分享不同看法。👀

text:
昨天孙宇晨和金明的对谈《AI 黄金时代，普通人如何下注？》非常有深度的，看完了。其中一个环节，孙哥 @justinsuntron 推荐的第一本书是安·兰德的《源泉》。他说孙学借鉴了安学，这本书算是孙学的祖师爷。

其实这本书我在苏北高中的宿舍就看过，早就忘记了。正好趁着这个机会，结合 Claude 辅助帮大家整理一下，那孙学的祖师爷“安学”到底写了什么？753 页，小毛哥带大家拆一遍，太长不读版放在图里。

一句话概括：一个建筑师被学校开除，宁可去采石场砸石头也不改一笔图纸；设计被人篡改，他直接把楼炸了，最后在法庭上被判无罪。

整本书只在问一件事：你是为作品活，还是为别人的眼光活？

1/ 作者：一个逃离苏俄的女人

安·兰德 1905 年生在圣彼得堡，十月革命后家里的药店被没收，21 岁只身去了美国，在好莱坞从临时演员做到编剧。她这辈子最恨一件事：集体以"大家"的名义，拿走个人的东西。《源泉》写完被 12 家出版社拒稿，原定书名叫《二手人生》。1943 年出版时卖得很慢，后来全靠口碑，累计卖了 1000 万册以上。

2/ 剧情：一个不肯改图的人

全书第一句："霍华德·洛克笑了。"他刚被建筑学院开除，原因是不肯照古典样式画图。之后他跟过一个落魄的老建筑师，被时代淘汰；宁可去采石场砸石头，也不接要改设计的单；被评论家设局，全社会一起骂他。最燃的一段：他替同学基廷匿名设计一个廉租房项目，唯一的条件是照图施工。图被改了，他就把楼炸了。然后在法庭上一个人讲完一大段自辩，陪审团判他无罪。

3/ 四个人，四种活法

- 洛克是原创者，只对作品负责。
- 基廷是二手人，每一步都问别人怎么看，事业开挂，最风光的作品却是洛克替他画的。
- 托黑是操纵者，自己不创造，专门教大众该喜欢什么、该恨谁。
- 华纳德是迎合者，天赋极高，却拿来讨好大众，手握一切，最后发现权力是借来的。
你可以对照一下，自己现在更像哪一个。

4/ 精华 5 句

① 别当二手人。你想要的是作品本身，还是别人看你的眼光？

② 先有作品，再有客户。洛克的原话："我不是为了有客户而去建造，我是为了建造才要有客户。"

③ 真正的自信是"我没在想你"。反派问洛克怎么看他，洛克说："我根本没在想你。"

④ 堕落是一笔一笔改出来的。基廷从没做过一个大坏决定，只是每次都多听了别人一句。

⑤ 先会说"我"，才会说"我爱你"。

5/ 孙哥学到了什么

安学说，理性的利己是美德，创造财富的人推动世界。孙哥在 GQ 采访的时候提到：“企业家才是整个地球赖以转动的核心，人赚钱越多，越崇高。”

安学说，别管别人怎么看。孙哥是挨骂当营销，越骂声量越大。安学说，对作品忠诚到可以炸楼。孙哥的公司直接起名 Only Fountainhead、Objectivists。

 6/ 也别全信

书里男女主的第一次，一直被女性主义者批评是在美化强暴；1949 年拍成电影，票房没回本；极端个人主义被骂到今天。兰德的答案很爽，但人不是一座楼，炸了可以重盖。

 7/ 小毛哥的读法

我读到的不是"要自私"，是"别当二手人"。最近的感受就是做 𝕏 也一样：搬运的是基廷，原创的才是洛克。现在 𝕏 的原创奖励，等于在算法层面奖励洛克、惩罚基廷。二十岁的时候，所有人都会让你改一笔。能不能像洛克那样笑出来，就是少年心气。

text:
We just launched Fact Sheets at Token Terminal, adding legal, operational, and economic context to our onchain data across 10,000+ tokenized assets.

Our onchain data tracks supply, holders, transfers, and activity in DeFi venues. Fact Sheets complement these metrics with information about each asset:

→ Who the legal issuer is and where it’s domiciled
→ What claim the token represents
→ Who holds the underlying assets
→ Who can redeem the token and on what terms

These details are often scattered across prospectuses, legal agreements, and regulatory filings. We’ve structured them into 60+ standardized fields per asset, with answers linked to the relevant passages in the original sources.

Combining these disclosures with onchain metrics lets you ask more precise questions. For example: which tokenized stocks issued by entities domiciled in Jersey have seen the largest increase in holder count over the past 30 days?

Fact Sheets give investors more ways to compare tokenized assets and interpret their onchain activity.

a task for you this weekend: review where you spend your time.

check your screen time on your phone and laptop, write it all down. also try to write for everything offline too, including sleep.

how much of your week goes towards:

> work that moves you forward?
> earning skills and improving your finances?

rest and enjoyment belong on that list too. the point is to ask whether the way you spend your time reflects what you say you want, and is it aligned with your purpose? 

pick a few realistic targets for next week. put them in your calendar, let your grok bot remind you and commit to following through for seven days.

then repeat & review what changed, i can guarantee you'll feel much better.

quoted_text:
Beijing just took a big step towards closing the Chinese frontier. The rules could give China's government the power to restrict AI developers from releasing their most advanced open-weight models.

It proposes banning exports of AI technologies that autonomously generate and modify malicious code. It also wants to restrict exports of AI-assisted vulnerability-discovery technologies. Giving a model away for free, ie open-weight, could qualify as an export.

Crucially, the rules distinguish between technologies already in the public domain and those not yet released. It specifically exempts existing open-source models. But new releases could potentially trigger export controls.

Providing foreign customers with access to models through APIs (ie, closed models) is generally exempt, whereas restricted models being served overseas could require a licence.

Beijing promises essentially automatic licensing for open-source releases, allowing developers to publish almost immediately after notification. But it's unclear whether this applies to those capabilities proposed for outright export prohibition. 

If intelligence generalises, how can China's AI labs distinguish between a smart model and one that has the capabilities proposes for restrictions?

text:
AI 버블 붕괴가 아닌 단순 변동성인 이유

 벤 호로위츠 & 데이비드 색스(@DavidSacks)  & 차마스(@chamath)- All-In Podcast 

1. 닷컴 버블과의 결정적 차이: "수요 부족 vs 극심한 공급 부족" (벤 호로위츠)

1999년 '라우드클라우드(LoudCloud)'의 트라우마: 호로위츠와 마크 안드레센은 사실상 네오클라우드의 원조 격인 라우드클라우드를 1999년에 창업했습니다. 당시에는 인터넷 인프라와 브로드밴드, 브라우저가 막 보급되던 시기라, 막대한 빚을 내어 깔아놓은 광케이블 대역폭을 소비할 '최종 소비자 수요'가 턱없이 부족했습니다.

현재 AI 시장의 정반대 역학: 하지만 지금 AI 시장은 수요 부족이 아니라 '절대적인 공급 부족' 상태입니다.

앤디 재시(아마존 CEO)의 증언: 녹음 전날 호로위츠가 앤디 재시와 통화하며 "2028년까지 용량이 다 동났다던데 맞냐"고 묻자, 재시는 "2028년 이후까지도 물량이 없다. 빨라야 2028년 말에나 숨통이 트일 것"이라고 답했습니다.  $AMZN

공급망 가격의 상승: 토큰당 가격은 내려가고 있지만, 충분한 전력과 냉각 시설이 갖춰진 GPU 가격과 데이터센터 공간 임대료는 오히려 오르고 있습니다. 건설 인력 부족과 지역 사회의 정치적·규제적 반발로 데이터센터 신축이 극도로 어렵기 때문이며, 이는 이미 공급망을 확보한 CoreWeave에게 엄청난 순풍(Tailwind)으로 작용합니다.  $CRWV

2. GPU 수명 연장과 '강제된 희소성' (데이비드 색스)

단순 변동성인 이유: 수조 달러 규모의 미래 가치를 지수적(Exponential) 성장률에 기반해 평가할 때는 현재의 작은 데이터 하나에도 시장이 과민 반응하며 큰 변동성을 보입니다. 하지만 펀더멘털은 전혀 흔들리지 않았습니다.

GPU 경제적 수명의 깜짝 연장 (3~5년 ➔ 6~8년): 과거에는 GPU의 유효 수명을 3~5년으로 잡고 감가상각을 계산했으나, 추론(Inference) 수요가 폭발하면서 수명이 6~8년으로 늘어났습니다. 

실제로 이미 감가상각이 끝났어야 할 구형 칩(A100, H100)조차 현재 프리미엄 가격에 임대되고 있어, 장비 소유주들에게 예상치 못한 추가 수익(Upside surprise)을 안겨주고 있습니다. 심지어 VC들과 액셀러레이터들이 스타트업을 유치하기 위해 직접 남는 컴퓨팅 파워를 사들여 미끼로 쓸 정도로 구하기 힘든 상태입니다.

공급 과잉(Glut)이 불가능한 이유: 물리적 세계(Atoms)에서 기가와트(GW)급 전력과 데이터센터를 세우는 것은 일론 머스크의 로켓 과학자들조차 혀를 내두를 만큼 어렵습니다. 여기에 지역 커뮤니티의 인허가 지연 등 규제 역풍까지 겹쳐, 공급 과잉은커녕 '강제된 희소성(Enforced scarcity)'이 시장을 지배하고 있습니다.

3. 신용 리스크의 실체와 OpCo-PropCo 구조 (데이비드 색스)

폴리마켓 파산 확률(27년 말 15%, 28년 말 23%)의 오류: 차마스와 색스는 CoreWeave가 본사(OpCo)와 개별 프로젝트 자산 법인(PropCo, 이른바 '박스')을 완벽히 분리해 두었기 때문에 본사가 파산할 일은 없다고 일축했습니다. 설령 특정 데이터센터 프로젝트가 부실해져도 해당 특수목적법인(박스)만 법정관리(Receivership)에 들어가 담보로 잡힌 GPU를 매각해 정리하면 끝납니다.

무담보 채권 vs 자산유동화(ABS) 조달: 이번 주 유통시장(Secondary market)에서 20% 할인되어 수익률이 15%로 치솟은 채권은 CoreWeave 본사의 '무담보 회사채'입니다.

첫째, 유통시장 금리가 올랐다고 해서 CoreWeave가 기존 채권에 대해 내는 이자(9.6% 쿠폰)가 당장 늘어나는 것이 아닙니다.

둘째, 신규 데이터센터('박스')를 짓기 위한 350억 달러의 추가 자금 조달은 본사의 무담보 신용으로 빌리는 것이 아닙니다. 박스에 담긴 ①투자적격등급(Investment-grade) 우량 고객사(MS, 구글 등 매출의 75% 차지)의 5년 장기 계약서와 ②가치가 유지되고 있는 GPU 실물 자산을 담보로 한 자산유동화금융(Asset-backed financing)으로 조달합니다. 

따라서 대출 기관 입장에서는 CoreWeave가 아니라 마이크로소프트의 신용도를 보고 돈을 빌려주는 셈이므로 프로젝트 파이낸싱에는 문제가 없습니다.

4. 북극성 지표: '투자 회수 기간(Payback Period)' (데이비드 색스)

CoreWeave(2.5년) vs SpaceX/xAI(1년): 색스는 데이터센터 비즈니스에서 가장 주시해야 할 단 하나의 지표로 '투자 회수 기간'을 꼽았습니다.

CoreWeave: 5년 장기 고정가 계약을 맺는 대신 2.5년 만에 모든 투자 원리금을 회수합니다(GW당 약 200억 달러 수준으로 수익화).

SpaceX(일론 머스크): 양측이 90일 내에 해지할 수 있는 조건(사실상 현물 Spot 가격)으로 계약하기 때문에 GW당 약 500억 달러 수준으로 수익화하며, 투자 회수 기간이 불과 1년입니다.

결론: 마치 파리의 알짜배기 에어비앤비를 소유한 것처럼, 막대한 설비투자(CapEx)를 하더라도 1년~2.5년 만에 원금을 다 뽑아내고 부채를 빠르게 롤오버할 수 있다면 극도로 무능하지 않은 이상 망하는 것이 불가능합니다. 단, 향후 수요가 줄거나 시공 지연(지체상금 발생 등)으로 이 회수 기간이 길어지기 시작한다면 그때가 진짜 위험 신호입니다.

5. 궁극의 해자는 '전력(Power)'과 인프라 직접 소유 (차마스 & 호로위츠)

미국의 심각한 전력 적자(Electron Deficit): 차마스는 계획된 발전소가 모두 제때 지어진다는 비현실적 가정을 하더라도, 미국은 2050년까지 1.4테라와트시(TWh) — 캘리포니아주 6개 분량 — 의 전력이 부족할 것이라고 지적했습니다. 여기에 차세대 AI가 유발할 폭발적인 전력 부하(Load growth)는 아직 반영조차 되지 않았습니다.

하이퍼스케일러 병목 현상: 향후 JP모건이나 씨티은행 같은 거대 금융사, 혹은 혁신적인 제품을 만든 스타트업이 클라우드(AWS, Azure 등)에 가더라도 "전력 용량이 없어서 서비스를 못 띄워준다"며 거절당하는 초유의 사태가 벌어질 것입니다. 따라서 이제는 하이퍼스케일러에만 의존할 수 없으며, 토지, 전력, 인프라를 직접 소유하는 것이 AI 시대 궁극의 해자(Moat)가 됩니다.  $NBIS, $BE, $IREN, $CRWV

중동의 기회 상실과 엔비디아( $NVDA)의 독점력: 원래 사우디, UAE, 카타르 등 중동 산유국들이 풍부한 에너지와 하향식(Top-down) 의사결정을 바탕으로 AI 데이터센터의 메카가 될 절호의 기회를 잡았으나, 최근 전쟁과 드론 공습 리스크로 그 기회를 완전히 날렸습니다(단 한 대의 드론만 방공망을 뚫어도 데이터센터가 전소되기 때문). 

한편, 엔비디아는 칩뿐만 아니라 후공정 패키징과 고대역폭메모리(HBM) 물량까지 싹쓸이해(구글조차 자체 메모리 모듈을 설계해야 할 정도) 공급망을 완벽히 통제하고 있어, 컴퓨팅 현물 가격은 당분간 매우 높게 유지될 전망입니다.  $NVDA

"It wasn’t so long ago that DEI offices had enormous power on campus, where they could sway hiring decisions or help bring down even world-renowned faculty members.

Just ask David Sabatini. He was a molecular biologist working in Cambridge to figure out a protein called mTOR, which plays a critical role in tumor development, and he was at the top of his field. His research laid some of the groundwork for drug discoveries around organ transplantation and cancer treatment, and he was predicted to win the Nobel Prize. But Sabatini was fired in August 2021 from the job that paid his salary and resigned from two others, his name and reputation destroyed.

He had been working in science for about 25 years without so much as a complaint, he told me. But then Kristin Knouse, a fellow researcher with whom Sabatini had a consensual relationship, accused him of sexual harassment. 'I lost everything,' he told me back in 2022. 'My whole life imploded.'" 

—@SnoozyWeiss

text:
たった今、世界のAI覇権のバランスは完全にぶっ壊れました。これほんまにやばいです。
週明けのAI関連株は大暴落どころの騒ぎじゃないかもな…。
何が衝撃的なのか、ガチ解説します。
もう何もかもが変わっちまったんだな...。

■何がおきたか
DeepSeek v4.1-Flash 1017というモデルが公開されました。世界のAI情勢を破壊します。ヤバいモデルです。
このモデル簡単がどういうものなのか説明すると、
フロンティアモデルを一部で越える（SOTA級）のモデルを中華ラボがいきなり出してきた。

問題はその性能、値段とサイズと仕組み
どれも本当に破壊的なものだから、1個ずついきます。

■性能
全分野でOpus5.5を超えたっていうわけじゃないけど。
完全にDeepSeek v4.1-Flash 1017はSOTA級

DeepSWEっていうベンチが一番衝撃的かな。
- 今回のFlash：成功率77%、約0.20ドル／タスク
- GPT-6.1 Solの最も高得点の設定：約75%、約0.65ドル／タスク
つまり、この比較では約3分の1の費用で、成功率も少し高い。大量に実装・修正を回す用途には大きな差。
というか、成功率でSolを越えてるっていう事実がヤバいんだよ。

■値段
もう完全に乱暴に言うと。ほぼタダです。<言い過ぎ
INPUT$0.15Output$0.3

入力10万＋出力1万トークンの例だと
Solより約86〜93%安く、Opusより約93〜97%安い
DeepSeekハーネスを使えば、自分の利用では、入力のキャッシュヒット率が99%になることもあったので。
実際はもっと安い。
過去に湯水のように使えるAstra,Opus,Fableをくれとは言ったが。ここまでやれとは言ってない。
本当に、なんだろう、マジで安いんだよ。
実際の感覚だと200倍ぐらい安いね。

■サイズ
これだけヤバいモデルのオープンウェイトが同時に無料公開されました。
そのサイズは763B。重みだけで約510.3GB

例えば米国のフロンティアモデルのサイズは10Tとか言われてるんですね、公開情報じゃないからわからん無いけど。Kimi K3とかが2.8T

要するに、めちゃくちゃサイズが小さいんですよ。
このパラメータ数って多ければ多いほど計算に計算資源と電力がかかるんで、コストかかるんですよ。

アメリカのAIモデルって、バカみたいに計算資源を保有してるからゴリ押しでそれを解決してるんですけど。

こんだけ軽かったら、もう普通に家で使えるレベルなんですよ。

実際、DGXSpark × 4台とかMacStudio 512GBで動かせると思います。
バカみたいなデータセンターがなくても、フロンティアモデルが動くようになっちゃったってわけ。

■仕組み
ここがかなり驚き度の高いポイントなんですけど。
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash自体はもともと存在していて。
まあそこそこ人気だったんですけど。本当に安くてそこそこ性能いいから、結構人気あるよね、ぐらいの賢さだったんですよ。

そのもともとあったモデルを自己フィードバックを使うRLで強化した。って公式は言ってて。
まあ詳しい説明は省きますけど。要するに、既に存在していたモデルを後から調整していくようなやり方で、とんでもなく性能をあげた。

驚くのは、既存モデルの後学習で、開発タスクの成功率を上げながら、処理時間や出力量まで減らしたところです。性能を上げたうえで、使う側の費用まで下げてきた。その性能の上り方が半端じゃないんだよ…意味わかんねぇよ…

DeepSeekのラボが今世界で最もAI、優れたAIラボであるということを認めなきゃいけない。

quoted_text:
X Layer x TapeOut Space 回顾：机会、项目与下一站

10 月 16 日晚，X Layer（@XLayerOfficial）与 TapeOut （@TapeOutWorld) 举办联合 Space。会上确认两件事：TapeOut 协议已原生部署在 X Layer，X Layer 是 TapeOut 多链部署的第一站；双方同日启动 X Layer x TapeOut 开发者加速计划，奖池 10 万美元打底，为期约两个月。

主持人是 X Layer 生态增长负责人 CC（@EudemoniaCC）。TapeOut 团队到场的是三号成员 Alda（@nat_poprika）和四号成员 Percy（@HYPERTXT__），生态嘉宾有 Benson（@benson_doge）、Kexin（@web3kexin）、星帅（@xing8047），以及 KOL 王短鸟（@Wangduanniao）。以下是内容回顾。

🔲 加速计划怎么参加

据 CC 介绍：

· 个人和团队都可以全程线上参加
· 报名和作品提交截止 2026 年 12 月 8 日 20:00（香港时间）
· 应用、游戏、工具、电路、电商服务等方向都欢迎
· 评判看三点：商业设计是否完整、用户体验、市场反馈
· X Layer 侧的支持包括交易流动性激励、Super Nova 计划、Boost 榜单，以及钱包侧流量和品牌宣发

CC 说，TapeOut 的协议和开发者工具已基本完备，目前缺少能让协议破圈的现象级应用。这次加速计划要找的是有真实用户、能持续用下去的产品。

🔲 TapeOut 是什么

Percy 的介绍：TapeOut 是一套开源协议，代码在 GitHub 公开。它让区块链除了记账，还能承载可验证计算和生产工具：把逻辑、甚至整个网站放进链上的电路容器里运行，这部分叫 DeWeb。

过去两个月是第一阶段，底层架构已经搭好。目前链上网站 150 多个、处理器 1,000 多个、电路近 6 万个。

未来一年的目标是从「大家玩得开心」走到「有人持续用、愿意付费」。具体是三件事：继续迭代协议底层和 DeWeb；把协议标准定稳，让其他平台可以直接接入；把开发门槛降到有想法就能做出来，10 月 10 日发布的 TapeCode 就是为此做的。

🔲 为什么是 X Layer

Alda 说，Blon（@Blonskr）和 Zakk（@zakk_okx） 深谈之后，认为 X Layer 确实愿意扶持开发者和新技术。X Layer 背后有 OKX 钱包入口、庞大的用户群和持续的建设者计划，能让 TapeOut 服务到更多开发者。

CC 从 X Layer 的角度补充了两点。一是 X Layer 目前以 meme 为主，需要在 meme 之外拓展 TapeOut 这样少见的产品类型，可组合的逻辑电路能形成 X Layer 自己的叙事。二是 Pod 和电路容器可以和现有生态结合，带来新的链上活跃、用户和应用场景。她 8 月底入职后，团队专门开过 TapeOut 的学习会。

🔲 TapeOut 想找哪些建设者

Percy 列了四类：

· 应用开发者，不限 Web3 老手，也欢迎 Web2 的产品经理、独立开发者、设计师和懂某个行业的人。他举的需求例子是小商家记账麻烦、社群投票不透明、公益捐款难追踪
· 愿意用 AI 编程的人。有了 TapeCode，从想法到上线的距离已经很短
· 电路和元件设计者，可以通过协议服务获得收入
· DeWeb 基础设施的建设者，一起优化用户体验

🔲 哪类项目会先跑出来

Benson 把现有产品分三类：有实际用途的资产，比如游戏道具、社区会员资格；围绕容器的资产管理和服务，比如锁仓、AI agent 管理；帮开发者把前两类做出来的底层工具，比如官方的 TapeKit 和 TapeCode。他认为早期最先跑出来的是工具类，其次是轻游戏、社区互动这类门槛低的小应用。衍生品、交割、算力租赁这类复杂金融产品需要较长的合约审计和优化周期，不会很快出来。

星帅更期待软硬件结合的项目。他介绍了社区正在推进的一个项目：把真实芯片的设计蓝图一比一上链，芯片从生产、流通到销售的每个环节，都可以核验实物和原始设计是否一致。他认为芯片企业为了供应链安全，会愿意为这类验证付费。

Kexin 期待电路有明确用途，成为别人搭应用时可以直接引用的组件，再围绕组件长出订阅和维护服务。短期他看好贴近现有需求的小工具，比如帮人看懂电路、查生态数据、找现成组件的工具，以及 DeWeb 上的小游戏、学习工具、作品展示站。目标用户清楚、功能集中的产品更容易起步，他举的例子是生态里的 TapeUP（@tapeupio）。

王短鸟从持币者的角度回答：用户最在意的是能不能赚钱。他提到前段时间 X Layer 上的一次铸造，不少人有收益，他印象中约 500 个 OKB 参与其中。在他看来，这类项目减少了 OKB 的流通，对 OKB 价格有帮助。CC 回应，价格是共识的体现，有涨有跌很正常，有持续商业需求的项目终会带来回报。

🔲 下一步要解决什么

Alda 提到两个门槛。

一是使用门槛。以前做东西要先懂电路、流片，现在 TapeCode 可以用自然语言开发，技术经验不多的人也能一个人做出商业化应用。

二是 DeWeb 的大文件存储。这项功能已在内网测试，未来几周发布，同时推出去中心化中继网关网络和 DeWeb 跨应用的消息通道。另外，社区提出的 TAP-11 提案会让容器可以对外提供 API 服务。

🔲 从零到第一个产品

Percy 给的路径：

1. 从一个具体的人的具体麻烦出发
2. 装 TapeCode，大约 10 分钟出原型，顺带走一遍前端、后端、合约、审计的流程。创建电路容器后，约 3 次授权就能把 DeWeb 网站部署到 X Layer，省去买云服务器、买域名、配 DNS
3. 有了 MVP 之后找真实用户，按早期反馈迭代，同时找融资。TapeOut 计划和 X Layer 一起推出 ITO 机制（一键流片融资），目前尚未上线

🔲 两个商业化案例

Alda 对参赛开发者的建议：先找到用户愿意付费的场景，做小而精，把一个点做透。做完可以发到 TapeCode 的交流板块和榜单，团队会跟进答疑。卖东西时尽量减少用户的支付和操作步骤。

她举了两个已经在赚钱的例子。

一位开发者铸造了自己全部的晶体管，建了自己的处理器，在网站上替用户流片电路，手续费是官方流片的 3 倍。官方流片步骤复杂，他替新手省掉了这些步骤。

另一位开发者 Martin（@martin23_sen） 看到官方晶体管市场体验不好，自己做了一个 TapeOut 协议交易市场Firsto（@FirstoAI）。现在这个市场占协议交易量约 70%，Space 当天完成了近 200 BNB 的矿机交易，他靠手续费获得稳定收入。

🔲 怎么向新人介绍 TapeOut

Kexin 的说法：可以把 TapeOut 理解成链上的数字电路系统，像拼积木，有人做零件，有人把零件组合成工具，有人把工具做成应用，新人挑一个环节入手就行。

他建议先体验一个具体应用，或者去 https://t.co/BZDvEZ4FAZ 的官方画布里搭一个简单电路。设计都在浏览器里完成，决定流片时才需要上链、才产生成本。

他也提到目前的理解门槛：新用户一进来就看到 NAND、电路容器这些概念，很容易不知道从哪开始。介绍时应该先讲能用它做什么，再讲背后的原理；开发者需要能直接跑起来的示例。Benson 也认为门槛仍然偏高，需要更好地接住 Web2 和圈外用户。

🔲 中文台提问：FabX 怎么参与

中文台莫信（@musinoot）提到，X Layer 上最近出现了基于 TapeOut 生态的项目 FabX（@Fabx_global），社区不少人参与了，但不清楚该囤晶体管、攒挖矿代币，还是设计最优电路，应该看哪些数据。

Benson 的回答（个人观点）：

· 最优首创电路可能被抢，投入前先看它是否容易被抢
· 晶体管目前约一半已销毁铸成电路板，要留一部分，不要全部铸成电路板
· 他自己的配置思路是 $FAB、晶体管、电路板大致 1:1:1，再配一些 OKB；质押 OKB 和 BEM 可以提高产量

🔲 收尾

Benson 希望 X Layer 上长出一批愿意持续使用和付费的用户，开发者靠服务获得收入。Kexin 希望技术能走进普通用户的生活、解决实际问题。Alda 希望无数开发者把网站和线上服务跑在 X Layer 的 DeWeb 上，做出能持续经营的产品。

本文基于 Space 录音整理，发言内容来自自动转写，可能存在个别偏差。嘉宾观点不代表 X Layer 中文台立场。本文为社区内容，非 X Layer 官方发布，仅作生态跟踪整理，不构成任何投资建议。

孙宇晨的这个采访反响强烈，但是这个视频最大的Alpha其实是主持人。你难道不好奇，是谁让孙哥瞬间变了一个人，收起薄肌黄毛的嬉皮笑脸，这么严肃认真地输出？

他叫金明 William Joy，圈内叫他仙道。很低调，连 X 账号都没有。但他绝对是一个T0级的人类，我觉得能放到一起对标的大概只有谷爱凌了。他的履历第一眼看离谱到像编的：

- 现役自由潜水国家队，世界冠军，两项世界纪录，59 项国家纪录，打破了欧美33年开赛以来对自由潜水所有世界纪录的垄断
- 本科进哈佛学数学计算机，学生时代创业，入驻Harvard Innovation Lab，拿哈佛真理基金投资
- 极链科技创始人，27 岁拿到包括阿里在内的 10 亿元投资
- 湖畔大学四期，最年轻的创一代学员
- 从 2010 年持有特斯拉至今，加拿大持有 Tesla 最早的自然人
- 投资人，掌舵908HOLDING家办，前几天Token2049 Coinbase 全球交易赛获得第三，亚洲第一，为中国队拿到唯一的奖牌

仙道今年7月在本末社群的香港活动上做过一个精彩的压轴演讲，我推荐X上的大家如果没有看过，一定不要错过。覆盖面涉及到投资、卡牌、健康抗衰biohacking、美学、人生哲学、运气、社会责任，信息密度极高。在这个一天薄肌黄毛复读机的时代，已经很少能看到这么有深度+inspiring的内容了。

孙哥对话的视频，我只是2倍速看了一遍而已，仙道的这个视频，我1.5倍速看了两遍，甚至还在不断回去看细节。不要看AI总结，这个视频值得你的时间，看完你会来谢我。
author: otterpal24
quoted_text:
孙宇晨最新深度采访完整版：看空BTC，看空纳指，观望ETH，看好AI应用，不玩A股... 严肃分享了很多市场观点和交易仓位，值得一看

看空BTC。认为比特币面对AI和量子计算的威胁很难全身而退，市场低估了这类风险对 BTC 的潜在冲击。抗量子升级只能救"愿意自救的人"，硬分叉冻结老币在比特币的去中心化下几乎不可能达成共识。但是他的BTC是底仓，在过去一年的下跌中并没有减仓。

ETH目前仅2成仓位观望。 在去年 3600–4000 减了八九成的ETH（去年 11–12 月，减持逻辑是 4800 那个"只靠 Tom Lee 续命"的二顶），截至目前仍然没有买回。ETH减仓期间，他增配了美股。

纳指中线"微微看空"，看空但还没做空。认为资金抱团太严重，硬件股被炒成软件股，AI 循环融资一出事全出事。美债是所有资金的"母级"，现在被权益"子级"吸血，利率必须高才接得到钱，高到一定程度钱又会倒流。芯片短期不排除过剩，像 2000 年的光纤。

AI板块最看好应用。尤其 AI 健康管理（数据采集→挖掘→决策，不用等生病才去医院）。最不看好存储、光模块。一个锚：单一企业市值上限≈美债的一半，所以英伟达顶多再翻 4 倍，而应用层能翻 4 倍以上的机会太多了。明年后年主题会分化。

人民币会走强，美债危机被过度担忧。只要美国还握着 AI（芯片、存储、模型）的终极控制权，美债就不缺买家，"孙悟空跳不出如来佛的手掌心"。

基本没有A股仓位，但会做一些研究。对于A股光模块行情，他的解释是，这一方向能够连接美国AI投资需求，同时中国企业已有一定制造与产业布局，因此容易形成资金集中。所有老登类资产（白酒等）都不看好，新登类资产积极拥抱。

Hyperliquid是本轮周期里重要的新发展。认为美股永续合约为整个行业打开了新的产品空间，DEX 能否挤掉 CEX 取决于美国监管给不给 Uniswap 式豁免。

RWA 空间非常大。波场11月也要大力推美股上链，逻辑同 USDT：给第三世界一个配置美元资产的入口。

author: zemummy1
quoted_text:
@zemummy1        直播纪要
第一趋势交易中的止损和止盈应该怎么处理？
             趋势单不能把止损放得太窄，应根据关键结构设置止损，同时控制仓位。既然做趋势，目标空间也要足够大，不能只看几个点的利润。

第二开仓和仓位应该怎样安排？
    连线者目前是十倍开多，先使用50%仓位，下跌后继续加仓。嘉宾认为主要问题是仓位偏大、止损太窄，或者没有等到更合适的进场位置。

第三怎样计算止损和盈亏比？
             进场前就要同时计算目标位和止损位。例如5万8800加仓、5万5止损，目标看7万至7万2、7万3附近，盈亏比约为1∶3至1∶4；7万9500做空时，止损则考虑放在8万2500以上。

第四6万进场、5万5止损，止盈位置应该怎么定？        
                如果只看到6万6，目标和止损空间接近，盈亏比并不合适。趋势判断成立时，应有看到7万2、7万3的空间；行情启动后也不要急着止盈，比特币趋势通常会持续21至50天，可在周期结束、出现明显利空或走势异常时再考虑离场。

text:
I’m going to let you in on a secret about rape that I learned while bouncing at 3 nightclubs concurrently for my entire undergrad. 500 nights at the club dealing with women and creeps have produced some insight.

The first thing to understand is that 99% of date-rape cases are just patently false. Every weekend like clockwork a new tiny girl who hadn’t eaten all day would confidently down 5 shots of tequila then claim she was drugged once word got around that she shit herself in a cab, or fell asleep in a dumpster.

I’ve lost count of how many of them were perplexed to report that their drug tests came back clean the next morning.

BUT… In my 500 nights of service, I witnessed it happen for real, bill cosby style, twice. 

And in 100% of those cases it was a black or an Indian guy.

The first was a guy named Sohil who had actually openly made some suspect remarks to people I knew. Why was nothing done? Because the concept was so completely alien to the white guys around him that they simply didn’t believe what they were hearing. 

It was exactly like the scene from American Psycho where he talks about a girls head on a stick as though it’s the punchline to a joke, and his friends just exchange a weird look and carry on. That’s how crazy the prospect of rape sounds to white guys, he might as well have said he had a head in his freezer.

Ultimately, Sohil was caught trying to sneak into a drugged girl’s bedroom window after her roommates had shuttled her home for the night. He was sentenced to 2 years in prison. There was no international outrage, no big news articles, nothing. Just a post on Facebook shared between the bar staff.

The second was a black guy from Martinique. He was a charming niggardly character who hung around the bars every weekend bumming cigarettes or making a few bucks selling fake cocaine. He lived in someone’s walk-in closet for $300 a month.

He had rumours circulating about his predation, but nobody had anything concrete until he was finally caught inappropriately touching an incapacitated girl and force feeding her drugs. 

He was quickly and brutally sentenced to a swift release and a mild scolding from a social worker. He had successfully argued to the judge that people would kill him if he were sent back to Martinique, and was therefore let off with not even a slap on the wrist. 

The funniest part of this whole ordeal is that we have reason to suspect that he was a refugee in the first place because he had raped the wrong guy’s sister back home. You genuinely can’t make this shit up. 

Word got around to the bars, but this was back in the day. We didn’t have ID scanners, and hiring was a revolving door. Every Fortnite we’d have a new roster of Dianabol enthusiasts standing at the entrance letting groups of bombshells skip the line. It was impossible to entirely keep people out.

And so within 2 months it happened again. Exactly the same as last time. And the black guy hit the judge with the exact same excuse. Luckily the judge finally came to his senses, and sent him back to a third world shithole. He has lived in Paris France ever since. 

I tell these stories because I’m at my whits end with headlines like the one I see below. At this point we’re so used to being gaslit that the omission of a description is as good as a 4K portrait.

So I’ll do my small part to set record straight. 

It is never the white men.

text:
🧰 太大方了，Anthropic 把自己做 Claude 应用的示范代码全摊开了——claude-quickstarts，照着抄就能跑起一个能用的 AI 应用。

正挂在 GitHub 热榜上，已经 1.8 万 star、3106 个 fork，MIT 许可证，拿去改商用都行。

从零接 Claude API，最耗时间的不是写功能，是搞清楚「这东西到底该怎么搭」：会话怎么存、工具怎么挂、agent 跑崩了怎么续。claude-quickstarts 把这些都做成了能直接跑起来的完整项目——客服机器人、金融数据分析、浏览器自动化、能自己写代码的 agent，每个都带自己的 README 和配置说明，你照着改比对着文档猜快太多。

最值得翻的是 computer use 那两个：一个是让 Claude 直接操作桌面的 demo，另一个是在原生 macOS 上的参考实现，提示缓存、服务端压缩、批量工具调用、沙盒化 shell、轨迹记录这些门道全写进代码里了。另外还有一个把 Managed Agents Sessions API 包成九个工具的 MCP server，stdio 和 Streamable HTTP 两种接法都给了。

与其对着文档猜，不如先把官方的示例跑一遍。

GitHub：https://t.co/He29X5GtnP

Doing good in this space clearly isn’t always viewed as a good thing. This is the proof.

text:
🚨Anthropic正式确认，第三方应用可以继续使用Claude 订阅额度！

10月7日， @AnthropicAI  更新了Claude Agent SDK的官方政策，明确确认，第三方应用仍然可以通过Claude Agent SDK消耗用户现有的 @claudeai  订阅额度。

这事其实挺有意思的。

今年5月，Anthropic曾宣布准备将Claude Agent SDK、claude -p以及第三方应用的使用量从订阅额度中剥离，改成独立的Credits计费。

结果6月份临时暂停了这项调整。

现在到了10月份，Anthropic又明确确认，开发者仍然可以沿用原来的订阅额度调用方式。

Max和Team用户甚至还额外获得了每月API Credits。

而且已经有产品已经接入了。

10月10日，Amp宣布正式支持用户接入自己的Claude Pro / Max 、订阅，底层直接使用Claude Agent SDK，同时保留自己的云端运行环境、线程共享、多Agent编排等能力。

这意味着，第三方Agent产品可以把Anthropic官方的 Agent SDK当作底层Runtime，在上面继续构建自己的产品和工作流。

我觉得这对整个Agent生态其实挺重要的。

当模型能力和Agent Runtime都可以作为基础设施被复用，第三方开发者就有机会把更多精力投入到应用、工作流和用户体验上。

而且用户已经为Claude付过一次订阅费了，能直接带着订阅额度使用其他产品，确实会降低尝试新Agent的成本。

接下来就看Anthropic愿意把这条路开放到什么程度，以及会有多少第三方Agent跟进了？

@lobehub 快接一下

text:
J'ai vu une Tesla décoller. Et j'ai entendu beaucoup de bêtises.

« Ça ne sert à rien. » « Gadget de milliardaire. » « Qui a besoin d'une voiture qui vole ? »

Personne. Et c'est exactement pour ça que c'est important.

En 1978, Brabham a aligné en Formule 1 une voiture équipée d'un ventilateur géant à l'arrière. Il aspirait l'air sous le châssis et plaquait la voiture au sol. Elle a gagné sa première course avec une avance insolente. Elle a été interdite immédiatement.

Quarante-huit ans plus tard, on y revient. Un système de succion qui colle la voiture à la route et lui permet de passer sous la seconde au 0 à 100. 

Personne n'a « besoin » de faire le 0 à 100 en moins d'une seconde. Comme personne n'a besoin d'une Formule 1. Et pourtant : les freins carbone de votre berline, l'hybridation de votre moteur, l'aérodynamique de votre SUV, les palettes au volant — tout ça vient de voitures de course que personne n'utilisera jamais pour aller au travail.
La Formule 1 ne sert à rien. Pourtant elle sert à tout.

En 1973, quand la France a lancé Ariane, l'Europe sortait de onze échecs consécutifs du programme Europa. La presse parlait d'argent jeté dans l'espace. Vingt ans plus tard, Ariane détenait la moitié du marché mondial des lancements commerciaux, et chaque satellite de télévision, de météo ou de GPS que vous utilisez a bénéficié de cette obstination.

Le progrès a toujours la même tête au début : un truc inutile, cher, ridicule, construit par des gens qu'on prend pour des fous.
Ce que j'ai vu à Dallas, ce n'est pas une voiture volante. C'est un châssis, une gestion de l'énergie et une maîtrise des flux d'air que l'industrie automobile mettra dix ans à digérer. 
Les applications viendront : sécurité, freinage, stabilité, consommation. Elles finiront dans des voitures ordinaires conduites par des gens qui expliqueront, en 2036, que tout ça était évident.

La question n'est jamais « à quoi ça sert ».
La question est : qui ose encore construire des choses qui ne servent à rien ?

Il y a cinquante ans, c'était nous. La fusée, le TGV, le Concorde, le Minitel. 

L'Europe construisait des choses absurdes et magnifiques.

Aujourd'hui, on commente depuis le siège arrière car nous sommes hors course. 

Merci @elonmusk de nous faire rêver

孙宇晨的这个采访反响强烈，但是这个视频最大的Alpha其实是主持人。你难道不好奇，是谁让孙哥瞬间变了一个人，收起薄肌黄毛的嬉皮笑脸，这么严肃认真地输出？

他叫金明 William Joy，圈内叫他仙道。很低调，连 X 账号都没有。但他绝对是一个T0级的人类，我觉得能放到一起对标的大概只有谷爱凌了。他的履历第一眼看离谱到像编的：

- 现役自由潜水国家队，世界冠军，两项世界纪录，59 项国家纪录，打破了欧美33年开赛以来对自由潜水所有世界纪录的垄断
- 本科进哈佛学数学计算机，学生时代创业，入驻Harvard Innovation Lab，拿哈佛真理基金投资
- 极链科技创始人，27 岁拿到包括阿里在内的 10 亿元投资
- 湖畔大学四期，最年轻的创一代学员
- 从 2010 年持有特斯拉至今，加拿大持有 Tesla 最早的自然人
- 投资人，掌舵908HOLDING家办，前几天Token2049 Coinbase 全球交易赛获得第三，亚洲第一，为中国队拿到唯一的奖牌

仙道今年7月在本末社群的香港活动上做过一个精彩的压轴演讲，我推荐X上的大家如果没有看过，一定不要错过。覆盖面涉及到投资、卡牌、健康抗衰biohacking、美学、人生哲学、运气、社会责任，信息密度极高。在这个一天薄肌黄毛复读机的时代，已经很少能看到这么有深度+inspiring的内容了。

quoted_text:
孙宇晨最新深度采访完整版：看空BTC，看空纳指，观望ETH，看好AI应用，不玩A股... 严肃分享了很多市场观点和交易仓位，值得一看

看空BTC。认为比特币面对AI和量子计算的威胁很难全身而退，市场低估了这类风险对 BTC 的潜在冲击。抗量子升级只能救"愿意自救的人"，硬分叉冻结老币在比特币的去中心化下几乎不可能达成共识。但是他的BTC是底仓，在过去一年的下跌中并没有减仓。

ETH目前仅2成仓位观望。 在去年 3600–4000 减了八九成的ETH（去年 11–12 月，减持逻辑是 4800 那个"只靠 Tom Lee 续命"的二顶），截至目前仍然没有买回。ETH减仓期间，他增配了美股。

纳指中线"微微看空"，看空但还没做空。认为资金抱团太严重，硬件股被炒成软件股，AI 循环融资一出事全出事。美债是所有资金的"母级"，现在被权益"子级"吸血，利率必须高才接得到钱，高到一定程度钱又会倒流。芯片短期不排除过剩，像 2000 年的光纤。

AI板块最看好应用。尤其 AI 健康管理（数据采集→挖掘→决策，不用等生病才去医院）。最不看好存储、光模块。一个锚：单一企业市值上限≈美债的一半，所以英伟达顶多再翻 4 倍，而应用层能翻 4 倍以上的机会太多了。明年后年主题会分化。

人民币会走强，美债危机被过度担忧。只要美国还握着 AI（芯片、存储、模型）的终极控制权，美债就不缺买家，"孙悟空跳不出如来佛的手掌心"。

基本没有A股仓位，但会做一些研究。对于A股光模块行情，他的解释是，这一方向能够连接美国AI投资需求，同时中国企业已有一定制造与产业布局，因此容易形成资金集中。所有老登类资产（白酒等）都不看好，新登类资产积极拥抱。

Hyperliquid是本轮周期里重要的新发展。认为美股永续合约为整个行业打开了新的产品空间，DEX 能否挤掉 CEX 取决于美国监管给不给 Uniswap 式豁免。

RWA 空间非常大。波场11月也要大力推美股上链，逻辑同 USDT：给第三世界一个配置美元资产的入口。

quoted_text:
@carmenli , CEO of @silicondata and @computeexchange , joins the show to explain how compute is becoming a brand-new asset class. 
A former energy options market maker at DRW who later ran global data integrations at @Bloomberg , Carmen was pre-seeded by DRW founder Don Wilson to build the GPU industry benchmarks. Silicon Data is the referee "the Bloomberg for compute" while Compute Exchange is the liquidity layer where GPUs, tokens and servers change hands.
We get into why token price indexes are falling, recent token & model consumption trends, why GPU residual values are above accounting depreciation schedules, and how neoclouds, their lenders, and compute users can hedge GPU exposure to reduce business volatility.

• "The A100 has been around for six years at this point, and we still see three-year contracts signed on A100s." Residual values are still hovering above five-year straight-line depreciation.

•  “we'd definitely be looking at 30 trillion of [GPU] derivatives every year."

Topics: Compute as an asset class, GPU indices, CME compute futures, GPU depreciation and useful life, neoclouds, token pricing, AI chip supply chain,

💡 This episode is presented by: @OxfordDataPlan –The Home of Alternative Data

*Not Investment Advice.

Highlights:

(0:00) Doug introduces Carmen Li, CEO of Silicon Data and Compute Exchange
(0:20) From energy options market maker at DRW to Bloomberg Data, and why AI startups' swinging GPU costs made compute an industry-wide hedging problem
(4:09) How DRW founder Don Wilson pre-seeded Silicon Data, and building products with no product or sales team
(6:10) Two sides of the coin: Silicon Data as "the Bloomberg for compute" and Compute Exchange as "the Nasdaq for compute"
(7:49) Licensing indices to CME for H100 and B200 compute futures, and four ETFs filed before the futures even trade
(10:22) What makes an index the source of truth: tracking supply-demand, resisting manipulation, staying neutral
(12:57) Normalizing 50 B200 server configurations, and what earns a premium or a discount to the benchmark
(16:04) Sizing the market: from 1–3 trillion in spot compute to a potential 30 trillion in derivatives notional
(18:13) Who hedges first: neoclouds, hyperscalers and the financiers holding GPUs on their balance sheets
(21:06) Michael Burry's depreciation bear case vs. the physical market: A100s still signing three-year contracts after six years

text:
I staged games in the Roman Empire, twenty centuries before you were born. 

I say this not to boast, though I did boast then on marble inscriptions, which was how we boasted before you invented the smaller, faster marble you carry in your hands.

I was an aedile, one of the lesser magistratus, the men who kept Rome running so the great men could be seen running it. You will not know the word. Cicero knew it; he called my office the care of three things, urbs, annona, ludi, the city, the grain, and the games. He listed them in that order out of politeness. We all knew the real order was grain, games, and then, if time remained, the city.

I have been here in your capital for some weeks now. I arrived by means I do not understand and will not insult you by pretending to. One moment the Forum, the smell of it, fish and incense and the particular sweat of a mob that has not yet decided what it wants; the next, this. Glass. Light that comes from no flame. A device that knows my face. I assumed at first that I had died and that this was the part of the underworld reserved for magistrates, an eternity of watching other men do my job badly.

I was wrong. They do it beautifully. I am not in Hades. I am in a triumph, and I am the defeated king paraded through the streets, made to walk behind the chariot and admire the magnificence of the men who conquered me. I came prepared to condescend. I have stayed to take notes.

Let me correct one thing you believe about us, since you believe so little that is true. You picture us in marble. Marble was for the dead and for the gods. The living Rome was brick and timber stacked seven stories high, tenements that burned so often we had a word for the nights they didn’t. It was a city of a million souls with no space to walk, shrieking with wagon-wheels all night because we banned the carts by day. It stank of the dye-shops, which bleached cloth with urine collected at every corner, and of the Tiber, which was also our sewer. I have smelled your capital. I grant you this much: on the smell, you have beaten us.

Now let me explain my trade, so you can measure theirs.

The formula is old, older than me, and a poet of my era gave it the phrase you still use, though you have mistranslated it for two thousand years. Panem et circenses. Bread and the circus-games. He meant it as contempt. He described a people who had once handed out imperium, fasces, legiones, omnia, command, the symbols of office, the legions, everything, and who now, having sold their votes so long ago that no one bothered to buy them anymore, wanted two things only, and anxiously. Grain, and the races. The list got shorter. It always gets shorter. And he included himself in the selling. “Ever since we stopped selling our votes.” He was not above the mob. He was the mob, with better Latin.

Here is the whole of it in one breath, so you will not mistake me: a people that once gave armies to its generals, and provinces to its governors, and the whole turning world to whichever man it chose, now, having learned that choosing changed nothing, asks of its masters one thing only, to be entertained while it is emptied.

You say vox populi as though it were holy, the voice of the people the voice of god. We had a truer phrase. Tacitus called them plebs sordida ac circo sueta, the grubby crowd, broken to the racetrack like a horse to harness. We did not worship the voice of the people. We fed it, which is different, and cheaper.

So. Bread, first, because bread is first, always, and the man who forgets it dies in the Forum surrounded by his own reserves. We fed Rome on grain that did not grow in Italy. It came by ship from Sicily, Africa, and Egypt after we took it. A senator of my age wrote, in a cold sweat, that Rome had provisions for fifteen days and no more, that we had chosen to feed ourselves on cargo-boats and accidents. We imported the bread of the mob from the provinces, and if this meant the Italian farmer could not compete with a slave-worked estate and a grain fleet, well. The farmer did not riot in the Forum. The farmer was far away, being noble, in a field. The mob was here.

I tell you this so you will believe me when I say I wept, actual tears, a Roman’s tears, when I understood what the first man of this city has done with beef.

For he has a shortage. His herds are the smallest in living memory, the price of ground meat climbs past every record, and the mob feels it, as mobs do, in the one organ that votes, the stomach. And what does he do? He does exactly what I did. He reaches past his own herdsmen, past the men of his own provinces, and brings in cheap foreign meat, from the south, from Argentina, three hundred thousand tons, the tariff flung open, and promises the mob it will come a quarter below the price. He fed the city on foreign flesh and let the home producer bear it. I invented this. I could have embraced him as a son.

And then, because I am a professional, I read the ledger. And here the apprentice surpasses the master in a way that frightened me.

When I undercut my farmers, the city at least got cheap bread. That was the bargain, crude but balanced. Here? The price paid to his own herdsmen for their cattle fell by a seventh in a single month. The price of the meat on the mob’s table fell by thirteen coins of the hundred. Thirteen. The herdsman is ruined, and the mob barely notices the gift. He has staged the true sacrifice of his own supporters, blood and all, and the crowd it was meant to appease cannot taste the difference. In Rome that scandal ends an aedileship. Here it is Tuesday. And the herdsmen, these ruined cattlemen of the far provinces, are his own people, the loudest of his mob, and they are thanking him for the chance to be slaughtered, because he told them, on the small marble, that he loves them. We put garum on everything, a sauce of fish left to rot in the sun until it turned to gold, and paid more for it than for the fish it ruined. So I do not judge a people by what it eats. I judge it by what it will swallow when told the price has come down.

We had an emperor, the divine Augustus, a subtle man, who wrote that he had been tempted to abolish the grain dole entirely, because the people had grown so dependent that the farms were failing. And he stopped himself. He did not abolish it, and his reason, which he wrote down, is the most honest sentence any ruler of mine committed to papyrus: he knew that some future ruler, out of desire for popular favor, would simply bring it back. He declined to do the right thing because he knew his successor would undo it to be loved. That is the whole of statecraft, and the only difference across two thousand years is that Augustus had the decency to be ashamed of the knowing, and to write the shame down, in the first person, where we could find it.

The bread had its rituals, and the rituals are what I look for first in a new city, the way you might look for a familiar face. To collect your grain you brought a tessera, a token of baked clay, your name on the list, and the loaf itself came stamped with the baker’s name pressed into the crust, so you knew whom to curse. We struck the goddess on our coins, Annona herself, the grain-supply made divine, so the mob could hold the promise of bread in its hand even when the granary was empty. Your man does not strike coins. He posts. The small marble is his mint, and he stamps it with the same word we did: SOON. He cut the bread-list too, as we did. We trimmed ours once from three hundred and twenty thousand to a hundred and fifty, but we needed a census, clerks, men at tables in every district. He cut five million from the list and needed no clerks at all. He turned the tessera into a form so tedious that the hungry struck their own names from the roll to be free of the paperwork. We needed a census. He needed only tedium. I bow.

And the morning ritual, the one I miss. Each dawn my clients queued at my door for the sportula, the little basket, a few coins, some bread, in exchange for their noise in the Forum when I required it. A patron bought his crowd one basket at a time. Your man has promised the sportula to the entire republic at once, two thousand coins, a check, soon, to every citizen. The basket has gone national. The queue is the whole country. The basket, I notice, has not yet arrived and the queue has not yet dispersed, which tells you the promise of the basket feeds the client better than the basket ever did. We knew this. We simply lacked the reach.

But the bread was never the art. Any fool buys grain. The art is the fuel that moves it, and here I set down my stylus and stared.

In my day, if the fleet did not sail, the city starved, and a magistrate could do nothing but pray to the goddess on the coin and hope the wind changed. The supply lay with the sea and the gods, and neither took instruction. Your man’s bread must also be moved by the black oil that drives your wagons, and that oil had grown ruinous on account of a war he is himself waging in the east, against Persia. Some things do not change, and the mob felt it again in the voting organ. So he picked up the small marble and called the king of the north, the cold empire, the one his own law, signed by his own hand three weeks before, had named the enemy. He bought the fuel from the enemy, lifted the ban, and announced to the mob that the oil was coming, in his words, in record numbers and fast.

Do you see what I am looking at? I could not command the wind. He commanded the enemy’s oil to sail twenty-five days before a vote, from a chair, between meals. Pompey was given command of the grain of the whole known world, and it was said to make him master of the earth. Your man did the same from a device in an afternoon, and the oil he summoned, when I had it reckoned, comes to a day and a half of what your wagons drink. This is the finest part, the part that proves these people are not my equals but my betters: the oil need not arrive. The announcement is the cargo. The price did not fall; it rose; and it did not matter, because the thing he shipped the mob was never oil. It was the news of oil. He feeds the city on the rumor of grain. I needed ships. He needs only to be believed for one more week than the truth takes to arrive.

Now. The circus. You have been patient, and the circus is always the reward.

I thought I knew spectacle. I bankrupted myself into debt that would make your eyes water to put three hundred and twenty pairs of swordsmen into the sand in silvered armor, for a dead father I barely knew, but really for the votes. We built arenas of marble for a hundred thousand souls, flooded one and staged a sea-battle in it, real ships, real drowning, and gave the mob, by the end, near half the year in games, so it would not think too hard about the rest. I believed we had reached the summit.

Children. We were children.

And yet we understood one thing these people have perfected past our dreams. We had teams, the Blues and the Greens, the racing factions, and men who had never held a sword would knife each other in the streets over a chariot’s colors, men who could not name their consul but could recite every driver’s victories back to the founding of the city. The emperor learned to wear the colors. He did not care which team won. He cared only that they cared because a man screaming himself hoarse for the Blues is not a man counting the price of grain. We could keep that fever alive for an afternoon, with horses, in a building. Your man keeps it alive in every waking hour, in every house at once, with no horses and no building at all.

For he built his arena on his own lawn. A cage for single combat on the grass of the first house of the republic, for his own birthday, every warrior falling by the knockout blow, and the mob that could not attend watched on the small marble, millions at once, for free. Here is the detail I will carry to whatever grave this age grants me: the city’s own clerk refused to record the combats, refused to let the victories count, because no one paid the city its fee of a hundred coins. A hundred. I tipped my barber more. They staged the greatest single combat in the history of the capital and decoupled it from the state entirely, so that the state was not even invited to write it down. We thought the games belonged to Rome. These people have privatized the circus so completely that Rome is not on the guest list.

You believe we built rooms for vomiting so we could gorge and begin again. We did not. The vomitorium was an exit, the passage that “spewed” the crowd out of the arena when the games were done. I mention it only because you have built the precise opposite: a passage that spews the crowd in and never lets it leave, running day and night into every house. That one is real, it is in your pocket, and it has no door.

And the emperor himself. We killed one of ours for this. Commodus, who shamed the purple by going down into the sand as a gladiator, and we senators sat in the stands chewing the laurel from our own wreaths to keep from laughing, because to laugh was to die. When he was strangled in his bath we struck his name from the records and called him forever “the gladiator,” as the worst insult we had. Your man came from the sand. He fought in the staged combats before he ruled, body-slammed a rich man in a ring, shaved the man’s head, flung coins into the crowd with his own hands. And they struck his name from nothing. They made him first citizen because of it. In Rome the arena was where an emperor went to fall. Here it is the ladder. I knelt. A Roman magistrate, in the dirt, before a man who learned statecraft in a wrestling ring. I am not ashamed.

Caesar, forgive me, you have no name I am permitted, so Caesar you will be, you did not invent any of this. You merely removed the shame. We kept the shame as a kind of tax on the thing, a toll the conscience charged. You abolished the toll, and the traffic, I must report, has never moved so freely.

There is an adviser here who gave your age the one line I would carve in stone. Asked how to handle the scribes who tell the mob the truth, he said: you flood the zone. You put out so much, so loud, so fast, so many cages and feuds and announcements that no single truth finds purchase. We did this too, with our half-year of festivals, but we did it with calendars, with buildings, a festival at a time. He does it from a chair, hourly, at no cost, and it never sleeps. We had a maxim for the whole enterprise, old even then: mundus vult decipi, ergo decipiatur. The world wishes to be deceived; therefore, let it be deceived. We said it with a shrug. He has built a machine that says it a thousand times a second.

What humbles me is not the scale. Not the speed. It is the totality.

Because here is the one wall my Rome could never breach, and these people have walked through it as if it were smoke. My mob knew. The poet sneered panem et circenses, and the mob read it and sneered back; they knew the games were games, the bread a bribe, and took the bribe with open eyes and open contempt, a bargain struck between cynics. We fed and entertained a people who understood they were being fed and entertained. It was a kind of honesty. A filthy one. But honest.

These people have built a circus so complete that the audience no longer knows it is in the stands. The mob does not take the bribe with contempt. It takes it with tears, with gratitude, defends the cage on the lawn as a revolution, thanks the man slaughtering its cattle, cheers the oil that never sails. My Romans knew they were a mob. Yours have been convinced they are an army. That is the innovation. That is the thing I came two thousand years to see, and wish, now, that I had not.

I will not speak of the checks that never arrive, nor of the ballroom he raises while the granary empties, nor of the war in the east that lit the price of everything; I will not speak of these, for we would sit here until the lamps gave out and the slaves had gone to bed.

I will speak instead of a story we told our children for five hundred years, about Cincinnatus, who was handed the absolute mastery of Rome in its hour of need, won the war in sixteen days, laid the power down, and walked back to his plough. The glory was in the laying down. I have been here some weeks. I have heard them tell many stories. I have not heard that one.

We fell, you know. They will tell you the bread and the games are why. They have it backwards. The bread and the games are not the disease; they are the medicine you give a republic that is already a corpse, to keep it smiling, to keep it warm and fed and roaring in the stands, so that no one has to say aloud the thing that is true, which is that the voting stopped mattering long ago, and the games are what we do with the silence where the voting used to be.

I know the smell of that silence. I made my whole career in it. I am standing in it again, in a new language, under a light that comes from no flame, and it smells exactly, precisely, unbearably the same.

When the poet finished the line about bread and games, he wrote what came next, and your translators always stop before it because it is too dark even for them. He described the mob on the day a great man fell, chattering idly as the statues came down, and one of them says: “I hear many are going to die.”

And his neighbor, not looking up, answers: “nil dubium, magna est fornacula.” No doubt. The furnace is a big one.

I have to go. There is a spectacle this evening, and one is expected to applaud. I would not miss it for the world.

I never could.

Watching big companies scramble to glue together a stablecoin payments stack they never actually built together is painful.

At Polygon we’ve never had that problem. We built the Open Money Stack as one product from the very beginning, with one team and one roadmap. Even acquisitions immediately fit into it. 

When someone wants to talk about onramps and then has questions about wallets or cross-chain transfers, they stay with the same people. You want a custom chain, same team. You want dedicated blockspace, same team. You want a stablecoin checkout flow in your app, same team. You want an insanely crazy custom unique solution that requires multiple domain experts to work together--again, same team.

There’s no handoff, no separate wallet team or chain team or checkout team, and no one telling them to talk to someone else.

We’re smaller, we move faster, we're more global and we came out of crypto with deep payments experience already in the building. That combination is difficult to assemble after the fact, and it’s why the conversations we have with customers tend to stay in one place from the first call to the last.

text:
A gasless marketplace needs a relayer that can move assets for users. But granting that access should not silently become permission to move every user’s assets.

During a two-day security sprint for Plakxio, we found that its ERC-1155 badge contract reported every whitelisted operator as approved for every holder.

The whitelist restricted which badge classes an operator could move, but not whose badges it could take. The function that added settlement operators also accepted ordinary wallet addresses, so the trusted entry did not even need to be a contract enforcing signed orders.

There was another problem: a holder could explicitly revoke approval and receive a successful transaction and event, but the contract never read that stored refusal. The operator still appeared approved and could transfer the holder’s badges without a signature or payment.

The fix added three controls: settlement entries must contain contract code, new grants wait through an activation delay, and holder opt-outs are enforced on both single and batch transfers.

We re-ran every step of the proof of concept against the remediation and closed the finding.

text:
A user could create a subscription that the system could never charge, change, or cleanly remove.

A review Zealynx co-audited with Shieldify exposed the identity split behind that dead end in Bastion Wallet.

An EOA could register directly through `Initiator`, bypassing the expected `SubExecutor` entry path. The subscription was then stored under the EOA, while later operations looked for it under the SubExecutor.

Payment failed a second way: the recorded initiator and the caller expected by `processPayment()` no longer matched.

The High-severity finding was fixed by restricting those operations to `SubExecutor` and moving the core validation into `Initiator`.

text:
Thorsten Ball 这个问题很值得讨论：AI Agent 时代，我们为什么还需要 PR？

真正值得学习的不是直接 Push to Main，而是 Amp 用什么替代了传统代码审查：

受限的主干权限、签名提交、自动化 CI，以及可追溯的 Agent 工作记录。

我更倾向按风险分级：

普通 UI、内部工具和低风险功能，减少 PR 仪式，让 Agent 提供完整的运行证据。

涉及资金、交易执行、权限或关键基础设施的改动，仍然保留独立审查。

该消灭的是无意义的等待，不是质量责任与风险控制。
author: runes_leo
quoted_text:
Why are you still using pull requests?

Is it for code review?

If so, do you really think your or your colleagues catch bugs and mistakes that an Opus 5.5 or Fable or Astra won't find? You can literally spawn all three of them and have them check four times each.

(Also, don't tell me you don't have a "stamp plz" Slack channel or group chat somewhere.)

Is it for knowledge sharing?

Surely there's better ways for that now than the PR, no? We have models that can generate explainer videos, presentations, podcasts, games, quizzes, walkthroughs, ... for any piece of code it can reach. 

Is CI the reason?

Well ackshually, CI means continuous integration and its original meaning is the *opposite* of having long-lived branches and PRs.

But, leaving that aside, your agents are hopefully already running the tests before they push something, and hopefully they can run as long as they want and don't block you so they can run the whole test suite and generate "irrefutable proof" and end-to-end demo videos and so on... And so they run the tests and confirm and then you push to a branch and everything runs again and then you merge and then it runs again? That doesn't make sense, does it?

Maybe you work in open source and you accept contributions, in which case I can't speak to the value of pull requests. It's been 2 years since my last OSS contribution. But from what I heard, the time of the PR is coming to an end in OSS too?

I honestly don't get why people still stick to PRs.

With agents you can now move 10x faster, you can finally do real continuous integration, and get more confidence in the changes the agent made.

Don't slow yourself down by having all the changes pile up in a PR.

Crypto's next wave of growth could come from Wall Street moving onchain, with Backpack positioning itself at the center of tokenized stocks

“I'm an investor in Backpack”

“I think it's by far built the best tech for tokenized stocks”

“I think Wall Street's becoming more like crypto”

“What's happening with tokenized stocks is very promising”

“80% of it should come from tokenized stocks or real world assets”

“The aggregate volume that gets transacted on chain is not going to grow much”

“Eventually just call this fintech”

@santiagoroel expects the next five to ten years of onchain growth to be driven increasingly by assets originating outside crypto.

He has invested in @Backpack and rates its tokenized stock technology highly.

Through Backpack Securities, the platform is already connecting traditional stock ownership with tokenized securities on Solana, allowing eligible investors to move between brokerage holdings and onchain representations.

His broader thesis is that crypto-native assets alone may struggle to generate the transaction volumes needed for the industry to expand significantly.

He suggests that tokenized equities and other real-world assets could eventually account for as much as 80% of onchain trading activity.

Hyperliquid's HIP-3 markets offer another glimpse of that direction, with perpetual contracts referencing commodities and other traditional assets attracting activity beyond conventional crypto pairs.

As more financial markets adopt blockchain infrastructure, Santiago expects the distinction between crypto and fintech to become increasingly blurred.

昨晚下跌的导火索是油价的加速上涨导致美股崩盘，疑似又一家重仓 AI 的基金被清算和上次Leopold类似的剧本

原油上涨原因源于，美国议员提出法案试图阻止特朗普与俄罗斯达成柴油协议，库存见底，油价大涨之后进一步引发美股大跌。

美股的跌幅已经是小型股灾，费城半导体指数，连续 8 个交易日下跌，创 2008 年以来最长连跌记录，引发 AI、半导体、存储股的连环下跌的导火索是 Coreweave 的债券问题，本周累计跌幅已经达到了25%

对于这次整个AI产业链的全面崩溃我们也做一个梳理，看看这一切是怎么发生的
1、长鑫研发的新技术取得关键进展动摇存储的定价，高溢价逻辑被动摇，存储板块包括长鑫自己都崩了

2、Anthropic估值预期缩水，增速继续明显放缓，影响下游的云订单，动摇整个AI交易的估值锚。根据最新消息 Anthropic原定于 10 月的 IPO 要延后，同时 2 万亿的 IPO 估值也会被压缩，最终定价会在 1.5 万亿～2 万亿。

3、CRWV债务风险飙升(崩塌前最关键的一块积木)，五年期CDS利差，创历史新高，隐含未来五年违约概率超过60%。部分债券价格跌破面值的80%，收益率升至15%至16%以上。

4、AI基建融资模式受到质疑，市场重新审视原先AI产业链投入了如此庞大的资金，其中有多少依靠持续借债？投入的回报率是否可以支撑的起年化 10% 以上的借贷利息？一旦需求收紧增速放缓，信用市场的紧张情绪将会蔓延向整个 AI 产业链

一系列连锁反应导致一家重仓 AI 的对冲基金，面临杠杆清算，全名Value Aligned Research Advisors。

根据持仓披露该基金管理资产91亿美金，2026 Q2（报告期 6/30，8/17 申报）
仓位总市值：401.1 亿美元
正股：167.3 亿美元
看涨期权名义：204.7 亿美元
看跌期权名义：29.1 亿美元

按照披露的仓位来看有 4 倍的名义杠杆敞口，具体持仓见图。作为风暴中心的 NBIS、CRWV、MU、INTC在持仓中占不小比例，承担了相当高的AI行业集中风险，按这持仓来看就算没有清算也是岌岌可危

这次 AI 崩盘震中是 CRWV 的债券问题，引发的连锁反应，如果CRWV债券收益率和CDS开始回落，AI 云止跌才代表风险结束

quoted_text:
Why I'm skipping Arcus, even though everyone on CT posting their ref links would have you believe it's the next gem

It's no secret that Arcus is a perp DEX built by the team behind dYdX. Most people remember dYdX for one of the biggest airdrops in crypto history. Naturally, that gives Arcus a bullish narrative and makes people want to farm points for a potential airdrop. So why am I sitting this one out? Below are my reasons, followed by a few closing thoughts. I'm not saying I have all the answers or telling anyone what to do. This thread is for information only

1. Constantly switching chains

2018-2020: dYdX was building on Ethereum. 2021-2023: StarkEx. Since 2023: Cosmos, with dYdX Chain. Since 2026: Robinhood Chain, with Arcus as a separate perp DEX from the dYdX team

Name a perp DEX that kept switching chains and ended up delivering a huge airdrop or exponential volume growth because of it. Recent examples of perp DEXs repeatedly changing chains have ended badly: SynFutures, Ethereal (Meridian), Perpetual Protocol, Synthetix Perps, Gains, Hibachi

2. They shut down the bridge, leaving some long-term holders unable to migrate or sell

As part of the move to its own chain, holders of the old ERC-20 token, ethDYDX, could swap it for native DYDX through a bridge. In December 2024, a governance vote approved ending support for that bridge by June 2025. A second vote in June changed the network parameters and shut off support. Someone could have held DYDX in a cold wallet for years, missed the announcements, and ended up holding a token with no remaining route to migrate into the active ecosystem. Holders posted collective appeals on the forum and asked for the bridge to be reopened. These were complaints from actual long-term holders, not just outsiders throwing shade.

The reported damage was around $25 million worth of tokens, affecting 45,000 holders. Institutions and exchanges, which received direct warnings, mostly migrated in time. Retail holders often weren't following the forum, where posts about the proposal had only hundreds of views, and missed the deadline. According to one of the people pushing to reopen the bridge, large holders openly said on the forum that removing retail’s tokens from circulation and getting rid of that extra supply benefited them. Effectively, burning other people's tokens to reduce supply, dressed up as a "decentralized decision."

3. Problems with the exchange’s infrastructure

Trading went down during the AWS outage in December 2021. In 2022, malicious packages were published through an employee's compromised npm account. In July 2024, the v3 website's DNS was hijacked, redirecting users to a phishing site that used Permit2 signatures to drain wallets. In January 2026, the official v4 client libraries on npm and PyPI were compromised, with attackers inserting wallet-stealing malware and a remote access trojan

In November 2023, one trader ran essentially the same play on dYdX twice within two weeks: build leveraged longs, then pump the token on spot. On SUSHI, he walked away with around $5 million. On YFI, open interest ballooned from $0.8 million to $67 million. When the price crashed, the exchange covered a $9 million hole, roughly 40% of its insurance fund. The team itself controlled this "decentralized" DEX's insurance fund, while margin requirements across roughly a dozen markets were manually raised after the fact, without a governance vote

dYdX was down for eight hours during the October 10, 2025 liquidation cascade, which wiped out $19 billion across crypto, the largest in its history. Worse, after the restart, the engine executed trades and liquidations at incorrect prices because of stale oracle data. Compensation was eventually paid: around $462,000 from the insurance fund. Getting that compensation through governance took weeks. This team has been building a perp DEX since 2018, yet it's still making mistakes you'd expect from some scam devs who vibe-coded a perp DEX website in a few days, like Dango or Hotstuff

4. Questionable moves from dYdX's founder

In late March 2024, the dYdX Foundation put a restructuring proposal to a vote: move the dYdX Operations Trust into a foundation in the Cayman Islands. The official reason was to protect contributors from the SEC, which was putting heavy pressure on DeFi at the time. dYdX didn't operate in the US, but US regulators had already pursued projects outside the country. A month and a half later, Antonio Juliano announced that he was stepping down as CEO for "personal and professional reasons." The timing, so close to the Cayman restructuring, immediately sparked speculation that he was running from regulators, though there was no direct evidence

In July, Bloomberg reported that dYdX was in talks to sell v3, the old Ethereum L2 version that had made it a market leader, to a consortium of major market makers, including Wintermute and Selini Capital. No completed deal was announced, and in October, v3 was simply shut down. Five months after leaving, Juliano returned as CEO. A couple of weeks later, he laid off 35% of the core team, explaining that "the company we've built is different from the company dYdX must be."

So, in 2024 alone, they moved the operating structure to the Cayman Islands, changed CEOs and brought the old one back, tried to sell the old exchange to market makers and shut it down three months later, laid off a third of the team, and lost their lead in the perp market, with market share falling from around 80% to under 7%.

Juliano now sits on Arcus's board and, in his own words, is responsible for strategy and long-term vision. Do you think Arcus can compete with the top five perp DEXs with someone like that on its board? You don't even have to look that far. Robinhood Chain already has a leader: Lighter. If Arcus fails to carve out its share of the market, are we going to watch the same drama unfold again?

5. Investors could earn fees on locked tokens

When dYdX Chain launched in 2023, the team heavily promoted the idea that "all trading fees go to stakers," paid in USDC. But there was an important detail: investors and the team could stake tokens that were still locked. They couldn't sell them, but they could collect a share of the fees. This is explicitly stated in the documentation. For a retail buyer, that was a pretty rough deal. You buy the token on the open market for the yield, then share those fees with a massive amount of insider allocations. The more locked tokens being staked, the smaller your share of fees per token

The main issue was how it was communicated. Fee sharing got plenty of attention, while the participation of locked investor tokens barely got a mention. It wasn't mentioned at all in the official launch posts. On top of that, staking payouts went live just two weeks before a major insider unlock. Blockworks covered this criticism in November 2023. The condition wasn't completely hidden, but plenty of people found out too late

6. Suspected insider moves in DYDX ahead of major events

dYdX postponed the unlock for investors, employees and consultants from February 3 to December 1, 2023. Around 150 million tokens, worth roughly $282 million at the time, were due to unlock, which would have doubled the circulating supply. The market reacted positively to the delay, but questions about insider knowledge followed. Back on December 26, 2022, an account that looked like an insider had already posted that the unlock would be delayed until v4 launched. The post was later deleted

As December 2023 approached, tokenomics news and the dYdX Chain mainnet launch helped send the token up 109% in a month, right before the unlock. Some in the community suspected the classic "pump before the dump." Arcus came with a similar pattern: DYDX rallied 40% in a day on a teaser for a "big announcement," then dropped 23% to $0.145 after the actual reveal. Make of that what you will

7. Paying for promotion on social media

There is confirmed information covering 2024-2026: dYdX allocated $150,000 to promotion through Kaito, and another $300,000 to developing and managing the VIP affiliate program over 12 months, starting in November 2024. Its own website also has a Master Agreement for Promotion and Marketing Services covering influencer campaigns and paid ambassadors

As for 2021-2023, the following is unconfirmed. Again, this is my own speculation. Remember how KOLs shilled DYDX in 2021 and called for $50-100? Some of them were the same paid shills who made fortunes from promotional posts. Of course, there may never be proof, and nobody is going to volunteer that they were paid to shill DYDX. But if dYdX openly used paid promotion in 2024-2026, what would have stopped them from doing it unofficially in 2021-2023, paying big influencers to push the token?

Look at the DYDX chart: from $28 to $0.1. Nothing about it looks organic to me. It looks like large investors spending years unloading on retail while people were being sold dreams of a $50-100 token. I have nothing against paid promotion itself. But when it looks more like an attempt to unload on retail than introduce people to your product, that's a red flag for me.

8. Arcus"s own points program

There was no point in being early to Arcus. Early users weren't what they needed. Their documentation literally said weekly points issuance would increase as platform volume grew. A points system without a fixed supply is a massive red flag to me. You can dilute points as much as you want, and nobody is going to keep track of it all. The funniest part is that, after CT started calling it out, they decided to change it and introduce a fixed supply after all. Watching them change the rules on the fly already makes me less interested in using the DEX

My main takeaway

The size of the dYdX airdrop was a product of market conditions, not proof of an outstanding product. Around the 2021 bull-market peak, plenty of projects had absurdly inflated FDVs: ICP at $150B, AVAX at $100B, DYDX at $28B, AXS at $45B, SAND at $25B, FTM at $11B and ENJ at $10B. Everything the dYdX team did between 2021 and 2026 has only reinforced my view that the project is terrible and the huge airdrop was a case of perfect timing

Now the team wants to cash in on that old hype through Arcus. But people have short memories. Nobody seems bothered by dYdX's history; they just remember the big airdrop. What the team actually did, and what kind of product they spent nine years building, apparently doesn't matter. I'm not going to say everyone is only in it for the ref fees and doesn't care about anything else. I write about perp DEXs myself, including ones where I see legitimate red flags. With Arcus, the red flags simply outweigh the green flags for me. That's why I'm skipping it

None of this rules out a good Arcus airdrop or a TGE in favorable market conditions. None of this changes the fact that the Arcus team is now much stronger than the dYdX team used to be. And none of this rules out Arcus becoming a top-five perp DEX by volume. Personally, though, I'm more bearish than bullish on Arcus. My reasons are above. Whether you trade there is up to you

text:
日本可能加速加息，如何影响全球风险资产

日本的加息节奏可能还会加快。今天 IMF 亚太部主任Krishna Srinivasan认为，日本央行推进货币政策正常化的方向是正确的，如果通胀超过预期，就可能需要更快加息，避免人们形成物价会持续更快上涨的预期。

日本央行9月已经把政策利率提高到1.25%，创31年新高，不少分析师预计年底前还会再加一次。

日本长期低利率，让日元成为国际市场重要的融资货币。部分投资者借入便宜的日元，换成美元等货币，再买入债券、股票等资产，争取获得高于借款成本的回报。如果日本继续加息，新借款和到期续借的成本就可能提高，同样的资产收益，扣掉利息以后能留下的钱会变少。

另外如果日元明显升值，没有充分对冲汇率风险的投资者，就需要拿出更多美元去买回日元还债。即便持有的资产价格没跌，换回日元后的收益也可能减少，甚至出现亏损。如果再遇到资产下跌或追加保证金，一部分资金就可能卖出资产、买回日元平仓，而集中买入日元又可能进一步推高汇率，让其他类似仓位也面临减仓压力。

这样，日本加息的影响就可能传到全球风险市场。直接使用日元融资的股票仓位可能先被调整。如果多个市场同时出现去杠杆，部分投资者还可能卖出其他容易变现的资产，补充现金和保证金，美股和 bitcoin:native 也可能受到波及。

加息预期变化越突然、日元上涨越快，留给这些资金调整的时间就越少。

text:
HOLY SHIT.

For crypto, this is one of the most insane posts of the year, but I'm guessing most people don't understand it.

Let me explain...

Bitcoin's accounts, and subsequently Ethereum's (and therefore every other EVM chain's), are built on a specific elliptic curve called secp256k1.

secp256k1 is a different elliptic curve from the one used across nearly every modern hardware device, including iPhones.

Modern devices mostly use a different curve called secp256r1, which is usually referred to as P-256 - one of the curves investigated in the article.

This mismatch has made it sooo difficult in the past to integrate crypto accounts natively into the security systems of modern hardware.

For example, Apple's Secure Enclave natively supports P-256, not secp256k1.

This has prevented crypto accounts from being able to use the same hardware protection as things like Apple Pay.

Same goes for the web with passkeys - WebAuthn uses P-256 signatures, which means Ethereum accounts using secp256k1 can't use them natively either.

But why did Satoshi do this?

The main theory for choosing secp256k1 was distrust of the P-256 curve - i.e. he thought there was an NSA backdoor.

A "backdoor" here basically means a secret, intentional weakness in the curve that would allow the NSA to exploit it and access private keys.

This was because P-256 was created with involvement from the NSA...

And the NSA provided a mysterious "seed" used to generate one of the curve's parameters without explaining where that seed came from.

This eventually transformed into a ~25-year-old mystery with a 5-figure reward for finding where this seed came from.

Claude figured it out in less than 30 mins. 

And the best part is its internal thinking was: "Hmm wait... is it suspicious that such an obvious thing wasn’t discovered in 25 years?"

The solution was stupidly simple - just the time the curve was created, put into a specific random number generator function.

This doesn't 100% prove there's no backdoor yet, but it provides strong evidence that this seed wasn't secretly engineered by the NSA.

And Claude did this with "just a simple prompt" in under 30 minutes.

text:
今天更新的 DeepSeek V4.1 Flash-1017，官方公布的 DeepSWE 成绩达到 77.0，超过 Opus 5 的 74.0 和 GPT-5.6 Sol 的 73.0；Automation-Bench 拿到 60.5，Opus 5 只有 50.3；Agents’ Last Exam 也是 35.4 对 28.6。

关键这还是 Flash，API 单价没有上涨，任务耗时和输出长度反而进一步下降。当然，部分复杂推理测试仍然落后于 Opus，但在 Agent 任务上，旗舰模型的优势已经没那么稳固了。

我觉得这次更新很值得注意的一点，是 DeepSeek 同时强化了自反馈 RL 后训练，以及对 DSH、CodeBuddy、WorkBuddy 等 Harness 的适配。

这其实说明了，对于大量实际应用场景，模型智能继续提升的边际收益正在迅速下降。

当一个便宜得多的模型已经能够完成任务，你再花几倍甚至十几倍的成本去换取更高的模型分数，对用户来说可能根本没有区别。反倒是 Harness 的设计、工具调用、上下文管理、任务执行的稳定性，越来越直接地决定最终交付质量。

这也意味着大模型厂商接下来的竞争会越来越深入到 Harness 和 Agent 产品层。谁掌握任务执行环境，谁就能获得最真实的反馈数据，知道模型究竟在哪一步犯错，再反过来指导后训练。更何况，这还关系到未来的模型分发入口。

我一直觉得，中国 AI 公司没必要照搬美国大厂那套疯狂堆资本开支、大力出奇迹的打法。前沿模型当然还要继续突破，但应用市场不会永远为那最后几分智能支付溢价。

DeepSeek 这次更新再次证明，把一个足够好的模型训练好、调度好、用好，比一味追求最强模型更有商业价值。

而对 Agent 创业者来说，便宜又够用的模型越来越多，接下来就更难把产品做不好归咎于模型了。

text:
AI 编程，要开始算人的时间了

AI 把代码写快之后，团队容易算错一笔账：少花了多少时间写代码，却忘了多花了多少时间阅读、确认、返工和救火。一个 Agent 跑完任务，接下来仍要判断：这次改动是否值得合并？

Claude Code 团队公开的审查实践，给了一把更实用的尺子：”减少每次改动消耗的人工时间，同时不增加回滚和事故。” 这里的人工时间，要把审查和出错后的修复一起计算。假如省下十分钟审查，换来两小时恢复，显然不划算。

我的建议是，给工作流分开记两本账：人的投入，包含审查、返工和事故恢复；交付的等待，记录 PR 卡在哪一环。前者看人忙了多久，后者看多久能交付。等待时间不能直接算作人工工时，却同样值得优化。先量出成本，再决定该加一道检查，还是删掉一轮无效往返。

交付应该自带证据。测试怎么跑、返回了什么、关键场景有没有验证，都应该跟着改动一起交上来。验证尽量发生在提交 PR 之前，再由一个新上下文的子代理复审。这样，人打开 PR 时，可以直接判断证据够不够，不用重新调查一遍。

证据还要能解释自己的盲区。测试通过覆盖了哪些行为？没有覆盖什么？一个检查全绿的 PR，也可能在需求理解、权限边界或真实使用场景上出错。验收者需要知道，这份证据究竟能支持多大的结论。

人工注意力则要跟着风险走。文案修订与自动更新器，当然不该消耗同样的审批成本。但轻量审批有可信作者、自动检查通过等前提，指定敏感路径仍必须人审。对个人开发者，我建议保留一条底线：方向、架构和风险边界，由自己做决定。

审查本身，也可能成为浪费。文章提到，一个 PR 在夜里经历了五十多轮审查与修改，最后由作者叫停。一条轻微意见，也可能让 Agent 再改一次、再审一轮。团队加入了收敛规则：三轮后退一步重想方案，前几轮后只复查新 diff，已报过的问题不重复。

这意味着，Agent 工作流还需要判断是否继续的依据。每轮检查都值得追问：“发现了什么真实问题？改变了哪个决定？继续检查还有多少收益？”评论变多、轮数变多，都不能单独证明质量变好。

撤回能力也要提前准备。小步改动、功能开关、分阶段发布，让错误更容易发现和修复；已经发生的事故，再沉淀为每日重跑的评测，检查审查器有没有进步。

下次验收 Agent，除了问“做完了吗”，再加一句：这套流程，究竟替人省下了什么？

text:
我看到有小伙伴在留言区问我，为什么有主业工作还能码出 27 万条的推文。

首先，码字对我来说是一种休息，也是一种娱乐，我这人挺宅的，除非是很好的朋友或者是业务，否则不会出门，所以时间就比较多，而且我也喜欢码字，娱乐时间对我来说就是码字的时间。

其次，虽然我有主要工作，但这些工作对时间的消耗并不多，反而是对精力的消耗非常大，而对我来说，码字的反而是回复精力，就像是打坐一样，所以有时候工作非常疲劳的时候我反而喜欢码字。

然后，27万条大多数都是回复，我是非常喜欢回复的人，在评论区没有被 AI 占领的时候我几乎没一篇评论都会回复的，即便是现在，我也会尽量回复看上去是真人的评论，可惜，太少了。

很多小伙伴和我说码字是一件辛苦事，经常坐在电脑前一个小时打不出来 50 个子，这点我还算有点优势，我几乎不存在坐在电脑前不知道写什么的状况，反而是总觉得时间太少，很多想写的没时间写。

我估计会有小伙伴问道 AI 的问题，其实是不是 AI 写的目前还是能看出来的，当然我觉得 AI 写的问题也不大，但不能全部都是 AI ，自己都不知道写的是什么肯定不行，如果是让 AI 辅助找数据或者是编辑问题也不大。

关键的还是在你写的内容到底想要对阅读者传输什么，这才是最重要的，也就是你写的东西的灵魂是什么，很可惜，AI 写的内容往往就是缺少灵魂。

一个 @Gate ，交易更多市场
