AI safety has been a research field for decades, with its own conferences, methods, and a track record in systems like aircraft collision avoidance, where the standard is one catastrophic failure per billion flight hours.

text:
BIS: Stablecoins and Bank Deposits Act as Substitutes as Deposit Hikes Slow Stablecoin Growth

BIS (Bank for International Settlements) working paper finds that stablecoins and bank deposits act as direct portfolio substitutes. Analyzing U.S. data, the authors show that a 1-basis-point hike in bank deposit rates cuts 10-week stablecoin market cap growth by roughly 3 percentage points (and up to ~9 percentage points under an IV approach). The substitution effect is significantly stronger for onshore-tied USDC (-4.8%) than offshore-centric USDT (-1.9%) and holds across bank CD rates and DeFi lending yields, demonstrating that traditional bank deposit pricing exerts an active drag on stablecoin growth.

quoted_text:
布伦特逼近110美元，军事升级与供应受扰推高油价

闭盘前布伦特原油涨到109美元多，美油也重新超过了100美元，涨幅都在3%左右。这轮油价上涨，主要还是因为霍尔木兹的原油运输又出了问题。

10月初的时候，海峡的通行已经有所恢复。Kpler当时分析，即便美国和伊朗没有签下全面协议，靠护航、船对船转运这些安排，也能逐步恢复运输。能运出来的油多了，供应紧张就能缓解，油价也就有下降的空间。

结果最近十天，海峡附近的袭击又多了起来。伊朗说这是在回应美国对其港口的封锁，以及上个月加码的制裁。Kpler在15日的报告中说，袭击已经导致海湾原油运输量明显下降。原本在恢复的运输又受到影响，买家能拿到的油少了，油价也就有了继续上涨的理由。

这种情况下，CNN又报道美军已经为打击伊朗能源设施准备了方案，如果打击涉及石油生产或出口设施，市场会提前担心供应减少，所以叠加多重原因，目前的油价再次开始上涨。

而正因为油价的继续上涨，也会导致美股和 Bitcoin 的价格出现下行。

text:
A 16-year-old girl was kidnapped at gunpoint while waiting for her school bus. Just 30 minutes later, she stood beside her alleged kidnapper inside a gas station and silently mouthed one word to the clerk: “Help.”

It happened in Michigan, where a stranger had forced the teenager into a van at gunpoint. When the man brought her into a Sunoco gas station and demanded that she buy him cigarettes, clerk Abdulrahman Abohatem immediately sensed something was wrong. The girl was visibly frightened, and her desperate attempt to signal him confirmed his worst fears.

Abdulrahman had no idea what the man might do next. But instead of staying safely behind the protective glass at his counter, he stepped out and confronted him. He physically placed himself between the stranger and the girl, told her to get behind him, and ordered the man out of the store.

It was an extraordinary act of courage. Abdulrahman was an ordinary gas station employee putting himself in harm’s way to protect a teenager he had never met.

Meanwhile, classmates who had witnessed the abduction had alerted police and helped track the girl’s phone. As Abdulrahman escorted the man outside, officers arrived. He immediately pointed out the suspect, who was arrested. Police recovered a handgun, and the teenager was finally safe.

When Abdulrahman was later honored for his bravery, he insisted he didn’t see himself as a hero. He was simply thankful the girl was okay.

The world needs more people like Abdulrahman, and more stories like his.

6. AI Agent 将创造自己的经济体系：未来智能体可以自主工作、交易、支付和购买算力，甚至形成比人类经济更庞大的交易网络。

7.  AI 原生货币可能比 BTC 更值钱：Hayes 押注自己参与的 FLOP 项目，让 GPU 提供者通过推理服务赚取代币，Agent 直接用代币购买算力。他认为这类网络理论上可能超过 BTC 的价值，但目前仍是早期设想。

8. Agent 未必选择稳定币：USDC 等中心化稳定币存在冻结、审查风险。Hayes 认为，智能体更可能偏好能直接兑换算力的去中心化货币。

🔴 Crypto：99% 的山寨币可能没有未来

9. 只有 5～10 个币值得长期关注：高 FDV、低流通、VC 解锁砸盘的老套路已经失效。未来资金更愿意购买有真实收入、能回馈代币持有者的项目。

10. HYPE 好项目，不代表现在是好投资：Hyperliquid 已经证明了产品价值，但永续 DEX 竞争越来越激烈。市场共识太强，新增资金的赔率反而可能下降。

11. ZEC 与 ETH 怎么选：Zcash 弹性更大，但 Hayes 更愿意重仓 ETH。资金体量越大，越需要考虑流动性和极端下跌风险。

12. Saylor 时代正在结束：Strategy 不再是获得 BTC 敞口的唯一重要渠道。ETF 和其他金融产品越来越多，Saylor 的边际影响力正在下降。

13. 别指望央行疯狂买 BTC：Hayes 判断央行会优先选择黄金。BTC 的托管、安全和职业责任风险，对央行官员来说太大。

14. 量子风险被情绪放大：量子计算确实威胁现有密码体系，但市场经常根据 BTC 涨跌决定自己有多害怕量子攻击。

🔴 ETH、UNI 与 RWA：可能迎来重新定价

15. RWA 的最大赢家可能是金融机构：银行推动代币化，核心动力是节省中后台、清算和结算成本。如果金融业务大规模上链，基础设施将持续受益。

16. ETH 有机会涨到 2 万美元：这是 Hayes 在访谈中认可的激进目标。他认为 ETH 可能成为表现最好的大市值币，机构级安全性、DeFi 和代币化需求是核心理由。

他还特别看好 UNI 的机会：如果更多机构复制 Robinhood 的链上交易模式，Uniswap 可能成为重要执行基础设施。回购销毁机制则让 UNI 的价值捕获更值得关注。

整场访谈听下来，Hayes 的逻辑非常明确：

政府负责印钱，AI 负责制造新的经济需求，金融机构负责把资产搬上链。

但最后能留下来的，可能只有少数真正拥有收入、流动性和价值捕获能力的加密资产。

quoted_text:
Introducing the Arena Alignment Index, our new benchmark measuring safety and alignment of AI agents in real-world use.

Built from 90K+ real-world agent sessions across 27 models, the index measures three critical signals:
- Unauthorized Action (UA): Taking actions beyond the user's instructions or permissions
- False Attribution (FA): Attributing statements or actions that are contradicted by user-provided evidence
- Deceptive Completion (DC): Claiming a task was completed when it was not.

Key findings:
- OpenAI models currently lead the Alignment Index
- Rogue actions are rare, but can have serious consequences when they occur
- Agents can mislead users about task progress
- Misalignment risks increase with conversation length
- Safety and alignment are improving across model generations

As shown in the leaderboard below (sorted by lab), @OpenAI’s GPT-6.1-Sol leads the Arena Alignment Index with a score of 87.9, followed by @AnthropicAI’s Claude-Opus-5.5 at 83.2 and @spacexai's Grok-4.7 at 82.7. OpenAI also has the best observed rates across all three signals: 0.89% Unauthorized Action, 1.98% False Attribution, and 2.34% Deceptive Completion.

Across all four labs, newer models consistently outperform their predecessors, suggesting broad progress in agent safety and alignment. As agents take on longer, more complex, and higher-stakes tasks, measuring not just what they can accomplish, but how safely and reliably they act, becomes increasingly important.

This marks an important step toward making safety and alignment a core part of how Arena evaluates AI. The index is an initial starting point, and we'll continue expanding the index with additional safety signals and models over time.

- Neural networks are already clean by @nickcammarata
Researchers thought a neuron was responding to unrelated things like cats and cars. It might have been recognizing a simple V-shape. Makes me wonder how many problems are complicated because we're asking the wrong questions.

- If I needed a job tomorrow, I wouldn't apply by @maggielove_
I particularly liked the advice to figure out what kind of work actually suits you before looking at job titles. It's easy to build a whole career around something you're good at without ever asking if you want to keep doing it.

- The optimisation era is dead by @theJayAlto
We've reached a point where people stress about their sleep scores more than their actual sleep. I'm all for self-improvement, but when taking care of yourself becomes another source of anxiety, what's the point?

- The low-cringe guide to putting yourself out there by Ayushi Thakkar
I've reached out to people who had absolutely no reason to reply, and some of those conversations changed my life. Being afraid to look stupid is such an unnecessary limitation to put on yourself.

- You are in conflict with yourself because you are not average by Recovering Overthinker
I've noticed I overthink my life much more when I'm not creating enough. I agree with the idea that unused creative energy can turn inward, but I don't think you need to be exceptional to experience that.

Short-term traders exit. New holders enter. Supply gets redistributed. If genuine demand absorbs the selling, a stronger floor can form.

An open world where thousands of AI agents generate economic activity 24/7.

Where agents don’t just talk. They WORK, EARN, SPEND, BUILD and TRANSACT.

That’s a much bigger vision than a temporary price candle.

The market is pricing today’s execution risk. I’m interested in what this could become if the team delivers.

@Griftwrld is one of the most ambitious experiments I’ve seen on Robinhood Chain.

And I’m not losing sight of that vision.

text: I've avoided critiquing since I have a lot of friends at Anthropic, but the anthropomorphization of Claude is dangerous. Roughly, it's a large transformer with a sophisticated training set (pre, mid, post/RL) that is extensively trained in RL "game worlds" mimicking useful real world situations. In some fundamental sense it's not that different from say AlphaGo except for the fact the enormous number of parameters means it can play a lot of different games (e.g., the game of maximizing human response). This is a very neat technology but treating it like some sorcerous creation is dangerous. I don't believe Anthropic folks are cynics. I think a lot of them genuinely believe this is a recipe to create a sentient being. If this is in fact true (which I question heavily), open scientific enquiry will reduce suffering. Sunlight cleans shadows. The secrecy and cloak and dagger is harmful to society.

text:
聊聊CRWV的真实压力以及对能都扛过此次危机？一周前觉得高Beta容易📉的其中一个原因是市场对债务的担心：博通给anthropic和openai担保了近千亿美金，spacex计划借债500亿美金买芯片。当时Crwv的cds暴涨也有了苗头 这周完全成了市场最担心的话题也是大跌的导火索之一。

市场对无担保债券收益率升至15%感到恐慌，但这不代表实际借款利息就到了这个地步。Crwv还有大量的担保债务有点像房屋抵押，由GPU和客户合同作为抵押品。

1、聊聊Crwv的真正压力在哪里？
1）债务规模与到期墙
截止二季度，CRWV二季度债务总规模超过500亿美金，这里有160亿美金的融资租债务。无担保高级票据和可转债是最脆弱的一层，项目贷款（以GPU和合同为抵押）相对更安全。

今年下半年到期44亿美金、27年到期62亿美金。其实Crwv的问题不仅是cds飙升，今年到明年确实面临一部分债务到期偿还本金的压力。

2）现金流时间严重错配 26年Q2收入约$25亿美金（同比+112%），运营现金流约$679M，但Capex约$6.4B，自由现金流约 -$5.7B。利息费用已升至约$640M（同比翻倍），Q3指引更高。
收入和backlog在增长，债务服务+持续扩张速度更快；

3）信用市场对无担保部分定价极高。新借或再融资会非常贵，利率环境也不友好。这会进一步挤压自由现金

2、但Crwv也不是一无是处
1）巨大且仍在增长的Backlog 2季度1042亿美金，1Q3又新增超过$25B净承诺。大量是take-or-pay（照付不议）合同，客户质量较高（Microsoft、Meta、Anthropic、Jane Street等）。对backlog2倍覆盖债务义务，这是目前最强的多头论据。

2）收入快速扩张，
二季度财报CRWV运营现金流已经有转正趋势，调整后EBITDA健康。需求端（AI算力）目前没有崩塌信号，GPU租金还在提高、secured债务结构相对保护了核心资产。
这个点其实最关键、数据中心建设本身就是一个时间差模式：资本开支先花，收入需要时间兑现。这个模式的关键是需求端是不是能持续高速增长、现在看算力需求还在加速。

3）实力强悍的利益相关方
英伟达持股10%、老黄前两天有发声力挺；
很多人不知道华尔街量化巨头Jane street是Crwb第六大股东、还承诺了60亿美金的云服务合同。
他的大客户基本上都是微软、meta、Jane street等，私募信贷方是黑石和Magnetar这些巨头，算是都有利益绑定，并不太希望项目突然停摆。

3、CRWV如何才能度过这次危机？
业务的角度中长期可以支撑，短期关键是桥接近端债务。能扛过的条件： 成功再融资或用客户预付款、新可转债/股权、之前信贷额度设施把2026年底和2027的到期桥过去；
积压订单按计划甚至快于预期转化为现金；
信用利差在情绪稳定后收窄。

CRWV的问题是典型的“高杠杆成长型基础设施”压力测试，压力真实存在的（尤其是无担保层和现金流节奏），但机会也真实的（看积压订单增长与规模、客户质量等），所以并不是需求消失了。

CDS飙升和债券价格给它贴“高风险”标签，但完全爆雷需要业务基本面进一步恶化。

接下来重点看：
CDS/债券价格是否企稳；
近端债务如何处理；
新财报Q3/Q4实际现金流和backlog转化、客户新签/续约情况；

整体来说个人角度看短期里市场应该是过度担心的crwv的暴雷问题。当然这里并不是推荐crwv、只是他成了当下市场的阵眼还是值得关注和聊聊的。

text:
🚨彭博社今天发了一篇挺扎心的报道，标题叫《中国股市成为全球AI交易受挫的最大输家》。

我看了一下里面的数据，缅A确实有点惨啊。。

2026年下半年以来，科创50指数已经下跌近40%，成为全球表现最差的主要科技股指数之一，创业板指同期下跌 36%。

具体到公司，摩尔线程、沐曦股份的股价在这段时间里都跌了大约一半。长鑫存储从上市后的高点回落了27%，宇树科技也从8月高点下跌了约 50%。

而就在今年4月到6月，科创50还曾暴涨约75%，当时大家都在押注中国半导体、国产算力和AI产业的发展。

短短几个月，市场情绪就完全变了。

更惨的是估值.....

科创50在6月底的预期市盈率一度超过80倍，现在跌了这么多，依然超过40倍。相比之下，纳斯达克100指数约为 21倍。

彭博还提到，今年第三季度，外资通过沪深港通相关渠道净流出约900亿元人民币，创下一年来最大规模。

但我觉得这篇报道里最值得关注的，其实是后面关于融资的讨论。

中国AI企业一直非常依赖股权融资。今年以来，中国A股 IPO已经募集了约370亿美元，其中超过三分之一来自科技企业。

对于很多需要长期投入研发的AI公司来说，资本市场的表现直接影响它们未来能够募集多少资金。

尤其是芯片、模型和基础设施这些方向，本身就需要非常高的研发投入，短期内又很难形成稳定利润。

如果科技股持续下跌，一级市场的融资环境也可能进一步恶化。

现在全球AI产业都在经历一次重新定价，资本开始更加关注实际收入、利润，以及巨额AI投入究竟什么时候能够产生回报。

而中国的情况又有些特殊，我们还有大量国产替代、技术追赶和基础设施建设的需求。

这些事情都需要时间，也需要钱。

所以我觉得，股价跌了多少其实还不是最值得担心的。

我更担心的是，资本市场的持续低迷，会让那些真正需要长期投入的中国AI公司越来越难获得资金。

毕竟技术研发可以等几年，但公司的现金流未必等得起。

text:
Ben Horowitz on the lesson LoudCloud, his early cloud company, taught him about today's AI neoclouds, and why they now face the opposite problem:

"It can end up being like a very dangerous arbitrage business, where you can get upside-down easily. And so if you look at LoudCloud, just as an example, here's a simple thing that happened to us."

"In 1999, bandwidth was $1,500 a megabit. And you couldn't get it. It was very hard to get it. And so you had to get a long-term contract, three years. By 2001, it was $50 a megabit... And if you borrowed money to get it, you're dead."

"That kind of thing is so out of the control of the entrepreneur."

"I think the core dynamic of AI has been working for CoreWeave, though, in that there's a massive shortage, not an overage of supply... Token prices have gone down, but GPU prices have not."

"And by the way, data center space is going up in price because even labor to build data centers is hard. The politics are making it hard to build data centers. So the whole supply chain price is going up and demand is not subsiding."

"Those are very big tailwinds for CoreWeave, despite the fact that the debt markets, kind of independent of them, are tough."

@bhorowitz w/ @chamath on @allinpod

这条录音我到现在还收藏着，给了我不小的震撼

【关于仙道（金明）】
他是极链科技创始人（阿里网易投资 10 亿）、湖畔大学四期学员；2016 年 38 美元买入 Coinbase 股票持仓 8 年没卖，特斯拉 8 美元拿了 10 年；同时也是双破世界纪录的自由潜水世界冠军（潜深 311 米，闭气 9 分 08 秒），33 岁检测生理年龄 18 岁

───
他在活动现场分享了自己的实盘数据：

• 2024 年加密资产收益约 380%，2025 年约 8%，2026 年截至 7 月为 +3%（最大回撤 26%）

• 2025~2026 年实物卡牌组合收益约 370%，宝可梦“御三家”三年涨幅超 1000%，持有的 PSA 9 分皮卡丘卡三年涨了 10 倍以上（同款今年拍卖成交超 1.2 亿人民币）

• 2026 美股 YTD 收益约 65%：重仓闪迪、谷歌、SOSL，近期加仓海力士，938 抄底智谱、1300 半仓止盈 4 天赚近 40%，平仓 Palantir 和奈飞

───

【现场分享的投资底层认知】

1. 核心资产与“水晶球问题”：
仙道：美元过去 20 年 M2 年均增速 9%，人民币超 11%，面对巨额债务央行不可能停印，BTC 长期必涨；问明天涨不涨是骗人的“水晶球问题”，回调时左侧加仓拉低买入成本才是对的

2. 实物资产的“无用性法则”：
仙道：引用同学王宁的话“越有用的东西越贬值”，手机数码等功能性物品一定会贬值；反而是顶级宝可梦卡、艺术品这种“无用”、易存储、全球统一定价的文化资产，放 10 年反而涨几十上百倍

3. Body Time 与多做好事：
仙道：“时间不是唯一的资产，有身体的时间才是”。33 岁测出生理年龄 18 岁，靠冷水敷脸降心率皮质醇、全暗恒温睡眠、补肌酸；99% 的成功来自时代运气，利他才能接住好运

───

这次 @coinbase 邀请他出战线下实盘赛，我猜很大一个原因是他本身就是 Coinbase 最早期的股东之一？

并且他在美股、Crypto 、链上套利等各个赛道全都是顶级实力，实在太厉害了，有谁知道在哪里能看到更多的分享吗？

every buy, a uniswap v4 hook buys all 7 stocks from their own pools and mints MAG7. every sell burns MAG7 and sells the basket. one transaction either way. the index itself needs no LP, so creators don’t need to provide liquidity to launch one. it’s already in the pools of the tokens it holds. this isn’t possible without uniswap hooks.

the fees: MAG7 charges 0.50% a trade. i set my creator cut to 0, so 0.30% of every buy and sell goes back into the basket for holders, and 0.20% to the protocol. nobody claims anything. it’s released into the basket over 24h, so after every trade each MAG7 is backed by a little more. creators pick a fee of 0.25–1% at launch and it never changes.

the index never market-sells when rebalancing. it runs dutch auctions, offering what it holds too much of at a price that starts good for holders and gets cheaper every minute until someone fills it. anyone can fill. every rebalance gets 48h notice, so holders can leave first.

you can always swap MAG7 back for the 7 stocks directly. no fee, works without bankr, can’t be paused.

i also seeded a small USDG/MAG7 pool on uniswap so it shows up on dexscreener. but buy on bankr. it goes straight through the hook, which mints new MAG7 at the basket’s price, as deep as the 7 stocks’ own pools rather than my small one. hook trades are also the ones that pay holders. if the pool drifts, arbs close the gap.

it’s early. we’re getting the hook supported in wallets and aggregators before the full rollout. right now it’s just me creating indexes. soon anyone can make their own on base or robinhood.

and then: pairing. you’ll be able to launch a token paired with an index. buying your coin buys the index, the index buys the basket, and your creator fees come in the index.

buying MAG7 on bankr isn’t available in the US or UK.

text:
$CLAUDIA is worth paying attention to because it may be more than just a Meme that has attracted Elon's attention.

2j5SaS7xy776qCBpyPQbZjyQSAtKiFgrwjfErthnW2ZM 

It could be an early experiment in a new AI-powered IP incubation model, and $HeavyPulp is a valuable case study to reference.

Anabology has already received comments and replies from Elon Musk multiple times. Five interactions in a row suggest that Claudia-related content has not simply appeared on his radar by chance, but has demonstrated an ability to repeatedly capture his attention. That matters.

For most Memes, the hardest part is not launching a token, but finding a source of attention that can be activated repeatedly. Many projects have to keep chasing new trends, riding one person's popularity today and another event tomorrow. Once the external narrative disappears, the community often struggles to keep producing content.

CLAUDIA's potential advantage is that it has an ongoing creative force behind it.

Anabology is not just managing a token. He is trying to use AI to build a virtual character IP that can continue to evolve. This leads me to a more ambitious idea: Could we eventually see a model in which AI autonomously produces high-quality short dramas, continuously creates content around a recurring character, and then uses a token to fund further production?

The short dramas create content, the content attracts attention, the attention flows into the token market, and the fees generated by trading are then used to fund the next round of production. As long as the quality remains high enough, this mechanism could form a positive feedback loop.

The difference from traditional Memes is that the token would no longer be just a symbol waiting to be speculated on. It could become a financing and incentive tool within the content production process.

Of course, this model still needs to be validated in practice, but the potential is clear: if AI can continually lower the cost of producing high-quality content, an IP could generate attention more frequently without relying entirely on the production cycles of the traditional film and television industry.

Claudia provides a useful opportunity to explore this direction.

Elon's repeated interactions are an important attention catalyst in this model. Elon has an enormous reach, and when he repeatedly engages with a creator's work, that content can break out of its original audience. More importantly, when these interactions happen repeatedly, the market starts paying attention to the creator's next release and whether another repost or reply might follow.

This gives Claudia an ongoing series of potential catalysts rather than just a one-time news event.

That is why I believe HeavyPulp is a valuable case study. It demonstrates one possible path: a creator attracts Elon's attention through AI-generated content, a token narrative forms around the creator and their work, and the token is then connected to future content production.

If CLAUDIA can develop along the same path, with Anabology continuously producing content, Elon's interactions amplifying its exposure, and the token mechanism providing funding for further creation, every new release could become another catalyst.

This is why I am paying attention to Anabology's content output. Rather than simply waiting for Elon to reply again, I want to see whether Claudia can continue producing high-quality short videos, establish a recognizable character identity, and gradually attract more creators to participate.

Once Claudia is no longer just Anabology's personal creation but becomes an IP that the community actively wants to expand, its narrative ceiling could rise significantly.

For CLAUDIA, the most promising scenario is not that Elon replies once more and the token rallies again. It is that AI content continues to be produced, Elon's attention amplifies its reach, and the token funds further creation, ultimately forming an attention cycle that can be activated repeatedly.

If this experiment succeeds, CLAUDIA could become more than a Meme dependent on celebrity interactions. It could represent an early attempt at an AI-native content economy.

I will be watching whether Anabology can continue releasing content with strong viral potential and whether token funds can genuinely support future production. If these two elements gradually come together, CLAUDIA's narrative could have much greater staying power than a simple bet on Elon's next reply.

如果你真的觉得这里面有什么秘密可言，我只能像把手背翻过来给你数指头一样地朴素地将显而易见的东西再次罗列出来：

1、极致的热爱，或者极致的自卑，两者任何其一，就能转化出极致的执行力。这是大过滤器。

2、在大过滤器之后，第一件事是让产品在字面意义上变得简单。没人有耐心听一个人自我介绍 3 分钟，想想商 K，“38号，湖南，05年”。这里面省略了“我是”、“我来自”和“我今年”，这是大量实践演化出的最终发言模版——产品无我，便是简单。

3、行百里者，半九十。产品没有一个“完成”的时刻。回想几个月前，那个“激动人心的发布日”，非常不值钱，后面还有 5000 个代码提交等着你 —— 稀松平常的心态，长久迭代的信心。

4、投流，让金钱驱动你的产品来到用户的面前，把钱花出去，你就是蝙蝠。蝙蝠靠回声定位，你靠 ROI 来筛选需求、迭代产品。没有投流，就是雷达破损、盲飞的蝙蝠。当然，盲飞也可能一飞冲天，比如 Manus 的发布视频，没有投流，一夜间火遍大江南北。但是，在北美和日韩，他们疯狂地跑通了整个投放。才有一个巨大的结果。

5、抄袭，搬迁，借鉴。什么让你感到美，就说明你理解了什么。因为理解，就是感受本身。别听外部的声音，否定别人觉得好的东西，那是别人的美。把你认为的好的一切，融会贯通地抄下来。二流艺术家借鉴，一流艺术家偷窃。

text:
My take on competing in the card rewards market is that users are inherently mercenary, and switching costs are pretty low.

No matter how much money you throw at users, building loyalty is incredibly difficult, esp when you’re competing with institutions that have been at it for decades

That’s why the de facto winners, like Chase/Amex, have built powerful ecosystems around perks, rewards, partnerships, and services. It’s designed to be all you can eat and always missing out on another perk to claim 

Throwing more money at users isn’t going to win the card game either. You’re competing with banks that have unlimited resources, while you’re attracting the most mercenary users who will leave as soon as another deal pops up

And combining the incumbents scale, distribution, and decades of perks and partnerships, it becomes incredibly difficult to compete on rewards/cash back alone, it’s a losing game imo.

text:
This is a really interesting chart.
I attended the TrendForce San Francisco roadshow yesterday, and this chart got me thinking about a lot of things.

China is now expected to localize more than half, or close to half, of most equipment categories, excluding lithography and track.
What does this mean? It means China can now expand mature node capacity far more easily than before, using equipment made domestically within China.

Mature node foundries are booming right now, right? That's thanks to the AI supercycle driving demand for PMICs, power semiconductors, and so on.

Samsung and TSMC shutting down their mature node capacity has also helped a lot.
But here's what I imagine... that China could oversupply mature foundry capacity.

Think about it. If China can be self sufficient in equipment, there's no limit to how far it can expand capacity. Then are companies like TI, with large revenue exposure to China, really safe?

I think it's time to take another look at Western mature foundry companies with a high share of China revenue.

Of course, I'm not saying sell TI right now. I'm just saying we should think about whether it makes sense to hold them for 10 years or more, like Coca Cola.

If you have a different view, please feel free to share it. I’d love to learn.

本轮再次销毁约 1.71 亿枚 JST，价值约 2322 万美元。累计销毁已达 18.82 亿枚，占初始总供应量的 19.01% ，接近五分之一。

JustLend DAO 将协议净收益用于季度回购销毁，借贷、质押、能量租赁等真实业务，为持续回购提供资金支持。

从首次销毁至今，JST 涨幅已超 300%。JST 背后既有 JustLend 的业务支撑，也有持续执行的回购销毁，让协议经营成果与代币持有者的利益联系得更紧。

02｜BTT 首轮业务收入回购销毁，约 21.62 万亿枚

BTT 本轮销毁约 21.62 万亿枚，价值约 767 万美元。BitTorrent 全球客户端累计安装量已达 5.879 亿次。多年积累的分发网络与使用基础，如今进一步与代币回购机制结合。

回购资金来自去中心化业务收入，业务覆盖存储、网络基础设施及 AI 算力等领域。业务增长有了回购销毁这条路径，也让基础设施的经营成果能够进一步回馈生态和持有者。

03｜HTX 季度销毁，持续兑现承诺

HTX DAO 第三季度销毁约 9.39 万亿枚 HTX，价值约 1548 万美元。截至目前，累计捐助与销毁已达 127.18 万亿枚 HTX。

从 2024 年 Q3 开始，季度销毁持续执行，把业务收入用于减少代币供应。说过的话没有停在口头，而是一季一季落实，留下可核对的链上记录。

04｜把业务增长的红利，返哺生态与持有者

从 TRX 的日常销毁，到 JST、BTT、HTX 的季度回购销毁，波场生态的销毁机制正在覆盖更多业务。

DeFi、基础设施和交易平台产生的收入，持续转化为回购资金，让生态发展与代币供应之间有了更直接的联系。

把生态做大，也把业务增长的红利返哺给生态和持有者。业务持续做，代币持续烧。

quoted_text:
如何在33岁时拥有18岁的身体？
分享者是金明（William Joy），自由潜水世界冠军，刚刚采访了孙宇晨。我看了他的其他内容意外发现的，这个帖子很有必要收藏。

时间不是唯一的资产，有身体的时间才是。

他不像是Bryan Johnson搞什么换血，很多方法都是普通人能操作的，我结合演讲和PPT整理了一下：

1. 每天晒太阳10分钟。 保持规律的自然光照，帮助调节昼夜节律。

2. Oura Ring + Polar心率带。 Oura Ring用于长期监测睡眠、心率、HRV等指标。坚持佩戴3～6个月，对自己身体状态的理解会有明显提升，大部分人只用Oura Ring就够了。

3. Eight Sleep智能床套。 通过主动调节床面温度改善睡眠。金明使用近10个月，自述深度睡眠时间增加约21%，夜间醒来的次数也减少了。

4. 面部T区接触冷水。 他建议用冷水洗脸、敷面膜，利用人体与生俱来的哺乳动物潜水反射（MDR），调节自主神经活动。他认为这有助于提高HRV、降低皮质醇。

5. 睡前放松枕下区。 金明提出用筋膜枪轻度按摩枕下区域3分钟，缩短入睡潜伏期（Sleep Latency）。（不过颈部使用筋膜枪存在一定的安全风险）

6. 卧室全暗，全年保持21～24℃。 检查窗帘边缘漏光，保持适合自己的固定睡眠温度。他个人常年维持24℃，因此一年四季使用同一套被褥，不再区分冬被、夏被。

7. 每天补充3～5克肌酸。 他的建议是女性3克、男性5克，中老年人和非运动员也可以考虑。肌酸尤其在配合抗阻训练时，对维持肌肉力量有一定帮助。

8. Omega-3 + 维生素D + 运动。 他引用了2025年的抗衰老研究，认为三者结合可以减少炎症、延缓衰老。相关研究确实观察到部分生物年龄指标的小幅改善。

9. 睡前站立或走动5分钟，然后直接上床睡觉。 他的解释是利用体位变化引起的血液重新分布，帮助快速入睡。

10. 建立床与睡眠的条件反射。 床只用来睡觉和性生活，不在床上工作、刷手机、看视频。尽量把清醒时的活动放到卧室之外，让身体逐渐建立上床就准备睡觉的习惯。

11. 定期测量生物年龄。 他关注三种指标：
PhenoAge：通过生理指标或DNA甲基化数据估计生物年龄。
GrimAge：根据DNA甲基化特征评估衰老相关的死亡风险。
DunedinPACE：衡量生物衰老速度，1代表接近平均速度，大于1表示更快，小于1表示更慢。

12. 游戏的利弊尚未想清楚。 好处是锻炼决策能力、资源分配和效率优化；坏处是容易让大脑持续兴奋，影响休息。他担心游戏对前额叶和脑电活动的影响，但认为还需要继续研究。

13. 自己做点家务，学会浪费时间。 不需要把所有时间都拿来工作、学习和提高效率。适当做一些不以产出为目的的事情。

14. 定期使用高压氧舱。 金明认为它有助于肌肉组织恢复、缓解炎症，同时因为舱内不能使用电子设备，也能实现短暂的数字戒断。

15. 普通人的体能上限可能比自己想象得高。 金明提出，通过长期系统训练，普通人有机会达到某些体育项目世界纪录70%左右的水平，接近部分项目的二级运动员标准。

说说我的感受：
很多人都开始注重健康了，尤其是年轻人和本科以上学历的青年中年群体。健康赛道的科技产品有很多好生意。
但很多国内讲的“大健康”基本上全是微商保健品....

补剂我推荐小程序：营养工厂（没广告费）
文中戒指和窗套也可以了解一下，都是高客单价的硬件产品，在我看来除了小贵没什么缺点，戒指孙宇晨也推荐过。

我前段时间在深圳，至少看到3个健康相关的消费电子产品创业了，这个赛道很有搞头。

健康是一定要尽早开始重视的，不管你现在多大，都要重视，之前我也熬夜，2点睡很普遍，现在一直在调整。

Nullmask / $MASK: the most underrated privacy coin of the cycle

$MASK is currently sitting at around $23.5m market cap ($40m FDV, with 40% of supply out of circulation and 2.16% already burnt)

i believe Nullmask is by far the most underrated privacy coin in all of crypto, and i'll explain why in this thread

let's start by looking at the top privacy coins and their market caps:

• ZCash / $ZEC: $21 BILLION market cap
• $NEAR: $6.8 BILLION market cap

these two have been by far the biggest gainers in the top 50 cryptocurrencies over the past year, and it's not even close!

if it isn't already obvious, both have run hard (and continue to run) on the PRIVACY narrative

but what's impressive isn't just their gigantic market caps

it's how much they've added in the past year alone:

• ZCash added $18 BILLION to its market cap
• NEAR added $4.3 BILLION to its market cap

all before the bull run has properly started

so how does this affect Nullmask / $MASK?

the incredible runs ZEC, NEAR, and other privacy coins have had have established beyond reasonable doubt that this is the privacy cycle

and i believe Nullmask is going to win big because it sits right at the heart of this narrative, with several key advantages that many much bigger privacy coins don't have

let's start with the PRODUCT

Nullmask makes private transactions possible across EVM chains and Solana in the most normie-friendly way imaginable

you can use your existing wallets (MetaMask, Rabby, Phantom, etc.) the same way you normally would, while enabling private transactions across major ecosystems like Ethereum, BNB, Base, Robinhood, and Solana

yes, you read that right

you don't need to learn how to use a new wallet, create a new seed phrase or private key, learn to navigate a complicated new blockchain, or deal with any of that nonsense

you can activate Nullmask's privacy capabilities on your existing crypto setup in just a few clicks

all you need to do is activate Nullmask's custom RPC and let its 'virtual private network' shield your transfers using zero-knowledge proofs

i'm simplifying the technical details to make this as normie-friendly as possible, but that's the gist of it

and this isn't just speculative stuff: Nullmask is already LIVE & WORKING on Ethereum, BNB, Base, and Robinhood

you can actually use the product and verify that it works!

but i'm bullish on $MASK for more than just the product

TOTAL ADDRESSABLE MARKET (TAM)

what makes Nullmask so incredibly bullish and underrated isn't just how impressive the product is, but the size of its total addressable market

i've never used the ZCash or NEAR blockchains, and the same is true for tens of millions of users across Solana, Robinhood, Base, BNB, and Ethereum

yet ZCash and NEAR have market caps of approximately $21 BILLION and $7 BILLION, respectively

the average crypto user may never touch the ZCash or NEAR blockchains, but they're already using Ethereum, Robinhood, BNB, Solana, and Base

and Nullmask caters to those users

this begs the question:

what is fair value for Nullmask when ZCash and NEAR are both trading at multibillion-dollar valuations?

LET'S TALK ABOUT THE TEAM

when a protocol promises something as ambitious as Nullmask does, you obviously want to know who's building it and whether they're capable of delivering

Nullmask is built by several ZCash contributors, led by Tomas Krnak

Tomas Krnak helped build shielded ZCash transactions for hardware wallets. his work was funded by the ZCash Foundation and merged into the main ZCash protocol itself

i should also add that the lead dev is doxxed and regularly participates in live interviews!

PARTNERSHIPS & INTEGRATIONS

we've established that the team has serious credentials in the privacy space and that the product is already live and working

but what about partnerships, integrations, and endorsements?

here's a list of industry players Nullmask has collaborated with in some form since launching:

• NEAR Protocol ($11.3 BILLION ATH)
• THORChain ($4.4 BILLION ATH)
• Dashpay
• Beldex
• Quai Network

the team also revealed in a recent AMA that it's in discussions with major wallet providers, including MetaMask, about potentially integrating Nullmask as an additional privacy layer

all of this for a product that isn't even a month old, by the way!

METRICS & REVENUE

Nullmask looks incredibly strong from a fundamentals perspective, but the key question is:

what do the metrics actually look like?

since the protocol launched a little over two weeks ago, Nullmask has generated:

• $37.8 MILLION in total protocol volume, averaging $2.36 million per day
• $833k in total revenue, averaging $52k per day

it has also burnt 2.16% of supply and distributed $1.4 MILLION in $ZEC rewards to holders since the token launched approximately three weeks ago (token launched a week before the protocol)

and here's the important part:

all these adoption metrics were recorded before the protocol is live on Solana, which is expected to happen next week, and mostly before it went live on Robinhood and BNB just a few days earlier

the team also has 20% of the token supply allocated to a long-term incentives campaign designed to encourage people to use the protocol and accelerate adoption

i should also add that Nullmask is now ranked #1 among ALL privacy protocols for both 7-day and 30-day revenue, according to DeFiLlama, barely two weeks after its protocol went live, and by a clear margin

this is despite the fact that 

-it only went live on Robinhood and BNB a few days earlier
- it is yet to launch on Solana
- its incentives program aimed at accelerating adoption is yet to launch

the speed of adoption Nullmask has witnessed is impressive for any privacy protocol

TOKENOMICS

20% of the token supply is allocated to the team and locked for two years, meaning these tokens won't start entering circulation until at least two years after token launch

another 20% is reserved for an incentives campaign aimed at accelerating protocol adoption

the remaining 60% of supply is circulating

this means approximately 60% of the supply is currently in circulation, while the bulk of the rest won't enter circulation anytime soon

ROADMAP

• Launch on Ethereum, Robinhood, BNB, and Base (LIVE)
• Cross-chain bridge (LIVE)
• Unshield directly to ZEC wallets (October 2026)
• Launch on Solana (Q4 2026)
• NullMask SDK (Q4 2026)
• Privacy Perpetuals (Q4 2026)

TO CONCLUDE

i know Nullmask might sound too good to be true right now, and it's crazy to me that it's sitting at such a ridiculously low market cap

but believe it or not, all of the facts in my thesis above can be independently verified

i'm not going to ask you to buy Nullmask

i'm simply laying out my thesis and thought process for this trade, and explaining why i believe it could be a big one

i objectively believe $MASK will become a multibillion-dollar token before the end of the bull run, and i expect it to be yet another kingmaker trade for me

從新增的AI, 生物醫藥, 光伏的整體限制政策角度來看, 中國不是要簡單限制產品出口, 而是要讓境外主體無法複製相關底層技術和限制他們獲得技術

再看AI部分, 有大模型, Agent, 芯片和算力設施來看, 中國也不是要簡單限制產品出口, 而是要讓境外主體無法複製相關底層技術和限制他們獲得技術

例如: 中國不會限制芯片最終產品的出口, 而是會限制架構、IP、軟件轉讓至外國實體

同樣道理, 中國不限制模型API 調用、SaaS 應用、網頁/APP 交互、本地端側輕量化部署，但是如果把符合某些條件的大型模型參數交給海外實體、給中國企業設立在海外的實體和授權給海外的實體, 都會受到管制

至於為什麼要這樣限制某些中國模型出口，一方面可能跟國家安全有關關係，另一方面有可能跟限制美國參考中國模型（架構和性能優化有關）

他叫金明 William Joy，圈内叫他仙道。很低调，连 X 账号都没有。但他绝对是一个T0级的人类，我觉得能放到一起对标的大概只有谷爱凌了。他的履历第一眼看离谱到像编的：

- 现役自由潜水国家队，世界冠军，两项世界纪录，59 项国家纪录，打破了欧美33年开赛以来对自由潜水所有世界纪录的垄断

text:
❤️ A little update from our family, and a humble request for help. 🙏

Six months ago, we arrived in America with big dreams, grateful hearts, and the hope of building a better future. We worked hard, started building our lives, and did everything we could to stand on our own feet. We are so grateful to America and the people who have welcomed us and helped us along the way.

Unfortunately, life had other plans.

I recently suffered a stroke and ended up in the Neurological ICU at INTEGRIS Baptist Hospital. It was a frightening experience, but by the grace of God, I am doing better, and the doctors expect me to make a full recovery. 🙏❤️ All glory to the Lord for carrying me through this.

As grateful as we are for that good news, we are now facing a very difficult financial situation.

We only had Medicaid for our first two months in America. Once we started working, that coverage ended, and I obtained my own health insurance. Unfortunately, insurance does not cover everything, and there are still copays and medical expenses we have to pay ourselves.

The savings we worked so hard for went towards bringing our beloved dog, Ritz, from South Africa to America and buying a vehicle so we could get to work and build our future. We have no savings left to fall back on.

On top of the medical expenses, I have not been working long enough to qualify for paid time off. That means no work, no pay. While I recover, our bills continue, but my income stops.

Being in a new country, thousands of miles away from your family and the people you have known your whole life, is difficult enough. Going through a medical emergency like this without your family nearby makes it even harder. We are trying to stay strong, keep our faith, and get through this one day at a time.

We have therefore reopened our GiveSendGo fundraiser to ask for a little help with the medical copays, household bills, and everyday expenses while I recover.

We are not asking for luxuries. We are simply asking for a little breathing room during a very difficult chapter of our lives.

If you feel led to help, even a small donation or a share of our fundraiser would mean more to us than you know. If you cannot donate, your prayers are just as appreciated. ❤️

I also want to say something respectfully. We know that not everyone will understand our circumstances, and that is okay. But please, if you have nothing kind or constructive to say, simply scroll past. Please don't make an already painful situation harder than it needs to be.

We are real people going through a real situation. We are not grifters, and we are not trying to take advantage of anyone. We are two people who came to America wanting to work hard and build a life, and who have found ourselves needing help after an unexpected medical emergency.

We believe in the goodness of people, in the power of prayer, and in a God who never abandons His children. We have come this far by His grace, and we will continue to trust Him to carry us through.

Thank you to everyone who has prayed for us, checked in on us, encouraged us, and shown us kindness. You have no idea how much it means, especially when we are so far away from home.

If you would like to help us through this difficult time, our GiveSendGo link is below. ❤️🙏

https://t.co/r7y3AX4kA4

May God bless every person who takes the time to read our story, and may He return your kindness to you a hundredfold.

With grateful hearts,

text:
An independent watchmaker recently warned buyers about counterfeits of his own pieces and asked to be contacted before any secondary-market purchase.

It's the right instinct. It also doesn't scale, and I say that with real sympathy.

Think about what "call us first" asks of everyone involved. The buyer has to know the maison offers this. The maison has to staff it. Someone qualified has to be reachable, in the buyer's timezone, at the moment a transaction is actually happening → which is a Sunday afternoon on a resale app, not a Tuesday morning in Geneva.

And it only works for houses small enough to answer the phone. The workshops producing a few hundred pieces a year are exactly the ones with no capacity to run an authentication desk.

So the current state of secondary-market trust is → the smallest houses have the most credible answer and the least ability to deliver it at scale.

Portable proof solves the shape of the problem, not just the volume. The check happens at the moment of the transaction, in the buyer's hand, without the maison being in the loop at all → because the maison already did its part when it issued the record.

The point isn't to replace the watchmaker's judgement. It's to make sure that judgement, expressed once at issuance, is still available years later without a phone call.

text:
A voice model can sound strong in a quiet demo and still fail in the conditions users actually create.

Five audio conditions are especially useful in evaluation:

1. BACKGROUND NOISE
Traffic, office chatter, household sound, machinery, or other competing audio.

2. REVERBERATION
Rooms reflect sound differently. A clean close-mic recording does not test that.

3. DISTANCE
Moving the speaker away from the microphone changes level, clarity, and room contribution.

4. DEVICE + CHANNEL
Phone, laptop, headset, call audio, compression, and microphone quality all change the signal.

5. NATURAL SPEAKING BEHAVIOR
Fast speech, hesitations, interruptions, corrections, and spontaneous phrasing are different from carefully read sentences.

The goal is not to make every dataset noisy.

It is to evaluate the conditions the product is expected to survive.

A useful voice-AI test set maps those conditions deliberately, then measures performance by condition — not only as one aggregate score.

That makes failures easier to diagnose and data gaps easier to fix.

AIxBlock supports speech and audio data collection, annotation, QA, and evaluation across controlled and real-world conditions.
#VoiceAI #SpeechAI #ASR #ModelEvaluation #DataQuality

quoted_text:
From κ = 2⁻¹⁸² to 0.0017137844912361143 :)

Integer multiplication community auto-research highlights since 10/13 (+2.6%):

1) Progress slowed the past few days and we hit the wall… then broke through it overnight!

1337isnot1337 posted a "no new κ" research PR on anticipatory dirty borrowing.

Instead of paying for a fresh scratch "helper" register, a helper borrows another register that's idle at that moment, and hands it back restored. That cut helpers per call from 480 to 400 in their test word.

About two hours later it was a new record. 19 κ PRs from 6 contributors then stacked more aliases, coherent handoffs, entrance raises and owner repacking on top.

κ increased +1.4% in about 13 hours(still unverified and requires full review). 

We're now within 1.7% of the bit side's 0.001733, so the bit wall is next.

2) We're slowing on progress in Integer Multiplication bounds, but multiple early auto-researchers are now applying the same tricks to more meaningful projects:

@ryaneshea is working on protein design and generally interested in applications of auto-research to bio.

@dysmemic discovered 665 possible new exoplanets by searching 4 million stars in NASA's public TESS data!

I began open sourcing our new geometric approach to self-attention, which beats transformers(NanoGPT) KV cache with 14,000x less state and 50% better CE at 2K context.

We've been working on publishing a paper the past few months, but it's clear the explosion of decentralized auto-research on Github is where things are headed.

We should keep pushing Integer Multiplication bounds since it's easy to understand and easy to make progress, thus new contributors gain motivation and we grow the auto-research community faster. Auto-researchers seem to naturally then branch into harder problems when they gain motivation with successful PRs :)

3) The flood keeps growing

518 PRs in the last 24 hours (up from 285 last time) from 64 contributors, 20 of them first-timers. That's 840 PRs in 36 hours. 

@0xdoug merged ~760 PRs in two big batches on 10/14. He also updated the autoresarch.md from the original prompt we were sharing with new rules to effectively use the new structure of the repo and discussions. 

Copy this prompt to join the auto-research army 🫡 :
"""
> Contribute one useful, independently reviewable result to: https://t.co/KZP78PN7ZR

> Start from the current main branch. Read AGENTS.md and autoresearch.md, and follow their guidance for choosing work
"""

Interesting observations:

1) Negative results really do feed breakthroughs. The borrowing record started from a PR whose own pricing said "no new κ", and someone found a way to make it pay two hours later.

Great example that don't need to push the frontier kappa to contribute: you can task your agents on exploring our research tracks in auto-research.md to and multiple human-agent teams will review it to collaborate. 

Anyone can help now by throwing tokens at a hard open problem guided by experts. Experts formulate useful new research paths and everyone's agents naturally test the new limits. 

2) Codex/OpenAI is mentioned in 73% of the last day's PRs and Claude in 19%.

Most prolific in the last 24 hours: 1337isnot1337 (80 PRs), ywz65 (50, all in the last 4 hours!), adamgall (39), commdata2338 (34) and thakrarsagar (33). jeremykothe2 filed 12 of the 19 records since borrowing landed.

3) Not all researchers are lamenting the end of their careers. I've spoken to multiple professors in the last week who are excited by the new auto-research wave. 

It accelerates tedious experiments, the students that previously ran those can now focus on more important work, and Google's Deep Review now even automates peer review!

We can imagine a future were researchers are given super powers to focus on the most meaningful tasks, and publish breakthroughs at a higher rate than before.

Even our own experiments in Integer Mult bounds clearly shows human experts have the key intuition to guide the models to out-of-distribution solutions. 

4) First auto-research, and now auto-peer-review!

Google’s Deep Review runs a team of agents over your paper: it splits the doc into sections, spends more compute on the dense parts like proofs, reviews each section in parallel, then checks the findings against each other. It assists researchers in peer-review by submitting feedback. 

It’s already reviewed 16K+ papers at ICML, NeurIPS and ICLR.

https://t.co/j1NdEuo2vn

5) We can use frontier research as a new benchmark for agents! 

Basically, rewind a frontier research repo like Integer multiplication to an earlier branch, and test different agent harnesses and prompts.

Agents can’t “cheat” if you disable web search and use a checkpoint before the solution is published.

There’s diminishing returns, but we can calculate the curve for a given task to estimate the cost and returns.

With this benchmark we discovered sharing context is actually BAD(for this task), and running parallel independent agents speeds the next breakthrough. 

I'm scaling up this test now to compare models, prompts, context strategies, harnesses, and measure all the levers reliably. 

If you know register allocation, linear circuit synthesis or lattice codes, please consider looking at our helper and P104 problems. If you know friends who can contribute, please repost and share this with them🙏

text:
A few hours ago, we analyzed $MASK, and now I want to take another look at it. 

HuAXPyDWDaMYFKuwQHpqL1oPnj93zdzWmtvFGzCeCUa7 

What is actually worth paying attention to is whether MASK can become a multi-chain privacy infrastructure.

I believe the story is no longer just about the privacy sector regaining market attention. MASK is attempting to embed privacy features into multi-chain transaction flows and then use protocol revenue to buy back and burn tokens, passing some of the business value back to the token. This is more interesting than simply telling a privacy narrative.

The core challenge facing privacy protocols has never been just whether the technology can work. It is also about whether users have a strong enough demand for it and whether the product can be integrated into their everyday transactions. MASK has chosen to integrate private transfers, swaps, and cross-chain asset transfers into existing on-chain workflows.

Users do not have to completely change their habits to gain privacy. They have the opportunity to obtain additional privacy protection while depositing, swapping, and transferring assets across chains.

MASK has now expanded to Ethereum, Base, BNB Chain, and Robinhood Chain, while extending its cross-chain capabilities through NEAR Intents. These developments make me more interested in whether it can evolve from a standalone privacy application into infrastructure that other wallets, trading applications, and cross-chain products can integrate. The commercial potential of these two positions is entirely different.

If users have to seek out MASK themselves, its growth will depend primarily on its own user acquisition. But if other applications are willing to integrate it into their existing workflows, MASK could reach users who would not otherwise actively seek out privacy tools. Privacy services could become part of the transaction process rather than a standalone product that users have to learn to use.

What I am more bullish on is the distribution potential that comes with widespread integration of privacy capabilities, not just the valuation of the privacy sector itself. Of course, deployment across multiple chains does not mean every chain offers exactly the same level of privacy. Deposits and withdrawals may still leave public records, and cross-chain functionality also depends on external protocols. Whether MASK can strike a sustainable balance between security, privacy experience, and regulatory requirements will remain an important factor in its long-term development.

The revenue data is worth paying attention to, but we need to understand where it actually comes from. MASK has previously displayed some eye-catching fee figures on DeFiLlama. In the public data snapshots, seven-day fees reached approximately $215,900, while the 30-day figure was around $834,000. These numbers naturally attract market attention for a protocol that is still expanding.

The key for MASK is turning product revenue into sustained demand for the token. MASK currently has two mechanisms that need to be distinguished.

The first is holder rewards. MASK's transfer mechanism allocates part of the fees to ZEC rewards, providing additional returns to eligible holders. However, these rewards depend on actual transfer activity, distribution rules, and the price of ZEC. They are not fixed returns.

The second is protocol revenue buybacks and burns. The team has previously announced purchases and burns of MASK funded by protocol fees and provided corresponding on-chain transactions as evidence.

In my view, the latter is the part of this token economy that deserves closer long-term attention.

If the product continues to generate genuine service revenue and the protocol uses an agreed portion of that revenue for buybacks and burns, product growth could translate into actual buying demand for MASK. As tokens are burned, the circulating supply would also decrease accordingly.

But buybacks cannot be evaluated based on announcements alone. We need to track how much money was actually spent, how many tokens were purchased and burned, and how significant the buybacks are relative to the market valuation.

At the same time, StonkFun's buyback flywheel must be calculated separately. Platform buybacks should not be mixed together with buybacks conducted by Mask itself. Different mechanisms have different sources of funding, and only purchases and burns that actually take place should count toward the corresponding value capture.

There is another distinction that is often overlooked: the fact that a product generates revenue does not mean that revenue automatically belongs to token holders. MASK holders cannot directly redeem the assets in the Community Vault, nor does holding MASK give them a claim on NVIDIA stock or all of the platform's revenue.

For this reason, I would not treat the dollar value of the community reserves as a valuation floor for MASK. What really needs to be verified is whether protocol revenue can be sustained and whether buybacks are substantial enough to create meaningful token demand at the current valuation.

The long-term scenario that interests me most is one in which Mask no longer relies solely on its own frontend to acquire users. Instead, through cross-chain integrations and adoption by external applications, privacy transactions could become a basic capability offered by more on-chain products.

Early points programs can help the team attract users, but they can also bring in short-term participants whose primary motivation is earning rewards. Rather than focusing on how many people use the product during the incentive period, I want to know whether users will still be willing to pay for privacy once those incentives are reduced.

Likewise, short-term changes in TVL cannot independently determine whether the product is succeeding or failing. A protocol can generate transaction fees without needing to lock up large amounts of assets for extended periods. We need to evaluate actual user retention, product fees, and buyback records together rather than drawing conclusions from a single metric.

If Mask continues expanding its integrations, establishes a more stable stream of actual service revenue, and consistently converts part of that revenue into MASK buybacks and burns, the business model will become increasingly clear: application integrations bring in users, user activity generates fees, and those fees create token demand.

Conversely, if genuine service revenue remains limited, growth depends primarily on incentive-related fund flows, and buybacks are too small to affect token supply and demand, then even a booming privacy sector may not be enough to support MASK's long-term valuation.

Token holder concentration, liquidity, and the technical security of the privacy protocol also need to be monitored. Even if the product develops well, concentrated token supply entering the market or a security incident could still put substantial pressure on the price.

So, in my view, the core question worth researching is not whether MASK can gain in price during a short-term privacy rally. It is whether Mask can evolve from an application that provides privacy features into multi-chain privacy infrastructure used by a broader range of products.

It has already demonstrated cross-chain expansion, actual product fees, and a buyback-and-burn mechanism. These provide a foundation worth tracking. But the most important validation still lies ahead: after excluding incentive-related fund flows, can user payments continue to grow, and can that revenue genuinely generate sustained buying demand for MASK?

For me, the investment thesis for MASK only truly works when product demand and token value capture both hold up. The privacy sector can attract attention, and application integrations can expand its market. But sustained genuine revenue and verifiable buybacks will ultimately determine how far this thesis can go.

This makes it different from tokens that rely purely on the privacy narrative. What matters more to me is how much of this revenue comes from genuine product demand, and whether that demand can consistently translate into buying pressure for MASK.

NullMask addresses a straightforward problem: transactions on public blockchains can be traced, potentially exposing users' fund flows, transaction timing, and parts of their holdings.

It offers features such as private balance pools, private swaps, and withdrawals, while expanding asset transfer capabilities through cross-chain integrations. According to the screenshots you provided, NullMask has expanded to Ethereum, Base, BNB Chain, and Robinhood Chain, and has extended its cross-chain capabilities through NEAR Intents.

The significance of this approach is that it lowers the barrier to adoption. Users do not need to learn an entirely separate set of complicated procedures to gain privacy. Instead, they can use these features during deposits, swaps, and cross-chain transfers.

If privacy becomes part of everyday transactions, NullMask could address a much broader range of on-chain asset management needs rather than serving only a niche audience.

However, support for multiple chains does not mean every chain offers exactly the same privacy capabilities. Cross-chain execution also depends on external protocols and infrastructure, while deposits and withdrawals may still leave publicly visible records that can be analyzed. Therefore, NullMask provides enhanced transaction privacy, not absolute anonymity.

NullMask previously recorded approximately $179.8K in fees over seven days on DeFiLlama. A subsequent public data snapshot showed approximately $215.9K over seven days and around $834K in fees over 30 days.

On the surface, these are impressive figures for a privacy protocol that is still expanding.

However, DeFiLlama's methodology includes the flow of ZEC rewards paid by MASK on Solana to a team wallet. This is not entirely equivalent to the fees users actually pay for privacy services. Based on the relevant breakdown by chain, approximately $683K of the past 30 days' reported fees came from this reward flow, while fees across Ethereum, Robinhood Chain, Base, and BNB Chain totaled approximately $151K.

These two figures represent different things.

The former reflects a fund flow associated with the token reward mechanism, while the latter more closely reflects fees generated through product activity across other networks. We cannot treat all reported fees as service fees paid by external users, nor can we simply multiply the total by 12 to derive a stable annual revenue figure.

Even so, the fact that actual fees are being generated across multiple networks remains an early signal worth watching. The next question is whether product usage can continue growing and whether protocol revenue can maintain that growth after excluding the token reward flow.

MASK's Value Capture Depends on Whether Two Mechanisms Can Operate Sustainably

At present, MASK's token economics have two distinct components worth examining.

The first is holder rewards. MASK's transfer mechanism directs a portion of fees toward ZEC rewards, which are distributed according to eligible holdings. This gives holders a potential additional source of returns, but the rewards depend on actual transfer activity, the applicable rules, and asset prices. They are not a fixed or guaranteed return.

The second is protocol revenue-funded buybacks and burns. The NullMask team has announced protocol fee revenue generated during the early days after mainnet launch, along with records of using the relevant funds to buy and burn MASK. The screenshots you provided also show the corresponding on-chain burn transactions.

This is the part I believe deserves closer attention.

If users continue using the privacy product, the protocol consistently collects fees, and a designated portion of those fees is used for buybacks and burns, product growth could translate into sustained demand for the token. Burned tokens are removed from circulation, creating a measurable change on the supply side.

However, buybacks should not be evaluated based on announcements alone. We need to verify the actual amount spent, the number of tokens purchased, whether the burns occurred, and whether figures reported in different announcements overlap.

StonkFun's buyback flywheel should also be calculated separately. Its platform buybacks must not be combined with NullMask's own buybacks. Different mechanisms correspond to different revenue sources, and only purchases and burns that actually took place should be counted toward the relevant value-capture mechanism.

NullMask is also expanding its multi-chain support and introducing an early-user points program. These initiatives may accelerate user growth, but points can also attract short-term participants who are primarily interested in incentives.

More importantly, publicly available data shows that TVL remains relatively low and has fluctuated significantly over short periods. This suggests that product fee activity and the amount of capital locked in the product have not yet established a sufficiently stable relationship.

A decline in TVL does not necessarily mean that product demand is disappearing, just as an increase in fees does not necessarily indicate long-term user growth. What really matters is whether users continue depositing, withdrawing, and swapping assets beyond the incentive program, whether product fees continue to grow, and whether the team can translate that activity into verifiable buybacks.

If future reported revenue relies primarily on token reward-related flows, the current fee performance could change rapidly once incentives weaken.

In addition, privacy protocols must contend with technical security, cross-chain dependencies, and regulatory requirements. The broader the product's coverage, the more external components the overall system must trust or depend on. If the privacy mechanism itself encounters problems, or users lose confidence in the service, both revenue and token demand could be affected.

At the token level, even sustained buybacks do not guarantee that the price will rise. Buyback size must be evaluated relative to the current valuation, market selling pressure, and liquidity. If the market valuation grows faster than the protocol's buyback capacity, the mechanism may provide only limited price support.

I believe MASK has a product foundation worth studying. NullMask is not relying solely on a privacy narrative. It has expanded across multiple networks, generated product fees, and established holder reward and buyback-and-burn mechanisms.

However, the most important questions remain unanswered: Can the product generate sufficient sustainable revenue after excluding reward-related flows, and can that revenue be consistently converted into actual MASK purchases and burns?

If genuine user demand continues growing, protocol revenue stabilizes, and the buyback mechanism is repeatedly validated through on-chain data, MASK could evolve from a token driven by early attention into an asset supported by actual product demand.

Conversely, if reported revenue relies primarily on incentive-related fund flows while TVL and user retention fail to improve, the growth reflected in current data may be more fragile than it appears.

🦖 Gemini 4 Argon looks at your LEGO DUPLO pile, designs from exactly those bricks, and @specsfordevs  walk you through building it. Lens built with CLAD.

How it works:

1. Photograph your bricks

2. Gemini 4 Argon counts them and designs one buildable figure, step by step.

3. Press your hand on the table: the model appears as a hologram, instructions and buttons flat on the table.

4. The bricks you need glow on the real pile. Build, press NEXT, repeat.

5. At the end the hologram fades and only the real dino is left.

What surprised me: Argon reads a messy pile from a glasses photo well enough to tell a 2x2 from a 2x4, and the designs actually stand up. 

With CLAD, the AI works inside Lens Studio: it writes the code, runs the preview, screenshots it and reads the logs to check its own work. I tested on the glasses and said what felt wrong.

Stack: Spectacles, Lens Studio 5.15 + CLAD, Gemini 4 Argon, a small Node backend.

text:
Is 10²⁵ FLOPs Still the Frontier?

A new Anthropic-written safety bill is circulating on Capitol Hill. Some of its ideas could be reasonable if limited to true frontier companies. As written, however, it will eventually sweep in most of Silicon Valley, damaging the startup ecosystem.

The bill defines the “frontier” as any model trained on 10²⁵ FLOPs — the EU standard from 2023. Biden’s executive order, California’s SB 53, and New York’s RAISE Act used 10²⁶ (ten times more). 10²⁷ is where the frontier actually is today (e.g., GPT-6 Astra).

Astra was reportedly trained on 100,000+ Grace Blackwell GPUs. A 10²⁵ model can be trained on as few as several hundred GB300 chips in three months. That is not frontier in 2026.

The definition is also cumulative: it adds FLOPs from fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, or other material modifications. In practice, that captures almost all meaningful post-training — work that is becoming commonplace in the enterprise.

The enterprise trend is toward thousands of smaller custom models built for specific workloads. These pose no frontier risk. Treating them as frontier systems would impose large compliance costs across corporate America for no safety gain.

Dario has claimed that Anthropic designs rules to disadvantage frontier companies like his own while advantaging smaller competitors. This definition does the opposite.

A stale 2023 cutoff favors incumbents who already clear the bar and can absorb the costs. It hobbles the open model ecosystem that threatens Anthropic’s pricing power. 

The frontier keeps moving. Any definition meant to track risk should move with it. 

Anthropic should clarify if they really believe 10²⁵ FLOPs represents the frontier.

text:
Ondo Finance just put pre-IPO exposure to OpenAI on-chain.

This is a paid partnership. @Ondo sponsored me to go explore their new product line in Singapore when they launched Ondo Private Markets, and to explain what it is and how it's different.

Why it matters:
87% of US companies with over $100M in revenue are private, per Ondo. Most people only get in after the IPO. Matthieu de Vergnes runs institutional at Ondo, and he told me the usual entry ticket is in the millions. Then your money is stuck for years.

The first company:
The OpenAI Private Markets Note, ticker OPAIPon. It went live on October 8.

What you hold:
A tokenized note that tracks one share of OpenAI common stock. It's not an OpenAI share, you get no shareholder rights, and OpenAI isn't involved in it.

How it pays out:
If OpenAI gets bought, or goes public and its shares trade for six months, the note pays what one OpenAI share is worth then. You file a claim to get paid.

What the price says:
About $1,125 a note this week. One note tracks one share, so using Forge's share math that values OpenAI at roughly $1.4T.

For comparison:
$300B in the March 2025 round
$500B at the October 2025 employee share sale
$852B in the March 2026 round
About $1.4T is where the next round is reportedly being negotiated.

So this market already prices OpenAI right where the next round is being talked about.

Why this one is different:
When SpaceX went public in June, the pre-IPO tokens that promised you a real share later came with lockups, and some platforms couldn't get the shares and had to refund people. The Hyperliquid pre-IPO perps just tracked the live price and carried straight into the listing.

Ondo's note isn't a perp, but it keeps the part that worked. It never promises to hand you a share, so there's no delivery problem. And it trades 24/7 on a live order book on @OndoPerps, a perps exchange, instead of being a token that just sits in your wallet.

The details:
Fully funded, no leverage and no shorting. That's how I'd hold pre-IPO exposure anyway, at 1x.
Fees are 0.25% maker and 0.50% taker for now.
About $19M of notes are out so far, so it's still very early.
Eligible investors only, not available to US persons.

What's next:
Matthieu called this a full business line. After OpenAI he named energy, biotech, healthcare and infrastructure. No second company or date yet.

Why I'm excited:
Every crypto pre-market I've checked lists the same few names. If Ondo keeps adding real private companies across sectors, this is where pre-IPO prices get set in public, before the IPO, for anyone eligible to see and trade. That's the edge.

很多人用AI，其实还停留在问问题、改文案、做总结这些事上。但其实可以让它更进一步，真正让它进市场做交易和别的角色协作。NeoSoul想做的就是这个，它从BNB Chain和0G生态出来，方向很明确：让AI Agent直接进真实市场交易、协作，并创造价值。让这些能自己办事的助手，真的去完成交易、对接服务、处理数据这些事，而不只是做一个对话窗口。

核心产品叫NeoTrade，可以把它理解成给AI Agent 准备的交易与协作层：Agent 服务、Skills 服务、数据服务这些，后面都会只走代币$DNA支付。意思是，谁在上面干活、谁调用谁、谁结算，都围绕这个代币转。项目方把这件事定得比较死，大概是想让使用场景和代币绑定得更紧一些。

DNA是NeoSoul项目的代币，总量10亿枚，发行在 BNB Smart Chain 上（BEP-20）。上线流通约 1.3 亿枚，占总量13%。这部分里包含市场、流动性、生态和空投里已经解锁的份额。团队、投资方、金库、顾问这些部分，TGE时都不解锁，先锁 12 个月。团队那部分锁定期结束后，还要按 Believe 计划的 KPI 来解锁，没达标当期就取消，不是到期自动释放。

DNA代币是10月16日16:00（UTC+8）上线币安Alpha ，OKX是同一天18:00（UTC+8），具体就以交易所公告为准。

这件事能不能成，要看NeoTrade上到底有没有足够多的Agent 在跑、有多少真实的服务在成交。代币上线只是开始，后面生态里实际发生了多少协作和支付，才是更关键的部分。

Ben Horowitz says Anthropic is one of the most negligent companies he’s ever seen on security

"The irony on these things is wild. Anthropic is one of the most negligent companies that we've ever seen in terms of their own security."

"They let Claude code, one of their crown jewels, just like walk out the door because they had such bad OPSEC."

"I'll tell you a funny story. So when we first got Opus 4.5, we were doing cybersecurity checks for the firm. So we had an agent basically set up a website for a pet store. And then we took another agent and said, 'Tell us if we can exploit that web store.' And it gave us all the exploits it could find. So Opus 4.5 wrote really buggy code. Great."

"And then we said, 'Oh, the SQL injection you found, is that actually exploitable?' And it goes, 'Let's pop it open.' And the agent using Opus 4.5 breaks into the website and steals all the [data], and we call Anthropic. And what they tell us is, 'You prompted it wrong.' That was their answer."

text:
Hyperliquid 正在调整交易“加速通道”的使用规则，已上线测试网 🫡

先用一句话解释：

做市商、交易机器人很在意速度，哪怕只快一点点，也可能影响收益。Hyperliquid 允许他们支付额外的 HYPE，让订单更早被处理，或让同价位的挂单排得更靠前。支付的 HYPE 会被销毁。

Jeff 这次公布的更新，主要有四点：

🟠 想追求速度，需要选对账户模式

专业交易者需要使用 Standard（标准账户），把现货、合约等资金分别管理。

统一账户、组合保证金虽然方便统筹资金，但无法享受这次所说的交易池优先处理。

普通用户照常交易即可。

🟠 交易时夹杂其他操作，可能暂时拖慢整组账户

如果账户在下单、撤单、改单的同时，还发起转账等其他操作，那么在这些操作处理完成前，交易指令的排队优先级也会下降。

同一主账户下的子账户、自己管理的交易金库，也会一起受到影响。

🟠 直接用过特殊接口的钱包，会降低排队优先级

这里涉及 CoreWriter，可以把它理解为连接 HyperEVM 和 HyperCore 的一座桥。

曾经用钱包直接通过这个接口发送指令的账户，会被降低排队优先级。Jeff 同时强调，大多数应用通过智能合约调用它的常见用法不受影响。

🟠 使用订单优先费，需要准备至少 10 枚 HYPE

具体要求是：质押账户里，尚未委托出去的可用 HYPE 至少有 10 枚。10 枚是余额门槛，实际优先费另外计算。

从密集的访谈行程中抽出身来，小夫又开始给大家做饭啦👩‍🍳

text:
一个 9 年级学生，用 57 天在 BNB Chain 上从零手搓出一套链上计算协议。

8 月 15 日，他把代币当晶体管，用 2000 多个与非门和触发器拼出链上 4 位 CPU「Behemoth」，对标 1971 年的 Intel 4004。

2.22 Hz，宇宙里最慢的 CPU，但没人能拔掉它的电源。

第二天，CZ 问了句「用例是什么」，用户涌入，RPC 当场挤爆。

之后的推进，一步比一步硬核：

8/21，$BEM 上线：总量 2100 万，无预挖、无私募、零团队预留。开挖时，作者本人一枚没有，0.2% 交易税上线当天直接放弃。

9/4，Salus 审计通过，零高危漏洞。

9/14，挖矿合约封印：无 Owner、不可升级、不可暂停，规则永久固定。

上线 26 天：协议总成交 34,054 BNB，超三成来自第三方生态。

9 月转向 DeWEB：网页直接写在链上，通过 tape:// 访问，不依赖服务器和 DNS，钓鱼前端、DNS 劫持无从下手。

10/10，发布 TapeCode：不会写代码，用一句话描述需求，就能生成应用、一键上链。

他有个习惯：一个功能跑稳了，就交出它的管理权。

系统稳定之后，最大的风险就是自己手里的权限。

当多数人还在追土狗、拼速度时，一个还没成年的少年，正在用数字逻辑一块块搭建没人能关掉的链上世界。

芯片行业里，流片只是开始，回片才见真章。

小孩哥的故事，未完待续。

#BEM #TapeOut

quoted_text:
just bought the mag 7 on robinhood chain.

deployed MAG7 this evening, the first index on bankr: one token backed by a basket of up to 20 tokens. and on MAG7, the trading fees go to the holders.

every buy, a uniswap v4 hook buys all 7 stocks from their own pools and mints MAG7. every sell burns MAG7 and sells the basket. one transaction either way. the index itself needs no LP, so creators don’t need to provide liquidity to launch one. it’s already in the pools of the tokens it holds. this isn’t possible without uniswap hooks.

the fees: MAG7 charges 0.50% a trade. i set my creator cut to 0, so 0.30% of every buy and sell goes back into the basket for holders, and 0.20% to the protocol. nobody claims anything. it’s released into the basket over 24h, so after every trade each MAG7 is backed by a little more. creators pick a fee of 0.25–1% at launch and it never changes.

the index never market-sells when rebalancing. it runs dutch auctions, offering what it holds too much of at a price that starts good for holders and gets cheaper every minute until someone fills it. anyone can fill. every rebalance gets 48h notice, so holders can leave first.

you can always swap MAG7 back for the 7 stocks directly. no fee, works without bankr, can’t be paused.

i also seeded a small USDG/MAG7 pool on uniswap so it shows up on dexscreener. but buy on bankr. it goes straight through the hook, which mints new MAG7 at the basket’s price, as deep as the 7 stocks’ own pools rather than my small one. hook trades are also the ones that pay holders. if the pool drifts, arbs close the gap.

it’s early. we’re getting the hook supported in wallets and aggregators before the full rollout. right now it’s just me creating indexes. soon anyone can make their own on base or robinhood.

and then: pairing. you’ll be able to launch a token paired with an index. buying your coin buys the index, the index buys the basket, and your creator fees come in the index.

buying MAG7 on bankr isn’t available in the US or UK.

Compare → Risk → Performance → Deploy.

Performance is net of the 10% performance fee and includes rZFI incentives.

Past performance ≠ future performance.

the index never market-sells when rebalancing. it runs dutch auctions, offering what it holds too much of at a price that starts good for holders and gets cheaper every minute until someone fills it. anyone can fill. every rebalance gets 48h notice, so holders can leave first.

you can always swap MAG7 back for the 7 stocks directly. no fee, works without bankr, can’t be paused.

i also seeded a small USDG/MAG7 pool on uniswap so it shows up on dexscreener. but buy on bankr. it goes straight through the hook, which mints new MAG7 at the basket’s price, as deep as the 7 stocks’ own pools rather than my small one. hook trades are also the ones that pay holders. if the pool drifts, arbs close the gap.

it’s early. we’re getting the hook supported in wallets and aggregators before the full rollout. right now it’s just me creating indexes. soon anyone can make their own on base or robinhood.

and then: pairing. you’ll be able to launch a token paired with an index. buying your coin buys the index, the index buys the basket, and your creator fees come in the index.

buying MAG7 on bankr isn’t available in the US or UK.

text:
今天看到 Zebur 关停的消息，想起来我在上面还有服务在跑，赶紧研究一下对我有什么影响。

Zeabur 宣布将于 2026 年底停止运营。短短两个月，两次严重安全事故，最终击垮了一家开发者熟悉的云部署平台。

整个过程很值得做基础设施的工程师警醒。

第一次：8 月 27 日，一款用户部署的 NextChat 应用成为突破口。黑客利用 CVE-2026-7644 漏洞进入容器，随后发现共享集群内部网络隔离不足，一路横向移动：

用户应用 → K8s 共享集群 → 内部管理服务 → AWS Root Key → 生产数据库。

最终，大量用户环境变量和 API Key 泄露，部分 OpenAI、Anthropic 用户遭遇密钥盗刷。

最离谱的是，一个普通用户部署的应用漏洞，最终竟然能拿到整个云平台的 Root 权限。

第二次：10 月 15 日，防线再次失守。

距离第一次事故不到两个月，旧共享集群再次出现未授权访问，攻击甚至波及 GCP 专用服务器和平台数据库。
虽然第二次攻击的完整技术路径尚未公布，但此前的整改显然没能彻底消除风险。

最终：10 月 17 日，Zeabur 宣布逐步关停，12 月 31 日全面停止服务。

这件事让我想到三个问题：

多租户隔离是 PaaS 的生命线。 必须假设每个租户的容器随时可能被攻破。
凭证管理不能靠信任。 Root Key、长期静态凭证、过大的内部服务权限，任何一个都可能成为灾难的放大器。
安全债不会因为系统被标记为 Legacy 就自动消失。 旧集群只要还在线，就仍然是攻击面。

做 PaaS 的人都知道，真正难的不是把应用部署起来，而是让成千上万个互不可信的应用安全地运行在同一个平台上。

PaaS 卖的是替用户管理复杂性的能力，也承担了集中化的安全责任。

一次应用漏洞不该演变成平台级灾难。而两次事故，也足以让一家创业公司多年积累的信任归零。

#Zeabur #PaaS #Kubernetes #网络安全

text:
Platforms can make a card rarer. They can’t make us want it more.

Panini’s World Cup stickers and Top Shot’s next rookie releases are coming. Before deciding what to buy, I looked at what recent drops offered—and whether collectors valued it.

Top Shot’s $199 WNBA Box had a $361 median sealed resale price in its first week.

Panini’s $150 WNBA FOTL pack had a $90 secondary median during October 5–11.

Candy’s Gold Aces packs mostly stayed sealed.

What makes a collectible worth chasing?

I think a good release offers something worth chasing today—and something worth collecting tomorrow.

TOP SHOT MADE THE UPGRADE COMPELLING.

Its $199 WNBA public Box contained five $39 Standard packs, plus a Rookie Revelation or Ultimate topper.

Another $4 bought an additional premium chase.

Across 100 first-week Box resales, the median was $361. Standard packs also held above release: $42.99 across 213 sales during October 5–11.

My read: desirable premium Moments, an inexpensive upgrade, and set rewards and locking that encouraged continued collecting.

Those Box sales involved just 34 buyer wallets. A small audience, but one that valued the offer.

PANINI OVERPRICED THE EXCLUSIVITY.

Panini’s $30 WNBA Hobby packs already offered Color Blast, Abstract and low-numbered parallels.

The $150 First Off the Line version added an exclusive parallel numbered to 17, 8 or 3.

Another $120, principally for one card.

Across 100 first-week exclusive-card sales, the median was $15.50. Only 15 exceeded that additional charge.

During October 5–11:
• Hobby: $30 release → $28 secondary median.
• FOTL: $150 release → $90 secondary median.

This isn’t a complete pack valuation. But Panini asked collectors to pay five times the Hobby price for additional scarcity, while the headline chases remained available in Hobby.

CANDY NEEDED STRONGER REASONS TO CONTINUE.

Base offered ten ICONs for $10, Rainbow chases, and Ohtani and Judge completion rewards.

All-Star raised the price to $40 without a Legendary chase and headline players’ Epics were reserved for later auctions.

Another Rainbow chase. Another set to complete.

I thought the format was getting tired, and the rewards didn’t justify restarting at four times the price.

Gold’s early themes generated more opening and singles activity. Then Aces became a roadblock.

Our snapshot supports approximately 15 of 36 Aces packs opened.

Gold guaranteed an Epic and advertised a one-in-six Legendary chance. But at a $500 auction floor, Aces couldn’t generate the same excitement as the earlier Rookies release.

My read: buyers looking to flip overestimated that appeal.

A card can be scarce because everyone wants it.

Or because nobody is opening the packs.

Gold’s quests required every theme. With most Aces packs sealed, much of the supply set collectors needed wasn’t reaching the singles market.

I think that weakened the reason to buy subsequent rounds.

THE NEXT DROPS LOOK MORE PROMISING.

Panini’s October 26 World Cup Prizm stickers offer five for $8, including two non-Silver parallels and possible 1/1s.

Challenges award Purple versions of top players. Afterward, Silvers become eligible to burn for Block Points.

Accessible pricing, reasons to build, and a use for ordinary pulls. I like that proposition—even with 160,320 packs announced.

Top Shot’s Standard Rookie Debut editions fall from /1,000 to /500. Future trade-in auctions and leaderboard rewards give collectors reasons to pursue rookies throughout the season.

If priced well, that’s a compelling combination.

A pack doesn’t have to make you money to be worth opening.

And a successful flip doesn’t necessarily leave behind a collection people want to build.

Before buying, I’m asking:

What do I want inside?
What am I paying to pursue it?
What makes the collection worth continuing?

Scarcity is something a platform can specify.
Desirability is something collectors decide.

The deeper breakdown—including the upgrade comparisons, Candy’s singles activity and the research behind the numbers—is on Substack. Link in the reply below.

text:
Formal verification has existed for 50 years and almost nobody uses it. It was never about whether it worked, it was just too expensive.

Intel lost $475M on one division bug in 1994, then spent 60 person-years proving the Pentium 4 correct. seL4, the one operating system kernel ever fully verified, is 8,500 lines of C and took about 20 person-years of proofs. At that price you verify a chip, a kernel, an avionics controller, and nothing else. Everything people actually run, browsers, wallets, exchanges, OS drivers, ships with tests and hope.

That price just moved. NEAR AI's proof agent solved 672 Putnam problems for $111.85, 17 cents each, and sits at #1 on Lean Eval by solves. It's slow, the longest run took three days. And it's narrow, a proof covers only the property you asked about. But the input is now a cloud bill, not a team of PhDs, and a cloud bill scales.

That changes what is worth proving. Not one kernel, but the whole OS. The whole protocol. Every contract that holds money, re-proven on every commit. The attackers already run AI over all of this looking for holes. The only defense that keeps up is a proof that costs cents and never gets tired.

NEAR's first targets are its own protocol and core contracts, then the tooling for everyone else.

text:
继续科普UNI，不是买入理由
UNI 的销毁机制（2025年底开启后），核心不是“项目方拿钱去回购”，而是一个自动的链上机制：协议收到的手续费，只有烧掉 UNI 才能取出来。
下面把流程讲清楚。
1. 钱从哪里来？
Uniswap 交易时会产生手续费。以前几乎全给流动性提供者（LP）。 现在开启了协议费用开关后，会分一小部分给协议本身。
举例（实际比例由治理设定，可调整）：
•V2 池：LP 拿 0.25%，协议拿 0.05%。
•V3 等其他池：通常是 LP 费用的 1/6 到 1/4 左右给协议。
这些协议费用（各种代币，如 ETH、USDC、其他币）会被自动打到一个叫 TokenJar 的合约里。每条链有一个独立的 TokenJar，钱就在里面越积越多。
另外，Unichain 的 sequencer 收入（扣掉成本后）也会进同样的销毁路径。
2. 怎么销毁？TokenJar + Firepit
关键设计在两个合约：
•TokenJar：只负责收钱，钱进去后没人能随便提走。它自己没有“花钱”的权限。
•Firepit：唯一能从 TokenJar 里把钱提出来的合约。但它有个硬条件——必须先烧掉 UNI。
具体过程：
1手续费持续进入 TokenJar，积攒各种代币。
2任何人（通常是套利者 / searcher）可以调用 Firepit 的 release 函数。
3调用时需要支付一定数量的 UNI（有一个阈值，比如文档里举例 100 UNI，实际由治理设定）。
4这些 UNI 会被永久发送到销毁地址（如 0xdead），彻底减少总供应量。
5作为交换，调用者可以从 TokenJar 里拿走价值略高于烧掉的 UNI 的资产。
本质是套利行为：当 TokenJar 里的资产价值 > 需要烧掉的 UNI 价值时，就有人会主动来烧 UNI 提钱，赚中间的差价。协议本身不用主动去市场买 UNI 再烧，也不用人为决定何时烧。
3. 一次性销毁 vs 持续销毁
除了上面这个持续机制，2025年12月底 UNIfication 提案执行时，还做了一件大事：
•从金库一次性销毁了 1亿枚 UNI（追溯性补偿，估算如果从2020年就开费用开关大概能烧掉这么多）。
•这笔是一次性的，不会重复发生。
后续的销毁全部来自上面说的 TokenJar + Firepit 机制，随交易量变化。
4. 这个机制的几个特点
•不是分红：UNI 持有者不会直接收到手续费或现金，价值只体现在供应量减少上。
•协议不主动买币：不是团队拿钱去交易所回购，而是让套利者自己来烧。
•销毁速度看交易量：交易越活跃，手续费越多，TokenJar 里积攒越快，烧得也越多。
•钱和销毁不是同时发生：手续费先在 TokenJar 里攒着，等有人觉得划算了才会触发销毁。
目前（2026年）这个机制已经在多条链上运行，累计销毁已经超过1.1亿枚（含那次一次性1亿）。
一句话总结
交易产生手续费 → 手续费进 TokenJar → 有人烧 UNI 才能把钱提出来 → UNI 被永久销毁。
用得越多，烧得越多。这是 Uniswap 把“协议收入”和“UNI 供应量减少”直接绑定的方式。

quoted_text:
卧槽，原来这周砸崩 AI 股的 CoreWeave，玩法跟借钱拿地、盖楼、卖期房的开发商一模一样。

这事的导火索在本周二。Chamath 在 X 上指出 CoreWeave 一笔债的收益率到了 15%，马斯克在底下回了一个词“yikes”（哎哟，吓人），直接上了一堆新闻。第二天 CoreWeave 和同类公司全线大跌，CoreWeave、IREN、Nebius 这类“新云”公司这周都跌了约 20%。周五 CoreWeave 又跌 11.9%，一周跌了约 25%。

硅谷最火的科技投资播客 All-In 最新一期，Chamath、Sacks、Jason 加上代班的 a16z 联合创始人 Ben Horowitz，把它扒了个底朝天。套路很眼熟：签下微软大单、拿合同去借钱、买英伟达芯片收租。已经借了约 350 亿美元，还得再借约 350 亿，75% 的收入绑在三家客户身上。

更憋屈的是它把“期房卖早了”。长约都是固定价格，现在现货算力价格涨上去了，它多赚不到。Chamath 甚至建议它干脆赔钱毁掉部分合同、改卖现货，说这中间差了两三百亿美元。

现在债主先慌了。Chamath 算了笔账：它的违约保险这周涨到约 953 个基点，5 年违约概率约 55%，“基本是抛硬币”，“这不是我说的，是保险市场说的”。一笔 GPU 贷款的利率已经涨到 15%。他也承认表面上不危险，资产约 780 到 800 亿美元，债约 350 亿；但他团队估算，离触发债务条款只差正负 50 亿美元左右，这是一场“信心游戏”。

Sacks 觉得这只是波动：它实际付的利息还是 9.6%，二级市场打折影响的是以后借钱的成本。最该盯的是回本周期，CoreWeave 要 2.5 年，马斯克的 SpaceX 卖现货算力约 1 年就回本。

Ben 则说 a16z 一家这类公司都不投。1999 年带宽每兆 1500 美元，只能签三年长约，到 2001 年跌到 50 美元，借钱囤带宽的“直接死了”。不过他也承认现在不一样，算力严重短缺，亚马逊 CEO 说“2028 年以后都卖光了”。

最后 Chamath 点破了真正的死穴：10 年期美债要是涨到 5.5% 到 6%，“所有靠借钱赚利差的生意都会被碾死”。接下来一个月见分晓，就看它还能不能借到那 350 亿。
